works.title: A History of the Lyre
works.author: Letitia Elizabeth Landon (L.E.L.)
works.blurb: A poem that traces a woman's heart through its joys and griefs, told as the history of her lyre.

works.title: A Last Confession
works.author: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
works.blurb: A dramatic monologue in blank verse: a dying exile tells his confessor of the girl he loved and how that love ended in murder.

works.title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Hermia flees Athens with Lysander rather than wed the man her father has chosen, and Helena, who loves the spurned Demetrius, follows them into a wood ruled by the quarrelling fairy king and queen. There Oberon's errand-boy Puck mistakes his victims, sending the lovers into a night of misplaced desire while Titania wakes to adore Bottom the weaver, now wearing an ass's head. By morning the couples are rightly matched, and the weddings at Theseus's court are crowned by the workmen's clumsy play of Pyramus and Thisbe.

works.title: A Mother's Tale
works.author: Walter Savage Landor
works.blurb: A narrative in blank verse that opens with the speaker's claim that she never knew but one who died for love.

works.title: The Abbot of Muchelnaye
works.author: Henry Alford
works.blurb: A narrative poem in three cantos, in nine-line stanzas, of an abbot of Muchelney in Somerset and the wife he lost and finds again.

works.title: Achilleid
works.author: Statius
works.blurb: Statius’s unfinished epic of Akhilleus’s youth, from Thetis hiding her son among the maidens of Scyros to Akhilleus’s own account of his boyhood training under Chiron.

works.title: Achilles in Scyros
works.subtitle: A drama in a mixed manner
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's drama in a mixed manner, first published in 1890. Thetis has hidden her son Achilles on Scyros, disguised as the girl Pyrrha among the daughters of King Lycomedes; Ulysses and Diomede arrive to find the hero whom the Greeks need at Troy, and Deidamia and a chorus of Scyrian maidens complete the cast.

works.title: Leucippe and Clitophon
works.subtitle: A Greek Romance in Eight Books
works.author: Achilles Tatius
works.blurb: Clitophon of Tyre falls in love with his cousin Leucippe, and the two flee together, only to suffer shipwreck, capture by Egyptian brigands, apparent deaths, abductions and a trial for chastity at Ephesus before they are reunited and married.

works.title: The Adventures of Kurroglou
works.author: Köroğlu
works.blurb: Köroğlu is the bandit-minstrel hero of the Turkic and Persian oral destan, the robber-poet whose adventures with his horse Kyrat and his band at Chamly-bill are told by the aushiks. The cycle mixes prose narrative with his improvised songs, here given in Alexander Chodzko's English version of 1842, collected from Persian reciters in thirteen Meetings.

works.title: Ælla: A Tragycal Enterlude
works.subtitle: or Discoorseynge Tragedie, wrotenn bie Thomas Rowleie
works.author: Thomas Chatterton
works.blurb: Chatterton's most admired Rowley forgery, a tragedy supposedly written by the fifteenth-century priest Thomas Rowley for William Canynge of Bristol. Ælla, lord of Bristol castle, marries Birtha, then is called away to repel a Danish raid. His friend Celmonde, secretly in love with Birtha, abducts her in the woods, and the Danes who capture them lead to a deadly end for all three. The minstrels' songs, including 'O! synge untoe mie roundelaie', sit within the play.

works.subtitle: Prose translation
works.author: Virgil
works.blurb: Virgil's Latin epic of Aeneas, the Trojan refugee who carries his gods to Italy and founds the line of Rome, in twelve books, rendered into plain English prose by John Conington.

works.title: Eneados (Douglas)
works.subtitle: The xiii. Bukes of Eneados of the famose poete Virgill translatet into Scottish metir
works.author: Virgil
works.blurb: Gavin Douglas's Middle Scots translation of the Aeneid, finished in 1513 and first printed in London in 1553, the first complete translation of the Aeneid into any form of English, with his own prologue to each book and Vegio's thirteenth book.

works.title: The Aeneid
works.author: Virgil
works.blurb: Virgil's Latin epic of Aeneas, the Trojan refugee who carries his gods to Italy and founds the line of Rome, in twelve books, rendered into English heroic couplets by John Dryden.

works.title: The Aeneid
works.subtitle: Prose translation
works.author: Virgil
works.blurb: Virgil's Latin epic of Aeneas in twelve books, rendered by J. W. Mackail into measured, Biblical-toned English prose.

works.title: The Aeneid
works.subtitle: The Aeneids of Virgil, done into English verse by William Morris
works.author: Virgil
works.blurb: Virgil's Latin epic of Aeneas, the Trojan refugee who carries his gods to Italy and founds the line of Rome, in twelve books, rendered into long rhymed fourteeners by William Morris.

works.title: The Aeneid
works.subtitle: Translated into English blank verse
works.author: Virgil
works.translator: trans. James Rhoades (Longmans, Green, 1893–96; one-volume edition 1907)
works.blurb: Virgil's Latin epic of Aeneas, the Trojan refugee who carries his gods to Italy and founds the line of Rome, in twelve books, rendered into English blank verse by James Rhoades.

works.title: The First Four Books of the Aeneid (Stanyhurst)
works.subtitle: Thee first foure bookes of Virgil his Aeneis translated intoo English heroical verse
works.author: Virgil
works.blurb: An extravagant attempt to naturalise Latin hexameter in English, famous for its coinages and its defiant spelling, covering Aeneas's storm-tossed landing, the fall of Troy, his wanderings and the tragedy of Dido.

works.title: Certain Books of the Aeneid (Surrey)
works.subtitle: Certain bokes of Virgiles Aenaeis turned into English meter
works.author: Virgil
works.translator: trans. Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey (printed 1557)
works.blurb: Surrey's blank-verse rendering of Virgil's account of the fall of Troy (Book II) and of Dido's love and death (Book IV), the poem that gave English its first unrhymed iambic pentameter.

works.title: The Aeneid
works.subtitle: Translated into English verse by E. Fairfax Taylor
works.author: Virgil
works.translator: trans. E. Fairfax Taylor (Everyman's Library, 1907; reprinted 1910)
works.blurb: Virgil's Latin epic of Aeneas, the Trojan refugee who carries his gods to Italy and founds the line of Rome, in twelve books, rendered into English Spenserian stanzas by E. Fairfax Taylor.

works.title: The Aeneid
works.subtitle: Translated into English verse
works.author: Virgil
works.blurb: Virgil's Latin epic of Aeneas, the Trojan refugee who carries his gods to Italy and founds the line of Rome, in twelve books, rendered into English blank verse by Theodore C. Williams.

works.title: The Speeches of Aeschines
works.subtitle: Against Timarchus, On the Embassy and Against Ctesiphon
works.author: Aeschines the Orator
works.blurb: The three surviving speeches of Aeschines, the Athenian orator and rival of Demosthenes: his prosecution of Timarchus (345 BC), his defence on the embassy to Philip (343 BC) and his attack on Ctesiphon over the crown awarded to Demosthenes (330 BC).

works.title: Three Hundred Aesop's Fables
works.subtitle: Literally translated from the Greek
works.author: Aesop
works.blurb: The classic English collection of the fables ascribed to Aesop, the Greek storyteller of the sixth century BC: talking beasts, birds and gods, each ending in a short moral.

works.title: Agamemnon
works.subtitle: The Oresteia
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: Browning's famously literal rendering of the play, in which Klutaimnestra, after ten years' waiting, welcomes Agamemnon home from Troia and murders him, with the captive prophetess Kassandra, in the palace at Argos. Browning keeps the Greek names in their Greek spelling.

works.title: Agamemnon
works.subtitle: The Oresteia
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: Clytemnestra waits through ten years for her husband Agamemnon to return from Troy, and greets him with purple tapestries and fair words. The captive prophetess Cassandra foresees the murder that awaits them both in the palace; Clytemnestra kills the king in his bath, and takes up the rule of Argos with her lover Aegisthus.

works.title: Agamemnon
works.author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
works.blurb: The ghost of Thyestes rises to urge on the doom of the house of Atreus. In Argos, Clytemnestra and Aegisthus, her lover and Thyestes' son, plot to kill her husband on his return from Troy. Agamemnon arrives in triumph with the captive prophetess Cassandra, who foresees his death and her own; he is cut down in the palace, and Electra sends the boy Orestes away to safety before the queen turns on her.

works.title: Ajax
works.subtitle: Aias
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Denied the armour of the dead Akhilleus, which is awarded to Odysseus, Ajax plans to murder the Greek chiefs; Athena drives him mad and he slaughters the army’s flocks instead. Waking to his shame, he deceives his captive-wife Tecmessa and the sailors of Salamis and falls on his sword, and his half-brother Teucer must then defend his body against Menelaus and Agamemnon until Odysseus secures his burial.

works.title: Ajax
works.subtitle: Aias
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: After the arms of the dead Akhilleus are given to Odysseus, Ajax sets out by night to kill the Greek leaders, but Athena clouds his mind and he butchers the army's cattle instead. Waking to his disgrace, he takes leave of his captive Tecmessa and the sailors of Salamis and dies on his own sword, and his half-brother Teucer must then defend the body against Menelaus and Agamemnon until Odysseus secures its burial.

works.title: Albion's England
works.subtitle: A continued historie of the same kingdome, from the originals of the first inhabitants thereof (1597)
works.author: William Warner
works.blurb: William Warner's fourteener history of Britain from Noah and Brutus to the Tudors, in the 1597 edition.

works.title: Alcestis
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Apollo has won Admetus, king of Pherae, the gift that he may escape his death if another dies in his place. Only his wife Alcestis agrees. As she dies, Herakles arrives as a guest, learns the truth, and wrestles Death at her tomb to bring her back.

works.title: The Alchemist
works.author: Ben Jonson
works.blurb: During a plague outbreak in London, Lovewit leaves his house in the care of his butler Face, who lets it to the con man Subtle and his accomplice Dol Common. Posing as an alchemist, Subtle fleeces a lawyer's clerk, a tobacconist, the greedy knight Sir Epicure Mammon and two Puritans of Amsterdam with promises of the philosopher's stone, until the master returns and the scheme collapses. Jonson's fast, savage comedy of London greed.

works.title: Alciphron
works.subtitle: A Fragment
works.author: Thomas Moore
works.blurb: Moore's verse retelling of The Epicurean: an Athenian philosopher's letters from Egypt, ending with the letter of the High Priest Orcus.

works.title: Alexandra
works.author: Lycophron
works.blurb: A riddling monologue in which a slave reports the prophecies of Cassandra, foretelling the fall of Troy and the wanderings of the Greek and Trojan heroes.

works.title: All for Love; or, The World Well Lost
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: John Dryden
works.blurb: Dryden's blank-verse retelling of the last day of Antony and Cleopatra, set in Alexandria after Actium. Ventidius, Dolabella and Octavia pull Antony back toward Rome and duty, while Cleopatra and her eunuch Alexas draw him back to love. Jealousy and a false report of her death drive him to fall on his sword; Cleopatra follows him in death, and the lovers are laid together before Caesar arrives.

works.title: Morte Arthure
works.subtitle: The alliterative Morte Arthure
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: An alliterative Middle English romance of about 4,350 long lines, preserved in Robert Thornton's manuscript, telling the end of King Arthur's reign: the Roman emperor Lucius demands tribute, Arthur crosses to the Continent and kills the giant of Mont-Saint-Michel, defeats the Romans and sets out for Rome, but is recalled by Mordred's treason, loses Gawain at the landing, and meets Mordred in a last battle before he is carried to Avalon. It is one of the finest English alliterative poems and a source for Malory.

works.title: All's Well That Ends Well
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Helena, the orphaned daughter of a famous physician, loves Bertram, the young Count of Rossillon, who is far above her in rank and will not look at her. When she cures the dying King of France with her father's remedy, she asks for Bertram as her reward, but he flees to the Florentine wars rather than accept her. She follows him, and by a bed-trick and a stolen ring she fulfils the impossible conditions he sets, while his braggart companion Parolles is exposed as a coward and a liar. This so-called problem comedy makes a bitter, unsettled mirror of the marriage plot, and its title is shadowed by doubt about whether all can truly be well.

works.title: Alma: or, the Progress of the Mind
works.subtitle: A Poem in Three Cantos
works.author: Matthew Prior
works.blurb: Prior's tetrameter conversation between Matthew and Richard, in the manner of Hudibras, on the seat of the soul: Alma, the mind, climbs through the body from the toes to the head.

works.title: America: A Prophecy
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Blake's prophecy of the American Revolution, in which the fiery spirit Orc rises against Albion's Angel and the Thirteen Colonies break free.

works.title: Amis and Amiloun
works.subtitle: A verse rendering
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: Two Lombard knights, born on the same night and alike as twins, swear brotherhood. When Amis is accused by a treacherous steward and must face trial by combat, Amiloun takes his place, and pays for it with leprosy; years later Amis, in turn, must sacrifice his own children to cure his friend.

works.title: The Roman History
works.subtitle: Books XIV–XXXI, Yonge translation, 1862
works.author: Ammianus Marcellinus
works.blurb: Ammianus Marcellinus's history of the Roman Empire from AD 353 to the disaster at Adrianople in AD 378, in the surviving Books XIV to XXXI, in C. D. Yonge's English prose of 1862.

works.title: Amours de Voyage
works.author: Arthur Hugh Clough
works.blurb: An epistolary novel in hexameters, set in Rome during the French siege of 1849, in which the doubting Claude and the Trevellyn sisters write home and fail to find one another.

works.title: Andreas
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The apostle Andrew's perilous sea voyage to rescue Matthew from the cannibalistic Mermedonians, told in a style deliberately recalling Beowulf's heroic diction.

works.title: Andreas (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The apostle Andrew's perilous sea voyage to rescue Matthew from the cannibalistic Mermedonians, told in a style deliberately recalling Beowulf's heroic diction, in the original Old English.

works.title: Andromache
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Taken to Thessaly as the spoil of Akhilleus' son Neoptolemus, the Trojan captive Andromache clings to the altar of Thetis while Neoptolemus' jealous Spartan wife Hermione and her father Menelaus plot the death of her and her child. Old Peleus comes to her rescue, but Hermione, terrified of her husband's return, is carried off by Orestes, who contrives that Neoptolemus is killed at Delphi. Arthur Way renders the play in English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Antigone
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Antigone defies Creon’s edict and buries her brother Polynices, who died attacking Thebes. Condemned to be walled up alive, she hangs herself; Creon’s son Haemon, her betrothed, and then Creon’s wife Eurydice take their own lives, and the king is left to his ruin.

works.title: Antigone
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Thebes has fallen to Creon, who forbids burial of the traitor Polyneices on pain of death. His sister Antigone buries him anyway, appealing to the unwritten laws of the gods, and is sentenced to a living tomb. Jebb's plain prose follows the quarrel of niece and king through to the suicides of Antigone, Haemon and Eurydice, and Creon's broken closing lament.

works.title: The Tragedy of Antony and Cleopatra
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Mark Antony, one of the three rulers of Rome, lingers in Alexandria in the arms of Cleopatra, Queen of Egypt, until news of his wife's death and of Pompey's rising calls him home. He marries Caesar's sister Octavia to mend the peace, but soon returns to Cleopatra and is destroyed by Octavius Caesar's forces at Actium. Believing Cleopatra dead, Antony falls on his sword; she, refusing to be led in triumph through Rome, takes her own life with an asp.

works.title: The Library and Epitome
works.subtitle: The Library of Greek Mythology
works.author: Apollodorus
works.blurb: A systematic handbook of Greek myth, from the birth of the gods and the families of the heroes to the Trojan War and the homecomings, with the Epitome preserving the lost end of the text.

works.title: The Roman History: The Civil Wars
works.subtitle: The Civil Wars, Books I–V
works.author: Appian of Alexandria
works.blurb: Appian's account of Rome's civil wars from the Gracchi to the triumph of Octavian, in Horace White's English prose of 1899.

works.title: The Roman History: Preface and Foreign Wars
works.author: Appian of Alexandria
works.blurb: Appian's history of Rome's wars against other peoples, from the kings and Italy to Spain, Carthage, Illyria, Syria and Mithridates, arranged by nation.

sections.title: Of Sicily and the Other Islands

works.title: The Golden Asse
works.subtitle: The Metamorphoses of Apuleius, in Adlington's Tudor translation
works.author: Apuleius
works.blurb: Lucius, a curious young man of Thessaly, is turned into an ass by a witch's ointment and endures many masters and adventures, including the tale of Cupid and Psyche, until the goddess Isis restores him.

works.title: The Argonautica
works.author: Apollonius of Rhodes
works.blurb: Jason and the Argonauts sail to Colchis for the Golden Fleece, and Medea's love for him decides the quest, in the Hellenistic epic told in four books.

works.title: The Tale of the Argonauts
works.author: Apollonius of Rhodes
works.blurb: Jason and the Argonauts sail to Colchis for the Golden Fleece, and Medea's love for him decides the quest, in Arthur Way's rhymed English verse version of the Hellenistic epic.

works.title: Aria da Capo
works.subtitle: A Play in One Act
works.author: Edna St. Vincent Millay
works.blurb: At a black-and-white Harlequinade supper, Pierrot and Columbine play at love and boredom until the masque of Tragedy, Cothurnus, orders them off the stage to make room for a pastoral scene. Two shepherds, Thyrsis and Corydon, build a wall of coloured ribbons between their pastures, quarrel over a pool and a mine of jewels, and destroy each other. When the bodies are dragged away, Pierrot and Columbine resume their supper from the beginning: a one-act verse play against war and indifference, first performed in 1919.

works.title: The Acharnians
works.subtitle: A comedy first produced at Athens in 425 BC
works.author: Aristophanes
works.blurb: When the Assembly will not make peace, the countryman Dicaeopolis makes a private treaty with Sparta, wins round the furious old men of Acharnae with a speech made in a beggar's rags borrowed from Euripides, and opens a market of his own, while the general Lamachus marches off to war and comes home wounded as Dicaeopolis sits down to feast.

works.title: Aristophanes' Apology
works.subtitle: Including a Transcript from Euripides, Being the Last Adventure of Balaustion
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: Balaustion's account of the fall of Athens and a debate with Aristophanes on poetry, containing Browning's version of Euripides' Herakles.

works.title: The Birds
works.subtitle: A comedy first produced at Athens in 414 BC
works.author: Aristophanes
works.blurb: Two Athenians, sick of the law-courts, persuade the birds to build a walled city in the air, Cloudcuckoobury, which starves the gods of sacrifice until Zeus sends envoys and Peisthetaerus wins his sceptre and a royal bride.

works.title: The Clouds
works.subtitle: A comedy first produced at Athens in 423 BC
works.author: Aristophanes
works.blurb: Strepsiades, ruined by the debts of his horse-mad son, enrols in Socrates's Thinking-Shop to learn the Unjust Logic and cheat his creditors, but his son learns it too, with disastrous results.

works.title: The Ecclesiazusae
works.subtitle: A comedy first produced at Athens in 393 BC
works.author: Aristophanes
works.blurb: Praxagora, at the head of a band of Athenian women who have borrowed their husbands' cloaks and put on false beards, carries a motion in the Assembly handing the city over to the women, and then decrees that property and love shall be held in common, with riotous results for her husband Blepyrus, a stingy citizen and a young man hunted down by three old hags.

works.title: The Frogs
works.subtitle: A comedy first produced at Athens in 405 BC
works.author: Aristophanes
works.blurb: Dionysus, sick of the dearth of good poets in Athens, travels to Hades with his slave Xanthias to bring Euripides back from the dead, and ends by judging a contest between Aeschylus and Euripides for the tragic throne, in which their verses are weighed in the scales.

works.title: The Knights
works.subtitle: A comedy first produced at Athens in 424 BC
works.author: Aristophanes
works.blurb: Two harassed slaves of old Demus, the Athenian people, plot to topple their fellow slave Paphlagon, a thinly veiled Cleon, by pitting against him a Sausage-seller who is even coarser, louder and more shameless than he.

works.title: The Plutus
works.subtitle: A comedy first produced at Athens in 388 BC
works.author: Aristophanes
works.blurb: Chremylus, a good man who has stayed poor, follows a blind beggar home on the advice of Apollo's oracle and finds him to be Wealth himself. With his slave Cario he sets out to cure the god's sight so that the honest may prosper, braves the arguments of Poverty, has Wealth healed at the temple of Asclepius, and sees the world turned upside down: an informer is stripped, an old woman is dropped by her young lover, and Hermes and the priest of Zeus come begging for a living.

works.title: The Wasps
works.subtitle: A comedy first produced at Athens in 422 BC
works.author: Aristophanes
works.blurb: Philocleon, an old Athenian addicted to sitting on juries, is kept shut up at home by his son Bdelycleon, who tries to cure him by holding a mock trial in the house (the dog Labes is charged with stealing a cheese) and by teaching him the manners of a gentleman, with riotous results.

works.title: The Athenian Constitution
works.subtitle: The Constitution of Athens, in sixty-nine parts
works.author: Aristotle
works.blurb: The one surviving 'constitution' of the 158 that Aristotle's school compiled: a history of Athenian government from Draco and Solon to the fall of the Thirty and the restored democracy, followed by an account of how the city's offices and law courts worked in Aristotle's own day.

works.title: Metaphysics
works.subtitle: Metaphysica, in fourteen books
works.author: Aristotle
works.blurb: Aristotle's treatise on first philosophy, the study of being as being, of substance, form and matter, potency and act, and of the unmoved mover.

works.title: Nicomachean Ethics
works.subtitle: Ethics in ten books
works.author: Aristotle
works.blurb: Aristotle's treatise on the good life: happiness as activity in accordance with virtue, the moral and intellectual virtues, justice, pleasure, friendship and the contemplative life.

works.title: Poetics
works.subtitle: On the art of poetry, tragedy and epic, in twenty-six chapters
works.author: Aristotle
works.blurb: Aristotle's short treatise on poetic art: imitation, the structure of tragic plot, character, diction, and the comparison of epic with tragedy.

works.title: Politics
works.subtitle: A Treatise on Government, in eight books
works.author: Aristotle
works.blurb: Aristotle's treatise on the city and its constitutions: the household and the state, the best regime, citizenship, the kinds of government, revolutions and their causes, and the education of the citizen.

works.title: Rhetoric
works.subtitle: On the art of persuasion, in three books
works.author: Aristotle
works.blurb: Aristotle's treatise on rhetoric: the modes of persuasion, the emotions and characters of audiences, the lines of argument, and the choice and arrangement of style.

works.title: The Anabasis of Alexander
works.subtitle: The History of Alexander’s Campaigns, in seven books
works.author: Arrian
works.blurb: Arrian’s account of the campaigns of Alexander the Great, from his accession to his death at Babylon, in E. J. Chinnock’s English prose of 1884.

works.title: The Art of Preserving Health
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: John Armstrong
works.blurb: A blank-verse didactic poem in four books on air, diet, exercise and the passions, as ingredients of a healthy life.

works.title: As You Like It
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Banished from her uncle's court, Rosalind flees to the Forest of Arden disguised as the youth Ganymede, with her cousin Celia and the clown Touchstone, and meets the lovesick Orlando, whom she teaches to woo her in mock courtship. Among exiled lords, shepherds and rustic couples, mistaken loves are sorted out, the usurping duke is turned from his purpose, and the play ends in four weddings and Rosalind's epilogue.

works.title: The Ascent of Man
works.author: Mathilde Blind
works.blurb: Mathilde Blind's evolutionary long poem, in three parts, tracing life and the human soul from the primeval waters through the Pilgrim Soul's quest to the consoling leading of Sorrow.

sections.title: Part III: The Leading of Sorrow

works.title: The Assumption of Our Lady
works.subtitle: Middle English text of Cambridge University Library MS Gg.4.27.2 (to l. 240), continued from British Library MS Harley 2382, ed. J. R. Lumby (1866), re-ed. G. H. McKnight (1901)
works.author: Anonymous
works.blurb: A Middle English verse legend of the death of the Virgin: warned by an angel, Mary takes leave of John, the apostles are miraculously gathered, and Christ comes to bear her soul and body up to heaven.

works.title: At the Hawk's Well
works.subtitle: A play for dancers
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: Cuchulain, a young hero, climbs a barren hillside in search of a well whose waters give immortality. An Old Man has waited beside the dry well for fifty years, and warns him that the guardian, possessed by a hawk-woman of the Sidhe, will lure him away just when the water rises. Three masked Musicians open and close the play with songs and the folding of a black cloth.

works.title: Atalanta in Calydon
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: Algernon Charles Swinburne
works.blurb: A tragedy on the Greek model: the hunt of the Calydonian boar, the doom of Meleager, and the choruses that made Swinburne's name.

works.title: The Deipnosophists, Volume I: Books 1–5
works.subtitle: Or, The Banquet of the Learned
works.author: Athenaeus
works.blurb: A learned banquet in Rome, c. 200, told as a conversation: the guests of the host Larensius talk through food, wine, parasites, cooks and cups, quoting hundreds of lost Greek poets and comedians as they go. Books 1–5 cover the first feasts and the long preserved fragments of the Greek comic poets.

works.title: The Deipnosophists, Volume II: Books 7–11
works.subtitle: Or, The Banquet of the Learned
works.author: Athenaeus
works.blurb: The banquet of the learned goes on: Books 7–11 hold the long catalogue of fishes and the sayings of the comic poets about them, then ham, vegetables and fruit, the riddles and drinking games of the symposium, and the great survey of cups and goblets.

works.title: The Deipnosophists, Volume III: Books 12–15
works.subtitle: Or, The Banquet of the Learned
works.author: Athenaeus
works.blurb: The banquet of the learned continues: Book XII on luxury and the pleasures of peoples, Book XIII on women, love and the courtesans of Greece, Book XIV on cakes, music and the dessert course, and Book XV on garlands, perfumes and the songs of the table, all threaded with quotations from lost Greek poets and comedians.

works.title: Atta Troll
works.subtitle: A Summer Night's Dream
works.author: Heinrich Heine
works.blurb: Heine's mock-heroic satire in twenty-seven cantos, written in 1841 and published in 1847: a dancing bear escapes from his master at Cauterets in the Pyrenees, and the pursuit becomes a burlesque of the political poets and doctrinaire radicals of the day.

works.title: Aucassin and Nicolete
works.subtitle: The Song-Story of Aucassin and Nicolete
works.author: Anonymous (Old French)
works.blurb: The tale of the Count of Biaucaire's son, who would rather lose his knighthood than his love for the Saracen slave girl Nicolete, told in alternating sung verse and spoken prose.

works.title: Aurora Leigh
works.author: Elizabeth Barrett Browning
works.blurb: Elizabeth Barrett Browning's verse novel in nine books of blank verse, telling in the first person the life of Aurora Leigh, a poet who must choose between art and love, and her relation to her cousin Romney, a social reformer.

works.title: The Avowynge of King Arther
works.subtitle: The Avowing of King Arthur, Sir Gawan, Sir Kaye, and Sir Bawdewyn of Bretan
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: While King Arthur hunts at Carlisle, a monstrous boar draws the Round Table into a night of vows: Arthur swears to hunt it down alone and keep watch over it, Gawain to guard a lady against all comers, Kay to defend a forest against every knight, and Baldwin never to be jealous, never to refuse a guest, and never to fear death. A north-of-England verse romance of seventy-two sixteen-line stanzas.

works.title: The Anturs of Arther at the Tarnewathelan
works.subtitle: The Awntyrs off Arthure at the Terne Wathelyn
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: While Arthur hunts near Tarn Wadling, the ghost of Queen Guinevere's mother rises from torment to warn her of the fate that awaits the proud and the worldly, and of the fall of Arthur's realm; the court then rides to Carlisle, where the Scottish knight Sir Galeron claims Gawain's lands and the two meet in single combat. A north-of-England alliterative romance in fifty-five thirteen-line stanzas.

works.title: The Bacchae
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: The god Dionysus comes in human guise to Thebes, where the young king Pentheus denies his divinity, imprisons the stranger and tries to suppress the rites of the maenads. The god drives the Theban women to the mountain, lures Pentheus to spy on them in woman's dress, and brings about a terrible end at the hands of his own mother Agave. Gilbert Murray renders the tragedy in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: The Bacchanals
works.subtitle: The Bacchae
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: The Wine-god Dionysus comes in human guise to Thebes, where the young king Pentheus denies his godhead and tries to chain the stranger and suppress his rites. The god maddens the Theban women, drives them to the mountain, and lures Pentheus to spy on them in woman's dress, with a terrible end at the hands of his own mother Agave. Arthur S. Way's English verse translation, with rhymed choral odes.

works.title: Balaustion's Adventure
works.subtitle: Including a Transcript from Euripides
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A young Rhodian woman recounts how she saved a shipload of Athenians at Syracuse by reciting Euripides' Alkestis, which Browning renders in full within her narrative.

works.title: The Ballad of the White Horse
works.author: G. K. Chesterton
works.blurb: Chesterton's ballad of King Alfred and the battle of Ethandune, in eight books framed by a verse dedication to his wife: the Vision of the Virgin, the gathering of the chiefs, the harp in the Danish camp, the woman and the cakes, and the three stages of the battle.

works.title: The Baron's Little Daughter
works.author: Cecil Frances Alexander
works.blurb: A long narrative poem from Cecil Frances Alexander's collected Poems (1896).

works.title: The Barons' Wars
works.subtitle: In the Reign of Edward the Second (Books II–VI)
works.author: Michael Drayton
works.blurb: Drayton's verse chronicle of the civil wars under Edward II, in ottava rima — this edition preserves Books II through VI.

works.title: The Battaile of Agincourt
works.author: Michael Drayton
works.blurb: Drayton's account, in 315 eight-line stanzas, of Henry V's French campaign and the victory at Agincourt, opening with the dispute over the Salic law.

works.title: Homer's Battle of the Frogs and Mice
works.subtitle: after the pseudo-Homeric Batrachomyomachia
works.author: Thomas Parnell
works.blurb: Parnell's mock-heroic version of the Battle of the Frogs and Mice: a mouse drowns on a frog's back, and the two nations go to war while the gods look on.

works.title: Becket
works.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
works.blurb: Henry II raises his friend and Chancellor Thomas Becket to the see of Canterbury, hoping for an ally in the Church; Becket instead defends the Church's rights against the Crown. Through the quarrel at Northampton, exile in France, a patched-up reconciliation and the King's hidden love for Rosamund, the two old friends move toward the murder of the Archbishop in his own cathedral.

works.title: Bella Gorry
works.subtitle: The Pazon's Story
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: The Pazon's story, in blank verse, of Bella Gorry, who lived in a clay-walled cottage on the sandy coast near the Point of Ayre.

works.title: Beowulf
works.author: Beowulf Poet
works.blurb: The Geatish hero Beowulf crosses the sea to rid the Danish hall of Heorot of the monster Grendel, then Grendel's vengeful mother, and in old age faces a dragon guarding a cursed hoard — the oldest surviving epic in English.

sections.title: Prelude of the Founder of the Danish House

works.title: Beowulf (Hall)
works.subtitle: An Anglo-Saxon Epic Poem
works.author: Beowulf Poet
works.blurb: Hall renders the poem in close alliterative verse that keeps the four-stress line and heaps up compound words in the manner of the Old English original.

works.subtitle: Translated from Anglo-Saxon into Modern English Prose
works.author: Beowulf Poet
works.blurb: Kirtlan tells the story in plain modern English prose, following the Old English closely but without any attempt at verse or archaism.

works.title: The Tale of Beowulf (Morris & Wyatt)
works.subtitle: Sometime King of the Folk of the Weder Geats
works.author: Beowulf Poet
works.translator: trans. William Morris and A. J. Wyatt (1895)
works.blurb: Morris translates in a deliberately archaic diction, thick with Old English words and inverted syntax, so that the poem reads as if it had been composed in the saga-age English of his imagination.

works.title: Beowulf (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Beowulf Poet
works.blurb: The Geatish hero Beowulf crosses the sea to rid the Danish hall of Heorot of the monster Grendel, then Grendel's mother, and in old age faces a dragon guarding a cursed hoard, in the original Old English of the oldest surviving epic in English.

works.title: Betsy Lee
works.subtitle: Fo'c's'le Yarns, First Series: I
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: A Manx fisherman tells, in rhymed dialect couplets, how he courted Betsy Lee and lost her; the first of Brown's Fo'c's'le Yarns.

works.title: Beware of Smooth Water
works.author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
works.blurb: A light comedy of courtship in a Spanish household, where Don Alonso's daughters Clara and Eugenia, a nephew, gallants and servants cross one another's purposes. FitzGerald thinks it written for the 1649 wedding of Philip IV, and it closes on its own moral: beware of all smooth waters.

works.title: The Song Celestial
works.subtitle: Bhagavad Gita (from the Mahabharata)
works.author: Vyasa
works.blurb: On the field of Kurukshetra, as two armies stand ready, the warrior Arjuna lets fall his bow, and his charioteer, the god Krishna, answers his despair in eighteen chapters on duty, devotion and the self. Arnold renders the Sanskrit in blank verse, shifting into lyrical measures where the original does. The Gita is attributed by tradition to Vyasa.

works.title: Bird Parliament
works.subtitle: abridged from the Mantiq al-Tair
works.author: Farid al-Din Attar
works.blurb: An abridged English version of Attar's Sufi allegory in which the birds of the world gather to choose a king, are led by the hoopoe through seven valleys, and the few that survive the journey find that the Simorgh they seek is the mirror of themselves.

works.title: The Birth of the War-God
works.subtitle: Kumarasambhava
works.author: Kalidasa
works.blurb: Kalidasa's Sanskrit epic of the courtship of Shiva and Uma and the birth of Kumara, god of war, in seven cantos, in Griffith's rhymed couplets.

sections.title: Canto II: The Address to Brahmá
Canto III: The Death of Love

works.title: Black Marigolds (Chaurapanchasika)
works.subtitle: A free interpretation of the Chaurapanchasika
works.author: Bilhana
works.blurb: Fifty stanzas, each beginning "Even now", in which a condemned lover remembers his princess, in E. Powys Mathers's free-verse rendering of the poem attributed to the Kashmiri poet Bilhana.

works.title: A Blot in the 'Scutcheon: A Tragedy
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: Mildred Tresham, sister of the proud Earl Tresham, has secretly taken Lord Mertoun as her lover, and when he comes openly to ask for her hand the family honour seems about to be satisfied. Thorold Tresham learns of the earlier nights from his old retainer Gerard and, believing his house disgraced, confronts them both. Mertoun is killed in a duel at the foot of the yew-tree avenue, Mildred dies of grief, and Thorold dies after forgiving them, leaving the blot he sought to wipe away.

works.title: Griselda
works.subtitle: A Society Novel in Rhymed Verse
works.author: Wilfrid Scawen Blunt
works.blurb: Blunt's novel in rhyming couplets of Parisian and London society in the nineteenth century, told over five chapters.

works.title: Satan Absolved
works.subtitle: A Victorian Mystery
works.author: Wilfrid Scawen Blunt
works.blurb: A satirical dialogue in verse in which Satan pleads before the assembled angels and the Lord God, set against the conduct of Christian nations.

sections.title: Part I: The Antechamber of Heaven
Part II: The Lord God Holds Audience

works.title: The Consolation of Philosophy
works.subtitle: trans. H. R. James (1897)
works.author: Boethius
works.blurb: Imprisoned at Pavia and awaiting execution, the statesman Boethius is visited by Lady Philosophy, who drives away the Muses of tragic poetry and leads him, in alternating prose argument and verse, from grief at his fall to an understanding of true happiness, the government of the world by Providence, and the reconciliation of divine foreknowledge with human free will.

Book III: True Happiness and False

works.title: The Book of Ahania
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Fuzon's revolt against Urizen, the casting out of Ahania, and her lament over the Tree of Mystery.

works.title: The Book of Los
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Eno's lament, the binding of Urizen, and Los's forging of the Sun in the void.

works.title: The Egyptian Book of the Dead
works.subtitle: Translation and Commentary
works.author: Anonymous Egyptian Poets
works.translator: trans. P. Le Page Renouf and Édouard Naville (1904)
works.blurb: The funerary spells of ancient Egypt, known as the Chapters of Coming Forth by Day, from hymns to the sun and the Negative Confession to charms for the heart and the tomb, in the English translation of Renouf and Naville (1904).

works.title: The Book of the Duchess
works.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
works.blurb: An elegy in dream form: a sleepless narrator reads the tale of Ceyx and Alcyone, then dreams of a grieving Black Knight in a forest, whose lost lady, White, is widely taken to honour Blanche of Lancaster.

works.title: The Book of Thel
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: The shepherdess Thel questions Lily, Cloud, Worm and Clay about why life fades, enters the land of the dead, and flees back to the vales of Har.

works.title: The Book of Urizen
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Blake's myth of creation and fall: Urizen, the reasoning lawgiver, is cast out, bound by Los, and the material world and its religion take shape.

works.title: Boris Godunov
works.subtitle: A Drama in Verse
works.author: Alexander Pushkin
works.blurb: Pushkin's historical tragedy of the Time of Troubles. After the death of the young Tsarevich Dimitry, the boyar Boris Godunov is begged to take the crown, but a novice monk, Gregory Otrepiev, learns that he may pass himself off as the murdered prince and escapes to Poland. Backed by Polish nobles and the love of Marina, the Pretender invades Russia, while Boris, haunted by his crime, sees his power fail. Boris dies, and on the Pretender's approach Moscow turns against the family of Godunov.

sections.title: The Palace of the Kremlin (20 February 1598)
The Virgin's Field. The New Nunnery
Night. Cell in the Monastery of Chudov (1603)
Castle of the Governor. Mnishek in Sambor
A Plain near Novgorod Seversk (21 December 1604)
Open Space in Front of the Cathedral in Moscow

works.title: The Bothie of Tober-na-Vuolich
works.subtitle: A Long-Vacation Pastoral
works.author: Arthur Hugh Clough
works.blurb: A long-vacation pastoral in nine cantos of English hexameters, in which Oxford reading-party men and a Highland girl, Elspie, put the class question to the test of love.

works.title: Brand
works.subtitle: A Dramatic Poem
works.author: Henrik Ibsen
works.blurb: Brand, a young priest, preaches an absolute creed: all or nothing. He holds his village, his dying mother, his wife Agnes and his own child to that demand, and the cost rises with every act, until he stands alone on the ice-fields with the mad girl Gerd and the avalanche above him.

works.title: The Bridal of Triermain
works.subtitle: or, The Vale of St. John
works.author: Sir Walter Scott
works.blurb: A verse romance in three cantos, framed as a lover's tale told to Lucy: it follows Sir Roland de Vaux of Triermain into the enchanted Castle of Saint John, where he wakes the sleeping Gyneth, King Arthur's daughter, from her spell.

works.title: Britannia's Pastorals
works.subtitle: Books I-III (Book III unfinished)
works.author: William Browne of Tavistock
works.blurb: Browne's long Spenserian pastoral of Devon shepherds and nymphs, in rhymed pentameter couplets: the love of Marina and Celandine, her rescue from Famine's cave, and the shepherds' songs, in two books (1613, 1616) and an unfinished third.

works.title: The Bronze Cavalier
works.subtitle: A poem in two cantos
works.author: Alexander Pushkin
works.blurb: Pushkin's St Petersburg tale of the clerk Evgeny, ruined by the flood of 1824, and the bronze statue of Peter the Great that pursues him, in Charles Edward Turner's 1899 English version.

works.title: The Bruce
works.subtitle: Original Older Scots text, ed. W. M. Mackenzie (1909)
works.author: John Barbour
works.blurb: Barbour's verse chronicle of Robert the Bruce and Sir James Douglas and the Scottish War of Independence, culminating in Bannockburn, with its famous praise of freedom.

works.title: The Buddha-karita
works.subtitle: The Life of the Buddha
works.author: Asvaghosha
works.blurb: The first Sanskrit court epic on the life of the Buddha, from his birth at Kapilavastu to his enlightenment and first teaching.

works.title: The Bustan
works.subtitle: The Garden of Fruit, translated from the Persian by A. Hart Edwards
works.author: Sa'di of Shiraz
works.blurb: Sa'di's Garden of Fruit (1257): ten chapters of counsel and moral tales on justice, benevolence, love, humility, resignation, contentment, education, gratitude, repentance and prayer.

sections.title: Chapter I: Concerning Justice, Counsel, and the Administration of Government

works.title: Cain
works.subtitle: A Mystery
works.author: George Gordon, Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's biblical drama in three acts, first published in 1821. Cain, resentful of the fate bequeathed by his parents' fall, is led by Lucifer through the abyss of space and the realm of the dead, where he is shown the vastness of creation and the meaning of death. Returning to earth, he kills his brother Abel in a rage at God's favour and is marked by an angel and driven eastward from Eden.

works.title: Calvary
works.subtitle: A play for dancers
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: On the road to Calvary Christ is met first by Lazarus, who asks for the death he was denied, and then by Judas, who betrayed Him so as to be free of His power. Three Roman soldiers, who care for nothing but their dice, gamble for His cloak. The Musicians sing of the herons, swans and eagles for whom God has not died.

works.title: The Canterbury Tales
works.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
works.blurb: A fellowship of pilgrims riding from Southwark to Canterbury pass the road in stories — chivalric romance, low comedy, sermon, and fable — in the original Middle English, the foundation of English narrative poetry.

works.title: Captain Craig
works.author: Edwin Arlington Robinson
works.blurb: A blank-verse narrative in three parts: the narrator's friendship with a ragged, philosophizing old man in Tilbury Town.

works.title: Captain Tom and Captain Hugh
works.subtitle: Fo'c's'le Yarns, First Series: III
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: A dialect yarn about two Castletown sea captains who were schoolfellows, told by a seaman who warns that it is not much of a story.

works.title: Dio's Rome, Volume 1: Epitome of Books 1–21
works.subtitle: The Roman History of Cassius Dio, Books 1–21, from the landing of Aeneas to the Second Punic War and after, as preserved in the epitome of Zonaras
works.author: Cassius Dio
works.blurb: Dio's Roman History for the early centuries: the Trojan beginnings, the kings, the Republic and the wars against Pyrrhus and Carthage, as Zonaras epitomised the lost books, in Herbert Baldwin Foster's English of 1905.

works.title: Dio's Rome, Volume 2: Books 36–44
works.subtitle: The Roman History of Cassius Dio, Books 36–44, from Pompey's eastern wars (69 B.C.) to the aftermath of Caesar's assassination (44 B.C.)
works.author: Cassius Dio
works.blurb: Dio's Roman History for the last years of the Republic: Pompey's eastern wars, Cicero and Catiline, Caesar's conquest of Gaul, the civil war with Pompey, Caesar's dictatorship and his assassination, in Herbert Baldwin Foster's English of 1905.

works.title: Dio's Rome, Volume 3: Books 45–51
works.subtitle: The Roman History of Cassius Dio, Books 45–51, from the rise of Octavian after Caesar's murder to the death of Antony and the conquest of Egypt (44–29 B.C.)
works.author: Cassius Dio
works.blurb: Dio's Roman History for the years after Caesar's murder: Cicero against Antony, Mutina, the Triumvirate, Philippi, the Perusine war, Sextus Pompey, Actium and the fall of Cleopatra, in Herbert Baldwin Foster's English of 1905.

works.title: Dio's Rome, Volume 4: Books 52–60
works.subtitle: The Roman History of Cassius Dio, Books 52–60, from Maecenas and Agrippa on monarchy and the settlement of Augustus to the reign of Claudius (29 B.C. – A.D. 54)
works.author: Cassius Dio
works.blurb: Dio's Roman History for the principate of Augustus and his successors: the debate of Agrippa and Maecenas, the settlement of 27 B.C., Augustus's later years, Tiberius, Gaius and Claudius, in Herbert Baldwin Foster's English of 1905.

works.title: Dio's Rome, Volume 5: Books 61–76
works.subtitle: The Roman History of Cassius Dio, Books 61–76, from the death of Claudius and the reign of Nero to the reign of Septimius Severus (A.D. 54 – 211)
works.author: Cassius Dio
works.blurb: Dio's Roman History for the later first and the second century: Nero, the year of the four emperors, the Flavians, Trajan and Hadrian, Marcus Aurelius, Commodus, Pertinax and Septimius Severus, in Herbert Baldwin Foster's English of 1905.

works.title: Dio's Rome, Volume 6: Books 77–80
works.subtitle: The Roman History of Cassius Dio, Books 77–80, from the accession of Caracalla to the reign of Alexander Severus and the close of the History (A.D. 211–229)
works.author: Cassius Dio
works.blurb: Dio's Roman History for the reigns of Caracalla, Macrinus, Elagabalus and Alexander Severus, ending with Dio's own account of his retirement, in Herbert Baldwin Foster's English.

works.title: The Castle of Indolence: An Allegorical Poem
works.subtitle: Written in imitation of Spenser
works.author: James Thomson
works.blurb: Thomson's Spenserian allegory of a wizard's enchanted castle of sloth and the knight of arts and industry who overthrows it.

works.title: Cavender's House
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Edwin Arlington Robinson
works.blurb: Blank-verse narrative in three parts: Cavender returns after twelve years to his shuttered, darkened house and is confronted there by the presence of Laramie.

works.title: The Chase
works.author: William Somervile
works.blurb: A blank-verse poem in four books on hunting, from the breeding of hounds to the pursuit of the hare, the stag and the fox.

works.title: Chastelard: A Tragedy
works.author: Algernon Charles Swinburne
works.blurb: The first play of Swinburne's Mary Stuart trilogy. At the court of Mary, Queen of Scots, the French poet Chastelard, who has followed her from France, is bound to her by a desperate passion. Hidden in her bedchamber, he is discovered, spared, and then caught there a second time. He is condemned to death at St Andrews, and goes to the scaffold unrepentant, while the Queen, who has used and tempted him, looks on.

works.title: Childe Harold's Pilgrimage
works.author: Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's Spenserian travelogue in four cantos follows a world-weary young pilgrim through Portugal, Spain, Greece, Belgium, the Rhine and Italy, turning from personal gloom to meditations on liberty, ruin and the sublime.

works.title: Childe John
works.subtitle: János vitéz
works.author: Sándor Petőfi
works.blurb: Petőfi's Hungarian folk epic in twenty-seven cantos: the shepherd boy Jancsi (Childe John) is parted from his sweetheart Helen and goes out into the world through war, giants and witches, until he wins her back and a fairy kingdom, here in English verse by William N. Loew.

works.title: The Children of Herakles
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Hunted from city to city by the vengeful king Eurystheus, the old warrior Iolaus shelters the children of the dead Herakles at the altar of Zeus in Marathon. Demophon of Athens takes up their cause, but an oracle demands the sacrifice of a noble maiden before victory can be won, and Herakles' daughter Makaria offers her own life. Arthur Way renders the play in English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Christ I
works.subtitle: The Advent Lyrics
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: A sequence of lyric meditations, based on the liturgical O Antiphons of Advent, anticipating the coming of Christ.

works.title: Christ I (Old English)
works.subtitle: The Advent Lyrics: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The Old English verse of the Advent Lyrics: a sequence of lyric meditations, based on the liturgical O Antiphons of Advent, anticipating the coming of Christ.

works.title: Christ II
works.subtitle: The Ascension
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: Cynewulf's account of Christ's Ascension into heaven, drawing on a homily of Gregory the Great, and of the gifts of grace bestowed on humankind.

works.title: Christ II (Old English)
works.subtitle: The Ascension: Old English text
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: The Old English verse of Cynewulf's account of Christ's Ascension into heaven, drawing on a homily of Gregory the Great, and of the gifts of grace bestowed on humankind.

works.title: Christ III
works.subtitle: Judgment Day
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: A vision of the Last Judgment: Christ's sudden return, the terror of sinners and the joy of the blessed, closing the Exeter Book's Christ sequence.

works.title: Christ III (Old English)
works.subtitle: Judgment Day: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The Old English verse of a vision of the Last Judgment: Christ's sudden return, the terror of sinners and the joy of the blessed, closing the Exeter Book's Christ sequence.

works.title: Christ and Satan
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The last poem of the Junius Manuscript: the lament of the fallen angels in hell, Christ's Harrowing of Hell and Ascension, and finally Satan's temptation of Christ in the wilderness.

works.title: Christ and Satan (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The Old English verse of the Junius Manuscript in the Krapp and Dobbie edition: the last poem of the Junius Manuscript: the lament of the fallen angels in hell, Christ's Harrowing of Hell and Ascension, and finally Satan's temptation of Christ in the wilderness.

works.title: The Christian Captives
works.subtitle: A Tragedy in Five Acts in a mixed manner
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's tragedy in five acts, first published in 1890. In a castle garden by the sea, Almeh, daughter of the King of Fez, meets the Christian captives of the Moorish court, among them the Portuguese princes Ferdinand and Enrique; a chorus of the captives sings Latin hymns and speaks in turn.

works.title: Christmas Rose
works.subtitle: Fo'c's'le Yarns, First Series: II
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: A dialect yarn that begins on a Christmas-time evening at the school in the year of the great storm of 'hunder-thirty-nine' and ends with the mystery of who or what the Christmas Rose was.

works.title: Christs Victorie and Triumph
works.subtitle: in Heaven, and Earth, over, and after Death
works.author: Giles Fletcher the Younger
works.blurb: A Spenserian poem in four parts on the redemption of man, from Mercy's plea in heaven to Christ's temptation, his death on the cross and his resurrection and ascension.

works.title: Chronicle of England
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A rhymed chronicle of about 1,040 lines in couplets, from the coming of Brutus and the giants of Albion through the British kings Lud, Bladud and Arthur and the Saxon and Danish kings to the Norman Conquest and the Plantagenets, closing with the death of Piers Gaveston under Edward II.

works.title: Chronicle of the Cid
works.author: Anonymous (Poem of the Cid)
works.blurb: Robert Southey’s English compilation of the medieval Spanish chronicles and ballads recounting the life and legend of Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar, El Cid.

works.title: On Duties (De Officiis)
works.subtitle: Three books to his son Marcus: moral goodness, expediency, and the conflict between the two
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Cicero's last major work, written in 44 BC for his son Marcus, then studying at Athens: a Stoic-inspired guide to what is morally right, what is expedient, and how to choose when the two seem to clash. Walter Miller's translation for the Loeb Classical Library, with the chapter numbers kept as plain leading numbers.

works.title: On the Orator (De Oratore)
works.subtitle: Three books on the making of the perfect orator, in dialogue between Crassus, Antonius and their friends
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Cicero's dialogue on eloquence, written in 55 BC and set in 91 BC at the Tusculan villa of the orator Lucius Crassus. Crassus and Marcus Antonius, with Scaevola, Catulus, Cotta and Sulpicius, discuss what the perfect orator must know: his learning, the invention and arrangement of his matter, the use of wit, and the style and delivery of his speech. J. S. Watson's translation, with the chapter numbers kept as plain leading numbers.

works.title: The Letters of Cicero, Volume I
works.subtitle: Letters from 68 to 52 BC, including the letters of the exile
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The first volume of Shuckburgh's chronological translation of Cicero's correspondence: letters to Atticus, to his brother Quintus and to friends, from his candidacy for the praetorship to the year before the civil war, including the letters written in exile.

sections.title: Letters in Exile and After (58–52 BC)

works.title: The Letters of Cicero, Volume II
works.subtitle: Letters from 51 to 49 BC, from Cicero's journey to Cilicia to the outbreak of the civil war
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The second volume of Shuckburgh's chronological translation of Cicero's correspondence, carrying on the numbering of the first: Cicero's journey to Cilicia and his governorship of the province, the letters of his return to Italy, and the correspondence of the opening months of the civil war between Caesar and Pompey, to Atticus, to Tiro, to Terentia, to Caelius, to Appius Claudius Pulcher and to many others.

sections.title: Letters of 50 BC: The Proconsulate and the Return
Letters of 49 BC: The Outbreak of the Civil War

works.title: The Letters of Cicero, Volume III
works.subtitle: Letters from 48 to 44 BC, from Pompey's camp in Epirus to the eve of Caesar's murder
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The third volume of Shuckburgh's chronological translation of Cicero's correspondence, carrying on the numbering of the second: the letters from Pompey's camp in Epirus and the long wait at Brundisium after Pharsalia, through the years of Caesar's dictatorship, Cicero's retirement to his villas, his divorce, the death of his daughter Tullia and his consolation in philosophical writing, down to the winter of 44 BC. Addressed to Atticus, Terentia, Tiro, Varro, Papirius Paetus, Servius Sulpicius, Cassius and many others.

sections.title: Letters of 48 BC: Epirus and Brundisium
Letters of 47 BC: Brundisium and the Return to Italy
Letters of 46 BC: Rome under Caesar
Letters of 45 BC: Tullia's Death and the Philosophical Works
Letters of 44 BC: The Months before the Ides of March

works.title: The Letters of Cicero, Volume IV
works.subtitle: Letters from the Ides of March 44 BC to July 43 BC, from Caesar's murder to the eve of the second triumvirate
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The fourth and last volume of Shuckburgh's chronological translation of Cicero's correspondence, carrying on the numbering of the third: the letters written after Caesar's assassination on the Ides of March 44 BC. They follow Cicero's retreat to his country villas, his growing quarrel with Antony and the Philippics, the war at Mutina, and the last anxious exchanges with Brutus, Cassius, Decimus Brutus, Plancus and Lepidus, down to the summer of 43 BC. Addressed to Atticus, Tiro, Cornificius and many others, with letters to Cicero from the generals and the conspirators themselves.

sections.title: Letters of 44 BC: After the Ides of March
Letters of 44 BC: The Break with Antony
Letters of 43 BC: The Philippics and Mutina
Letters of 43 BC: Decimus Brutus, Plancus, Lepidus and the Last Letters

works.title: On Friendship (Laelius de Amicitia)
works.subtitle: A dialogue on the nature and laws of friendship
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Cicero's dialogue on friendship, written in 44 BC and dedicated to Atticus. The aged Laelius, mourning his friend Scipio Africanus, tells his sons-in-law what friendship is, why it rests on virtue, and what its limits and duties are. Shuckburgh's translation, with the chapter numbers kept as plain leading numbers.

works.title: On Old Age (Cato Maior de Senectute)
works.subtitle: A dialogue in which Cato the Elder, in his eighty-fourth year, defends old age before Scipio and Laelius
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Cicero's late dialogue, addressed to Atticus, in which the aged Marcus Cato answers four charges against old age: that it withdraws us from active employments, weakens the body, deprives us of pleasures, and stands near to death.

works.title: The Orations of Cicero, Volume I
works.subtitle: For Quinctius, For Sextus Roscius, For Quintus Roscius, Against Caecilius, and the Verrine Orations
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The first volume of Yonge's Bohn translation of Cicero's speeches: the early pleadings for Quinctius, Sextus Roscius and the actor Quintus Roscius, the Divinatio against Caecilius, and the great prosecution of Verres, governor of Sicily, in the First Pleading and the five books of the Second.

works.title: The Orations of Cicero, Volume II
works.subtitle: For Tullius, Fonteius, Caecina, Cluentius, Rabirius, Murena, Sulla, Archias, Flaccus and Scaurus; the Manilian Law, the Agrarian Law, the Catilinarians, and the speeches after his return
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The second volume of Yonge's Bohn translation of Cicero's speeches: the pleadings of his consular years and after, among them the Manilian Law, the three speeches on the Agrarian Law, the four Catilinarians, and the defences of Murena, Archias, Flaccus and Sulla, with the two speeches after his return from exile.

sections.title: After his Return, to the Senate
After his Return, to the People

works.title: The Orations of Cicero, Volume III
works.subtitle: On his House, the Haruspices, Plancius, Sestius, Vatinius, Caelius, the Consular Provinces, Balbus, Piso, Milo, Postumus, Marcellus, Ligarius and King Deiotarus
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The third volume of Yonge's Bohn translation of Cicero's speeches: the orations of his years after exile, among them the plea for his house, the defences of Sestius, Caelius, Plancius and Milo, the invective against Piso, and the three speeches before Caesar for Marcellus, Ligarius and King Deiotarus.

sections.title: On the Answers of the Haruspices

works.title: The Orations of Cicero, Volume IV: The Philippics
works.subtitle: The fourteen speeches against Marcus Antonius
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The fourth volume of Yonge's Bohn translation of Cicero's speeches: the fourteen Philippics of 44 and 43 BC, in which Cicero, after Caesar's murder, attacks Marcus Antonius in the Senate and before the people and urges war to save the republic, the work that cost him his life.

works.title: The Civile Wars betweene the Two Houses of Lancaster and Yorke
works.subtitle: Eight books in ottava rima (1609 text)
works.author: Samuel Daniel
works.blurb: Samuel Daniel's historical epic of the Wars of the Roses, from the deposition of Richard II to the marriage of Henry VII and Elizabeth of York, in eight books of eight-line stanzas. The first four books appeared in 1595; the 1609 edition corrected and continued the poem. Each book opens with a short verse argument.

works.title: Clarel: A Poem and Pilgrimage in the Holy Land
works.author: Herman Melville
works.blurb: Melville’s long narrative poem of a pilgrimage in Palestine, the longest poem in American literature: a young divinity student, Clarel, joins a company of pilgrims who travel from Jerusalem through the Judean wilderness to Mar Saba, the Dead Sea and Bethlehem, debating faith and doubt as they go. It runs to some eighteen thousand lines, chiefly in rhymed octosyllabic couplets with lyric interludes, in four parts: Jerusalem (44 cantos), The Wilderness (39), Mar Saba (32) and Bethlehem (35, the last an Epilogue).

works.title: Cleanness
works.subtitle: Clannesse
works.author: Gawain Poet
works.blurb: A homily in some 1,800 alliterative lines on purity, in which God rejects those who come unclean to his presence. It tells the parable of the wedding feast and retells three Old Testament judgements: the Flood, the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, and Belshazzar's feast with the profaned vessels of the Temple.

works.title: Cligés
works.subtitle: Cligés
works.author: Chrétien de Troyes
works.blurb: A Greek prince of Arthur's line and his love for Fenice, framed as an answer to the Tristan story.

works.title: The Cloud-Messenger
works.subtitle: Meghaduta
works.author: Kalidasa
works.blurb: An exiled Yaksha begs a passing rain-cloud to carry a message of love across India to his wife in the Himalayas.

works.title: Dipsychus
works.subtitle: A verse drama in two parts
works.author: Arthur Hugh Clough
works.blurb: In Venice a young man, scrupulous and unsure of his faith, is shadowed by a cynical Spirit who urges him to enjoy the world, take a profession and make terms with the way things are. Dipsychus answers in blank verse, lyric and song, and at last yields in part, with reservations.

works.title: Colombe's Birthday: A Play
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A play in five acts. On her birthday Colombe, Duchess of Juliers and Cleves, learns that her right to the duchy is disputed by her cousin Prince Berthold; her courtiers desert her, and only the poor advocate Valence, who has come to plead for his town, stays true. The question is whether she will keep a crown or find a love.

works.title: The Columbiad
works.subtitle: A Poem in Ten Books
works.author: Joel Barlow
works.blurb: Barlow's patriotic epic on the American Republic: the imprisoned Columbus is shown, in vision, the history and future of the New World by the genius Hesper, in ten books of heroic couplets.

works.title: The Comedy of Errors
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Two sets of identical twins, the sons of the Syracusan merchant Egeon and their twin servants, separated by shipwreck in infancy, are drawn into the same day in Ephesus. Mistaken for one another by wives, friends, a goldsmith and a courtesan, they bring on beatings, arrests and a supposed madness, until the Abbess who shelters one of them proves to be Egeon's long-lost wife, and the family is reunited.

works.title: Comus
works.subtitle: A Mask Presented at Ludlow Castle
works.author: John Milton
works.blurb: A masque of chastity and temptation, performed at Ludlow Castle in 1634 — a Lady lost in the wood and the enchanter Comus.

works.title: Conary
works.author: Sir Samuel Ferguson
works.blurb: Ferguson's blank-verse retelling of the destruction of the hostel of Da-Derga and the death of King Conary Mor.

works.title: Confessio Amantis
works.subtitle: Tales of the Seven Deadly Sins
works.author: John Gower
works.blurb: A lover confesses to Venus's priest Genius, who works through the Seven Deadly Sins with a great gathering of exemplary tales — classical, biblical, and romance — in eight books of octosyllabic couplets.

works.title: Congal
works.subtitle: A Poem in Five Books
works.author: Sir Samuel Ferguson
works.blurb: Ferguson's five-book heroic poem of Congal Claen, King of Ulster, and the battle of Moira (Moyra) in the seventh century.

works.title: The Conquest of Canaan
works.subtitle: A Poem, in Eleven Books
works.author: Timothy Dwight
works.blurb: Timothy Dwight's biblical epic in eleven books, the first American epic poem, follows Joshua's campaigns against Ai, Gibeon and the Canaanite kings in heroic couplets, with the love of the young warrior Irad and the maiden Selima woven through the war and a prophetic vision of later history in Book X.

works.title: Constance
works.subtitle: or, The Portrait
works.author: Edward Bulwer Lytton
works.blurb: A narrative poem in five parts, in heroic couplets, of love and fate begun in a portrait and played out on an English country estate.

works.title: The Tragedy of Coriolanus
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Caius Martius, the proudest soldier in Rome, wins the name Coriolanus by taking the Volscian city of Corioles, but his contempt for the common people makes him unfit for the consulship he is pressed to seek. Tricked and banished by the tribunes Sicinius and Brutus, he goes over to his old enemy Tullus Aufidius and marches on Rome at the head of a Volscian army. Only the pleading of his mother Volumnia, his wife Virgilia and his son turns him back, and the peace he makes costs him his life at Aufidius's hands.

works.title: Count Basil
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: Joanna Baillie
works.blurb: Count Basil, a young general in the Emperour's service, is kept at Mantua by his love for Victoria, the Duke's daughter, while the Duke and his minister Gauriceio plot to turn his troops against him. Basil wins the mutinous soldiers back, but when the Imperial army wins the battle of Pavia without him he can bear the shame no longer and shoots himself in a cave, dying in his friend Rosinberg's arms. This is the tragedy of love in Baillie's Plays on the Passions.

works.title: The Countess Cathleen
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: In an Irish famine of old times, two demons disguised as merchants buy the starving peasants' souls for gold. The young Countess Cathleen sells her own soul to ransom theirs, while the poet Aleel, who loves her, looks on in anguish. Yeats's first long verse play moves from the peasants' hut to her great hall and back, and ends with a vision of the soul's pardon.

works.title: The Course of Time
works.subtitle: A Poem, in Ten Books
works.author: Robert Pollok
works.blurb: Robert Pollok's blank-verse epic in ten books, in which a bard of Paradise tells a newly arrived spirit the history of mankind from the Creation to the Last Judgement; published months before the young Scottish poet's death, it went through many editions.

works.title: The Courtship of Miles Standish
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: Longfellow's hexameter tale of the Plymouth Colony, in which Miles Standish sends the young John Alden to woo Priscilla Mullins for him, and she asks why he does not speak for himself.

sections.title: V. The Sailing of the May Flower
VII. The March of Miles Standish

works.title: The Curse of Kehama
works.author: Robert Southey
works.blurb: A Hindu mythological epic in twenty-four sections, in irregular rhymed stanzas: the Rajah Kehama curses the peasant Ladurlad, who is drawn into a pursuit that reaches the Swerga and the hell of Padalon.

works.title: The Cyclops
works.subtitle: A Satyric Drama
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Odysseus and his men, landing on Sicily, bargain with the old satyr Silenus for food and wine, only to fall into the hands of the one-eyed giant Polyphemus. Euripides' only surviving satyr play, the lone complete example of the genre, is rendered by Shelley in 1819 and was first printed after his death.

works.title: The Tragedie of Cymbeline
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Cymbeline, king of Britain, banishes his daughter Imogen's secret husband Posthumus Leonatus. Tricked by the Italian Iachimo into believing her unfaithful, Posthumus orders her death; she flees in boy's disguise to Wales, where she finds her two long-lost brothers, and the play's tangled threads of war with Rome, the Queen's poison and a divine vision resolve in reconciliation. It includes the songs 'Hark, hark! the lark' and 'Fear no more the heat o' the sun'.

works.title: Cynegetica
works.subtitle: The Chase
works.author: Oppian
works.blurb: A didactic poem in four books on hunting: the hunter, his horses and hounds, and the wild beasts of the chase, addressed to the emperor Caracalla.

works.title: Daniel
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: A verse paraphrase of the Book of Daniel: Nebuchadnezzar's pride and madness, the three youths in the fiery furnace, and Belshazzar's feast and the writing on the wall.

works.title: Daniel (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The Old English verse of the Junius Manuscript in the Krapp and Dobbie edition: a verse paraphrase of the Book of Daniel: Nebuchadnezzar's pride and madness, the three youths in the fiery furnace, and Belshazzar's feast and the writing on the wall.

works.title: Dante at Verona
works.author: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
works.blurb: Rossetti's narrative poem of Dante in exile at the court of Can Grande, torn between the Florence that cast him out and the Beatrice he lost.

works.title: The Economy of Vegetation
works.subtitle: The Botanic Garden, Part I
works.author: Erasmus Darwin
works.blurb: Darwin's four-canto didactic poem in heroic couplets, in which Nymphs of Fire, Gnomes, Nymphs of Water and Sylphs preside over the natural philosophy of heat, earth, water and air.

works.title: The Loves of the Plants
works.subtitle: The Botanic Garden, Part II
works.author: Erasmus Darwin
works.blurb: Darwin's four-canto poem in heroic couplets, in which the botanic Muse presents the Linnaean sexual system of plants as a comedy of courtships, marriages and rivalries among flowers.

works.title: The Daughters of Troy
works.subtitle: The Trojan Women
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Troy has fallen. In the Greek camp the captive women of the royal house wait to be shared out among the victors: Hecuba is given to Odysseus, the prophetess Kassandra to Agamemnon, and Andromache to Akhilleus' son. Their one remaining hope is taken from them when the Greeks decide to hurl Hector's little son from the walls, and the play ends as the city burns and the captives are driven down to the ships.

works.title: Davideis
works.subtitle: A Sacred Poem of the Troubles of David
works.author: Abraham Cowley
works.blurb: Cowley's unfinished biblical epic in rhymed couplets, telling of David's youth and his persecution by King Saul, in four books.

works.title: The Dawn in Britain
works.subtitle: In twenty-four books
works.author: Charles M. Doughty
works.blurb: Doughty's blank-verse epic of Britain from the first settlement to the Roman conquest, told in twenty-four books in a deliberately archaic, Spenserian English.

works.title: De Monfort
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: Joanna Baillie
works.blurb: De Monfort, a proud German nobleman, is eaten up by hatred of Rezenvelt, a rival whose easy fortune and ready praise he cannot forgive. His sister Jane tries to reconcile them, but a false report that Rezenvelt means to marry her drives him past endurance, and he murders his enemy in a wood near a convent. Taken by the monks, he dies of remorse in his sister's arms. This is the tragedy of hatred in Baillie's Plays on the Passions.

works.title: The Death of Wallenstein
works.author: Friedrich Schiller
works.blurb: Wallenstein, dismissed by the Emperor and urged by his officers toward revolt, hesitates between the stars and his own ambition and opens talks with the Swedes. Max Piccolomini chooses duty over love, and dies in battle; Thekla follows him in grief; at Egra Wallenstein is murdered by his own officers.

works.title: The Deformed Transformed
works.subtitle: A Drama
works.author: George Gordon, Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's unfinished drama, dated Pisa, 1822, and first published in 1824, of which only two parts and the opening chorus of a third were completed. The hunchback Arnold, scorned by his mother, accepts from a mysterious Stranger a new and beautiful body, and with the Stranger, who takes the form of his former shape, joins the army of the Constable Bourbon at the sack of Rome in 1527. Byron's advertisement names an old novel, The Three Brothers, and Goethe's Faust as sources.

works.title: Deirdre
works.subtitle: A Dramatic Poem
works.author: Sir Samuel Ferguson
works.blurb: Ferguson's blank-verse drama of the flight, return and death of Deirdre and the sons of Usnach, set between Glen Etive and the House of the Red Branch at Emania.

works.title: Deirdre
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: Fergus brings Naisi and Deirdre back to Ireland from exile, on the promise of King Conchubar's pardon. Waiting in a guest-house in a wood, while musicians sing and hint at treachery, the lovers learn that Conchubar means to take Deirdre for himself. The tragedy of the old Irish tale ends in a trap, a death, and a queen's last choice.

works.title: The Demon
works.author: Mikhail Lermontov
works.blurb: A fallen spirit loves the Georgian princess Tamara, kills her bridegroom, wins her with his speeches, and loses her soul to an angel at her death.

works.title: The Demon
works.author: Mikhail Lermontov
works.blurb: A fallen spirit loves the Georgian princess Tamara, kills her bridegroom, wins her with his speeches, and loses her soul to an angel at her death.

works.title: On the Chersonese (Or. VIII)
works.subtitle: Diopeithes and the Chersonese, 341 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes defends the general Diopeithes and urges Athens to resist Philip in the Chersonese.

works.title: On the Crown (Or. XVIII)
works.subtitle: The speech in reply to Aeschines, 330 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes' defence of his public career against Aeschines' attack on the proposal to crown him.

works.title: On the Embassy (Or. XIX)
works.subtitle: Against Aeschines on the false embassy, 343 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes' prosecution of Aeschines for misconduct as an ambassador to Philip.

works.title: The First Olynthiac (Or. I)
works.subtitle: Help for Olynthus, 349 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: The first of three speeches urging Athens to send help to Olynthus against Philip.

works.title: The First Philippic (Or. IV)
works.subtitle: The first speech against Philip of Macedon, 351 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes' first attack on Philip of Macedon, calling on the Athenians to raise a proper citizen force.

works.title: For the Megalopolitans (Or. XVI)
works.subtitle: Athens and the Arcadian city, c. 353 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes argues that Athens should support Megalopolis against Sparta while keeping Thebes weak.

works.author: Demosthenes

works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes urges the Athenians to help the Rhodian democrats against a Carian-backed oligarchy.
