works.subtitle: The Lord's teaching to the heathen by the Twelve Apostles
works.author: The Apostolic Fathers
works.blurb: An anonymous early Christian church manual, rediscovered in 1873, setting out the Two Ways, rules for baptism, fasting, the Eucharist and church order.

works.title: The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, Books I–V
works.subtitle: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of the Greek philosophers from Thales to Heraclides of Pontus
works.author: Diogenes Laertius
works.blurb: The chief ancient source for the lives and sayings of the Greek philosophers, from the Seven Wise Men through Socrates, Plato and the Academy to Aristotle and his school, in C. D. Yonge's English prose of 1853.

works.title: The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, Books VI–X
works.subtitle: Antisthenes and Diogenes through Epicurus
works.author: Diogenes Laertius
works.blurb: Laertius's lives of the Cynics, Stoics, Pythagoreans, Eleatics, Sceptics and Epicurus, with the three letters and the maxims of Epicurus, in C. D. Yonge's English prose of 1853.

works.title: The Divine Comedy
works.subtitle: La Divina Commedia
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Cary's blank-verse version of the Commedia, the standard English Dante of the nineteenth century, rendered canto by canto in Miltonic pentameter.

works.title: The Divine Comedy
works.subtitle: La Divina Commedia
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Dante's vision of the afterlife in a hundred cantos, from the dark wood through Inferno and Purgatorio to the Paradiso, in Longfellow's blank-verse tercets.

works.title: The Divine Comedy (Norton)
works.subtitle: Translated by Charles Eliot Norton
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: A literal, unrhymed prose version of the Commedia by the Harvard scholar Charles Eliot Norton, long valued by students for its fidelity to Dante's sense; each canto opens with a brief summary of its argument.

works.title: The Divine Comedy (Plumptre)
works.subtitle: Translated by E. H. Plumptre
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.translator: trans. E. H. Plumptre (1886–87; text of the Isbister edition, 1899)
works.blurb: The Commedia in English terza rima by Edward Hayes Plumptre, Dean of Wells, keeping Dante's three-line stanzas and line count; each cantica was published with extensive notes, which are omitted here.

works.title: Christus: A Mystery. Part I: The Divine Tragedy
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: The first part of Longfellow's trilogy Christus: A Mystery, a dramatic poem on the life of Christ. After an Introitus in which an Angel carries the prophet Habakkuk to Babylon, three Passovers follow the Gospel story from John the Baptist's preaching and the temptation in the wilderness through the miracles, the raising of Lazarus, the Last Supper, trial and Crucifixion, to the appearances after the Resurrection. The Epilogue gives the Apostles' Creed, spoken line by line by the Twelve. Part II is The Golden Legend.

works.subtitle: From the Quarto of 1604
works.author: Christopher Marlowe
works.blurb: Marlowe's tragedy of the scholar who, weary of the limits of learning, sells his soul to Lucifer for twenty-four years of power and pleasure, and faces the hour of reckoning.

works.title: Domesday Book
works.author: Edgar Lee Masters
works.blurb: A verse narrative in blank verse that opens with a coroner's inquest into the death of Elenor Murray, a nurse found dead by the Illinois River. Witness after witness is called, and each account lays bare the hidden lives of a Midwestern town and of America.

works.title: Don Juan
works.author: Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's unfinished comic epic in ottava rima follows a young Spaniard through seductions, shipwreck, war and the courts of Europe, mocking cant, politics and poetry itself along the way.

works.title: The Dream of Gerontius
works.author: John Henry Newman
works.blurb: Newman's dramatic poem of a dying man's passage through death and judgment, in seven parts: the prayers at the deathbed, the soul's journey with its guardian Angel, the Demons, the choirs of Angelicals, and the soul's entry into Purgatory.

works.title: The Dreaming of the Bones
works.subtitle: A play for dancers
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: In the aftermath of the Easter Rising of 1916, a young man fleeing from the Dublin fighting meets two strangers among the ruins of Corcomroe Abbey in County Clare. They are the ghosts of Dermot and Dervorgilla, whose adultery brought the Norman invasion to Ireland seven hundred years before, and they ask for his forgiveness.

works.title: The Duchess of Malfi
works.author: John Webster
works.blurb: The widowed Duchess of Malfi secretly marries her steward Antonio against the commands of her brothers, the violent Duke Ferdinand and the scheming Cardinal. Their spy Bosola uncovers the marriage, and the brothers imprison, torment and finally strangle her, along with her children and her maid. Bosola, sickened by the deed, turns on his masters, and the play ends in a bloodbath of revenge and ruin.

works.title: The Dynasts: Part First
works.subtitle: A Drama of the Napoleonic Wars
works.author: Thomas Hardy
works.blurb: Hardy's vast panorama of the Napoleonic Wars, from the threat of invasion in 1805 to Austerlitz. Above the earthly action the Spirits of the Years and the Pities watch the workings of the unconscious Immanent Will, in choruses of lyric verse.

works.title: The Earthly Paradise
works.subtitle: Parts II–IV: May to February
works.author: William Morris
works.blurb: Morris's frame story of wanderers who, seeking an earthly paradise, settle in a western city whose elders swap classical and medieval tales with them month by month. Part II holds the tales of Cupid and Psyche, Alcestis, the Son of Croesus, Pygmalion and Ogier the Dane. Parts III and IV add the autumn and winter tales: the Death of Paris, the Land East of the Sun and West of the Moon, Acontius and Cydippe, the Man who never Laughed Again, Rhodope, the Lovers of Gudrun, the Golden Apples, Aslaug, Bellerophon, the Ring given to Venus and the Hill of Venus.

sections.title: The Story of Cupid and Psyche
The Land East of the Sun and West of the Moon
The Story of Acontius and Cydippe
The Man who never Laughed Again

works.title: The Earthly Paradise
works.subtitle: Part I: The Prologue, March and April
works.author: William Morris
works.blurb: Morris's frame story of Norse wanderers who sail in search of the earthly paradise and end their days in a western city whose elders trade tales with them month by month. Part I holds the Apology (‘the idle singer of an empty day’), the Prologue in which the wanderers tell their own story, and the tales of March and April: Atalanta's Race, the Man Born to be King, the Doom of King Acrisius and the Proud King.

sections.title: The Man Born to be King

works.title: Ecclesiastes
works.subtitle: Authorized Version of Ecclesiastes.
works.author: The Bible (Authorized King James Version)
works.blurb: The reflections of the Preacher on vanity, time and the limits of human wisdom.

works.title: The Troublesome Reign and Lamentable Death of Edward the Second
works.author: Christopher Marlowe
works.blurb: Edward II, newly king, recalls his favourite Gaveston from exile and showers him with titles, driving the barons under the younger Mortimer into open revolt. After Gaveston is killed and the king turns to the Spensers, Queen Isabella and Mortimer invade, depose Edward and have him murdered in Berkeley Castle. His son, the young Edward III, then brings Mortimer to the block.

works.title: Egyptian Tales, First Series
works.subtitle: Translated from the Papyri, IVth to XIIth Dynasty
works.author: Ancient Egyptian (anonymous)
works.blurb: Four of the oldest stories in the world: the magicians at the court of Khufu, the eloquent peasant, the shipwrecked sailor and the exile of Sanehat, translated from the papyri.

works.title: Egyptian Tales, Second Series
works.subtitle: Translated from the Papyri, XVIIIth to XIXth Dynasty
works.author: Ancient Egyptian (anonymous)
works.blurb: Four tales from the New Kingdom papyri: the stratagem by which Tahutia took Joppa, the prince doomed to crocodile, serpent or dog, the quarrel of the brothers Anpu and Bata, and Setna's theft of the magic book of Thoth.

works.title: Electra
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Orestes returns to Mycenae in disguise, sent by Apollo to avenge Agamemnon. Electra, who has mourned her murdered father for years, believes her brother dead until he reveals himself; together they kill their mother Clytemnestra and then her lover Aegisthus.

works.title: Electra
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Years after Agamemnon's murder, his daughter Electra still keeps vigil at the palace gates of Mycenae, scorned by her mother Clytaemnestra and her mother's lover Aegisthus. Her brother Orestes returns in secret with a false tale of his own death, and the siblings' recognition scene turns grief into revenge. Jebb's plain English prose carries the play's cold fury and its choral laments.

works.title: Electra
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: In a poor peasant's cottage on the borders of Argos, Agamemnon's daughter Electra waits in squalor for her exiled brother Orestes to return and avenge their father on Klytemnestra and Aegisthus. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy of recognition and vengeance in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Elene
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: Cynewulf's retelling of the legend of St. Helena, mother of the Emperor Constantine, and her journey to Jerusalem in search of the True Cross, opening with Constantine's vision of the Cross before his battle at the Milvian Bridge.

works.title: Elene (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: Cynewulf's retelling of the legend of St. Helena and her journey to Jerusalem in search of the True Cross, in the original Old English.

works.title: Emare
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: Emare, daughter of the emperor Artyus, wears a marvellous robe embroidered with famous lovers; when her father conceives a sinful passion for her she is set adrift in a boat and comes ashore in Galys, where the king marries her. His mother's lies drive Emare and her child into exile at sea again, until a penitent pilgrimage to Rome reunites the whole family.

works.title: The Emigrants
works.subtitle: A Poem in Two Books
works.author: Charlotte Smith
works.blurb: Charlotte Smith's blank-verse meditation on the French Revolution and the refugee clergy and nobility who fled to the Sussex coast, set against her own grief and the English countryside.

works.title: The Fragments of Empedocles
works.subtitle: Translated into English verse
works.author: Empedocles
works.blurb: The surviving fragments of Empedocles' two hexameter poems, On Nature and The Purifications, in William Ellery Leonard's English verse: the four roots, Love and Strife, the cycles of the cosmos, and the wandering of the soul.

sections.title: Last Echoes of a Song Half Lost

works.title: Empedocles on Etna
works.subtitle: A Dramatic Poem
works.author: Matthew Arnold
works.blurb: On the slopes of Mount Etna, the young harp-player Callicles and the physician Pausanias attend the philosopher Empedocles, who is exiled, weary of men and of his own restless thought. Callicles sings of the gods and of Chiron's teaching of Akhilleus, Pausanias hopes to cure his friend, and Empedocles on the summit, in a long meditation on mind, desire and the unity of things, leaps into the crater, while Callicles' song rises from below.

works.title: Endymion
works.subtitle: A Poetic Romance
works.author: John Keats
works.blurb: Keats's four-book retelling of the myth of the shepherd prince Endymion, loved by the moon goddess and wandering the earth, sea and underworld in search of her.

works.title: The Seven Tablets of Creation
works.subtitle: Enuma Elish
works.author: Anonymous Babylonian Poets
works.blurb: The Babylonian epic of creation, in which the god Marduk slays the sea-goddess Tiamat, fashions the world from her body, and receives his fifty names.

works.title: The Epic of Hades
works.subtitle: In Three Books
works.author: Sir Lewis Morris
works.blurb: A Victorian dream-vision in three books: the poet walks through Tartarus, Hades and Olympus, hearing the shades of Greek myth tell their own stories and the gods reveal what they stand for.

works.title: The Epic Songs of Russia
works.subtitle: The Byliny of the Kiev and Novgorod Cycles
works.author: Anonymous (Russian Byliny)
works.blurb: The great heroic songs of the Russian north: Ilya of Murom and the Nightingale the Robber, Dobrynya the Dragon-slayer, Sadko beneath the sea, and the champions who defend Prince Vladimir's Kiev.

works.title: The Discourses of Epictetus
works.subtitle: with the Encheiridion and Fragments
works.author: Epictetus
works.blurb: The lectures of the Stoic teacher Epictetus as recorded by his pupil Arrian, with the Encheiridion, or Manual, and the surviving fragments, in George Long’s translation.

works.title: The Epigoniad
works.subtitle: A Poem in Nine Books
works.author: William Wilkie
works.blurb: An epic in nine books on the war of the Epigoni, the sons of the Seven, against Thebes, in heroic couplets modelled on the Iliad.

works.title: Erec and Enide
works.subtitle: Erec et Enide
works.author: Chrétien de Troyes
works.blurb: The first Arthurian romance in French verse, telling how Erec wins Enide and then must prove himself again.

works.title: Erechtheus
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: Algernon Charles Swinburne
works.blurb: A tragedy on the Greek model. Athens is besieged by Eumolpus and his Thracians, and an oracle demands that King Erechtheus sacrifice one of his daughters to save the city. Swinburne's choruses sing of Athens, the sea and the sun, and the play ends with Athena's promise of the city's glory.

works.title: The Erle of Tolous
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A tail-rhyme Breton lay of about 1,220 lines: Barnard, earl of Tolous, defeats the emperor Dyaclysyon, wins a sight of the empress Beulybon through the knight Trylabas, and later, disguised as a monk, takes up her cause when two knights falsely accuse her. After the emperor's death he becomes emperor and marries her.

works.title: Eros and Psyche
works.subtitle: A narrative poem in twelve measures
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's narrative poem of Psyche and Eros, drawn from the story in Apuleius and told in seven-line stanzas across the twelve months of the year, from Psyche's earthly parentage in the spring to her reception into heaven in the winter.

works.title: An Essay on Man
works.subtitle: In Four Epistles to Henry St John, Lord Bolingbroke
works.author: Alexander Pope
works.blurb: Pope’s attempt, in polished couplets, to ‘vindicate the ways of God to Man’ — four epistles on man’s place in the universe, himself, society, and happiness.

works.title: Eugene Onéguine
works.subtitle: A Romance of Russian Life in Verse
works.author: Alexander Pushkin
works.blurb: Pushkin's verse novel of the bored St Petersburg dandy Onegin, the provincial girl Tatiana who loves him, and the duel that kills his friend Lensky.

works.title: Europe: A Prophecy
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Enitharmon's eighteen-hundred-year sleep, the reign of Urizen's law over Europe, and the coming of the revolutionary fire of Orc.

works.title: Europe
works.subtitle: Lines on the War
works.author: Reginald Heber
works.blurb: Heber's verses of 1809 on the war against Napoleon, opening in a grove at Dresden and ending in hope for Spain.

works.title: Evangeline
works.subtitle: A Tale of Acadie
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A story of a young Acadian woman who is separated from her promised husband when their people are driven from their homes, and who spends her whole life searching for him.

works.title: Everyman
works.subtitle: The Summoning of Everyman
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: God, displeased that mankind has forgotten him in worldly prosperity, sends Death to summon Everyman to a reckoning. Abandoned in turn by Fellowship, Kindred and Goods, and later by Beauty, Strength, Discretion and Five-Wits, Everyman is accompanied to the grave only by Good-Deeds. The best-known English morality play, in rhyming verse of the late fifteenth century.

works.title: The Pontic Epistles
works.subtitle: Ovid's Letters from the Black Sea, Books I–IV, prose translation by Henry T. Riley
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid's four books of verse epistles from exile, each addressed by name to a friend or patron in Rome, pleading for help and describing life among the Getae, in Riley's prose.

works.title: Exodus
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: A dense, martial retelling of the Israelites' flight from Egypt and crossing of the Red Sea, cast largely in the diction of Old English heroic poetry.

works.title: Exodus (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The Old English verse of the Junius Manuscript in the Krapp and Dobbie edition: a dense, martial retelling of the Israelites' flight from Egypt and crossing of the Red Sea, cast largely in the diction of Old English heroic poetry.

works.title: The Faerie Queene
works.subtitle: Books I–VI, with the Mutabilitie Cantos
works.author: Edmund Spenser
works.blurb: Spenser's vast allegorical epic of knights, virtues, and the Faerie court — six completed Books (Holinesse, Temperaunce, Chastitie, Friendship, Iustice, Courtesie) plus the fragmentary Mutabilitie Cantos, in the original 1590s spelling.

works.title: The Fairy Godmother-in-Law
works.author: Oliver Herford
works.blurb: A comic sequel to Cinderella, in which the Prince and Princess are visited by her fairy godmother, who proves an even more formidable relation than the average mother-in-law.

works.title: The Fall of Robespierre
works.subtitle: An Historic Drama
works.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
works.blurb: A three-act historical drama on the overthrow of Robespierre in July 1794, published at Cambridge in 1794 as a pamphlet under Coleridge's name. In the first act Tallien, Legendre and Barrere plot against the dictator; in the second he is denounced in the Convention and led off under arrest; the third follows the aftermath of his rescue by Henriot. The first act is Coleridge's; the second and third are Southey's.

works.title: The Fall of Troy
works.subtitle: Posthomerica
works.author: Quintus Smyrnaeus
works.blurb: Quintus Smyrnaeus continues the Iliad from the funeral of Hector through the deaths of Akhilleus, Paris and the Amazon queen Penthesileia, the wooden horse and the sack of Troy, to the Greeks' storm-wrecked voyage home.

works.title: The Farmer's Boy
works.subtitle: A Rural Poem
works.author: Robert Bloomfield
works.blurb: A rural poem in four seasons, following the labours and pleasures of a farm boy through the year.

works.title: The Fasti
works.subtitle: Ovid's Roman Calendar, Books I–VI, prose translation by Henry T. Riley
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid's poem on the Roman festival calendar, here in Riley's prose: the six surviving books, January to June, with the rites, myths and star-risings of each month.

works.title: The Fates of the Apostles
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: A brief martyrology recounting, in turn, the missionary travels and deaths of Christ's twelve apostles, closing the Vercelli Book poem with Cynewulf's runic signature.

works.title: The Fates of the Apostles (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: A brief martyrology recounting the missionary travels and deaths of Christ's twelve apostles, closing with Cynewulf's runic signature, in the original Old English.

works.title: Faust: The First Part
works.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
works.blurb: Dr. Heinrich Faust, a scholar sick of the limits of human knowledge, is wagered over in Heaven and then bargains his soul to the devil Mephistopheles in return for a moment of fulfilment. Mephistopheles draws him through the tavern, the witches' kitchen and a Walpurgis-Night revel, and into a love affair with the young Margaret, whose mother, brother and child are destroyed in its wake. Margaret, imprisoned for infanticide and awaiting execution, refuses Faust's offer of escape and gives herself up to God; a voice from above declares her saved.

sections.title: Walpurgis-Night's Dream (Oberon and Titania's Golden Wedding)

works.title: Faust: The Second Part
works.subtitle: Translated in the original metres by Bayard Taylor
works.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
works.blurb: The Second Part of Goethe's Faust in Bayard Taylor's translation in the original metres: Faust serves the Emperor's court, follows Helen of Troy through the Classical Walpurgis-Night to a marriage that ends with the death of their son Euphorion, wins land from the sea, and dies at the hour his own labour is complete, as the angels carry off what is immortal in him.

works.title: The Feast of Bacchus
works.subtitle: A Comedy in the Latin manner, partly translated from Terence
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's comedy in the Latin manner, privately printed at Oxford in 1889 and published in 1894, partly translated from Terence. The action takes place in a single day in a suburb of Athens, on the feast of Bacchus, among the households of Menedemus and Chremes.

works.title: Fifine at the Fair
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: Don Juan's long, teasing defence of inconstancy to his wife Elvire at a Breton fair, framed by the Prologue "Amphibian" and the Epilogue "The Householder".

works.title: Fingal: An Ancient Epic Poem
works.subtitle: In Six Books
works.author: James Macpherson
works.blurb: Ossian's epic of Fingal's rescue of Ireland from Swaran, king of Lochlin, in measured prose.

works.title: The Fleece
works.subtitle: A Poem in Four Books
works.author: John Dyer
works.blurb: Dyer's didactic poem in four books of blank verse on the English wool trade, from the care of sheep and the shearing to the loom, the markets and the ships that carry cloth to the world.

works.title: Floris and Blauncheflur
works.subtitle: Middle English text of the Trentham manuscript, ed. J. Lumby (1866), re-ed. G. H. McKnight (1901)
works.author: Anonymous
works.blurb: A Middle English romance of two children, the Christian Blauncheflur and the king's son Floris, who are raised together and then parted when his father sells her to merchants; Floris sets out for Babylon and wins her back from the Emir's tower.

works.title: The Foray of Queen Meave
works.subtitle: Five Fragments of an Ancient Irish Epic (The Táin Bó Cuailgne)
works.author: Aubrey de Vere
works.blurb: De Vere’s blank-verse retelling, in five fragments with a prologue, of the Táin Bó Cuailgne: Queen Meave of Connacht invades Ulster for the Brown Bull, and the young Cuchullain holds the ford alone.

sections.title: Fragment I: The Cause of the Great War
Fragment II: The Deeds of Cuchullain
Fragment III: The Combat at the Ford
Fragment IV: The Invasion of Uladh

works.title: The Forest Sanctuary
works.author: Felicia Hemans
works.blurb: A Spanish Protestant, fleeing religious persecution in the sixteenth century, tells his story from a North American forest where he has taken refuge with his child.

works.title: Fragments of Psalms (Old English)
works.subtitle: Metrical psalm passages from the Benedictine Office: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: Short passages of Old English verse translation from twenty-five psalms, found in the Benedictine Office.

works.title: The French Revolution
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Blake's unfinished poem on the fall of the Bastille; only the first of its seven projected books was printed, in 1791.

works.title: Friar Bacon and Friar Bungay
works.subtitle: The Honourable History of Friar Bacon and Friar Bungay
works.author: Robert Greene
works.blurb: Prince Edward, hunting near Fressingfield, falls in love with Margaret, the Keeper's daughter, and sends Lacy, Earl of Lincoln, to woo her on his behalf; Lacy falls for her himself. Meanwhile Friar Bacon of Oxford, a scholar of magic, builds a brazen head to wall England in brass, defeats the German conjurer Vandermast in a contest of spirits, and shows Edward the distant courtship in a glass. The play ends with Edward's renunciation of Margaret, her marriage to Lacy, and Bacon's prophecy at a royal wedding.

works.title: Fridthjof's Saga
works.subtitle: A Norse Romance
works.author: Esaias Tegnér
works.translator: trans. Thomas A. E. Holcomb and Martha A. Lyon Holcomb (1876)
works.blurb: Tegnér's Swedish romantic epic in twenty-four cantos, drawn from an Icelandic saga: the farmer's son Fridthjof loves Ingeborg, daughter of King Bele, and is parted from her by her brothers, outlawed, and finally reconciled, here in English verse by the Holcombs.

works.subtitle: Frithiof's Saga
works.author: Esaias Tegnér
works.blurb: Tegnér's Swedish romantic epic in twenty-four cantos, drawn from an Icelandic saga: the farmer's son Frithiof loves Ingeborg, daughter of King Bele, and is parted from her by her brothers, outlawed, and finally reconciled, here in the English verse of Captain Spalding, a second translation, in the original measures, of 1872.

works.title: The Furies
works.subtitle: The Oresteia
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: Pursued by the Furies of his murdered mother, Orestes flees to Apollo's shrine at Delphi and then to Athens. Athena sets up a jury of Athenian citizens to try him; the votes tie, and her own vote acquits him. She persuades the angry Furies to stay in Athens as the kindly Eumenides, honoured guardians of the city.

works.title: Gammer Gurton's Needle
works.author: William Stevenson (attributed)
works.blurb: Gammer Gurton loses the needle with which she was mending her servant Hodge's breeches, and the mischievous vagabond Diccon the Bedlam persuades her that her neighbour Dame Chat has stolen it. Accusations, a brawl and the arrival of the curate, Doctor Rat, and the bailiff follow, until Hodge, struck by Diccon, finds the needle sticking in his own breeches. One of the earliest English comedies, it opens Act II with the drinking song 'Back and side go bare, go bare'.

works.title: The Dispensary
works.subtitle: A Poem in Six Cantos
works.author: Sir Samuel Garth
works.blurb: A mock-heroic satire on the apothecaries who opposed the College of Physicians' free dispensary for the poor, told as an epic battle of drugs, doctors and allegorical spirits. Text of the first edition (London, 1699), with its original spelling.

works.title: The Gathas of Zarathustra
works.subtitle: Yasna 28–34, 43–51 and 53, from the Zend-Avesta, Part III
works.author: The Avesta
works.blurb: The seventeen hymns of the Gathas, the oldest layer of the Avesta and traditionally ascribed to Zarathustra himself, in L. H. Mills’s prose translation of 1887.

works.title: Gebir
works.author: Walter Savage Landor
works.blurb: Landor's first major poem, a blank-verse epic in seven books. Gebir, prince of Spain, invades Egypt and falls in love with its young queen Charoba, while his brother Tamar loves her sister Dalica. Magic, an underworld descent and a fatal gift of poisoned robes follow.

works.title: Genesis
works.subtitle: Genesis A and Genesis B
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: A verse paraphrase of Genesis running from the Creation and the fall of the rebel angels through Abraham and the near-sacrifice of Isaac, opening the Junius Manuscript.

works.title: The Story of Genesis and Exodus
works.subtitle: Middle English biblical verse paraphrase, ed. Richard Morris (EETS, 1865)
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: An East Midland verse paraphrase of about 4,160 short couplet lines, written about 1250, that retells the Book of Genesis and the first part of Exodus from the Creation and the Fall of Lucifer to the death of Moses, with much borrowed legend and commentary.

sections.title: The Fall of Lucifer and of Man
The Exodus and the Red Sea
Balaam and the Death of Moses

works.title: Genesis (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The Old English verse of the Junius Manuscript in the Krapp and Dobbie edition: a verse paraphrase of Genesis running from the Creation and the fall of the rebel angels through Abraham and the near-sacrifice of Isaac, opening the Junius Manuscript.

works.title: The Gentle Shepherd: A Pastoral Comedy
works.author: Allan Ramsay
works.blurb: Set in a Lowland village in the years after the Restoration, Ramsay's pastoral follows Patie, a shepherd who loves Peggy, a foundling he takes for a poor girl, while his friend Roger woos Jenny and the dull Bauldy plots against them. Sir William Worthy, the exiled laird, returns in disguise and the secret of Peggy's birth comes out, so that the lovers may marry. The play is built of Scots dialogue in couplets, with twenty-one songs set to old tunes.

works.title: The Georgics
works.subtitle: Dryden's heroic-couplet translation
works.author: Virgil
works.blurb: Virgil's Latin poem in four books on farming and country life, in Dryden's heroic couplets: tillage and the weather, the vine and olive, cattle and horses, and the keeping of bees.

works.title: The Georgics
works.subtitle: Fairclough's prose translation
works.author: Virgil
works.blurb: Virgil's Latin poem in four books on farming and country life, in H. Rushton Fairclough's plain prose: tillage and the weather, the vine and olive, cattle and horses, and the keeping of bees.

works.title: The Georgics
works.subtitle: Prose translation
works.author: Virgil
works.translator: trans. J. W. Mackail (1889; Longmans reprint 1910)
works.blurb: Virgil's Latin poem in four books on farming and country life, in J. W. Mackail's prose: the work of the fields and the weather, trees and vines, cattle and horses, and the keeping of bees.

works.title: The Georgics
works.subtitle: Blank-verse translation
works.author: Virgil
works.blurb: Virgil's Latin poem in four books on farming and country life: the tilling of fields, the vine and olive, the rearing of cattle, and the keeping of bees.

works.title: Germany: A Winter Tale
works.subtitle: Deutschland. Ein Wintermärchen
works.author: Heinrich Heine
works.blurb: Heine's satirical verse journey home from exile in Paris to Hamburg in twenty-seven cantos, mocking Prussian authority and German nationalism.

works.title: The Ghost
works.author: Charles Churchill
works.blurb: Churchill's rambling octosyllabic satire in four books, begun as an attack on the Cock Lane ghost hoax and growing into a gallery of attacks on Johnson, Mansfield and Warburton.

works.title: Gil Perez, the Gallician
works.author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
works.blurb: FitzGerald's free version of Calderón's play on a notorious Spanish robber, whose name he changes to Gil. A farmer of Galicia, Gil falls out with the law and takes to the hills; the play follows him through Portugal and Andalusia to a confrontation with the Judge and a final pardon.

works.title: An Old Babylonian Version of the Gilgamesh Epic
works.subtitle: The Pennsylvania and Yale Tablets
works.author: Anonymous Babylonian Poets
works.translator: trans. Morris Jastrow Jr. and Albert T. Clay (1920)
works.blurb: Gilgamesh's dreams of Enkidu, the wild man's taming and their wrestling meeting in Erech, and the pair's plan to go against the monster Humbaba in the cedar forest.

works.title: The Epic of Gilgamish
works.subtitle: Verse translation from the Assyrian and Babylonian tablets
works.author: Anonymous Babylonian Poets
works.blurb: The Babylonian epic of Gilgamish, king of Erech, and his friend Enkidu, who together slay the Ogre Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven, until Enkidu's death sends the hero in vain search of everlasting life.

works.author: Jayadeva
works.blurb: Jayadeva's twelfth-century Sanskrit song cycle of Krishna and Radha, in Sir Edwin Arnold's English verse: a hymn to Vishnu and eleven sargas of longing, quarrel and union.

works.title: The Glory of the Nightingales
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Edwin Arlington Robinson
works.blurb: Blank-verse narrative in six parts: Malory, bent on revenge, travels from Sharon to the seaside mansion of his old rival Nightingale, with the memory of Agatha, whom both loved, driving the story.

works.title: The Athenaid
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Richard Glover
works.blurb: Glover's posthumous blank-verse epic in thirty books, a sequel to Leonidas that sets Athens against the Persian Empire of Xerxes.

works.title: Leonidas
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Richard Glover
works.blurb: Glover's blank-verse epic of Leonidas and the three hundred at Thermopylae, in nine books, a patriotic favourite of its day.

works.title: The Gods of the North
works.subtitle: An Epic Poem
works.author: Adam Oehlenschläger
works.blurb: Oehlenschläger's cycle of thirty cantos retelling the Norse myths, chiefly the adventures of Thor and the mischief of Lok, among the Aesir and the giants, in Frye's English rhymed and blank verse.

works.title: The Golden Legend
works.subtitle: Christus: A Mystery, Part II
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A dramatic poem set in medieval Germany, drawn from Hartmann von Aue's tale of Poor Henry. Prince Henry of Hoheneck, wasting with a mysterious sickness, is told that only a maiden's willing death can cure him. Elsie, a peasant girl, offers hers, and the two travel through Strasburg, the Black Forest convent of Hirschau, the Alps and Italy to the medical school at Salerno, where Henry prevents the sacrifice. Lucifer in disguise tempts the travellers throughout, and a Miracle Play of the Nativity is performed inside the Strasburg scenes. Longfellow made the poem the second part of his trilogy Christus: A Mystery.

works.subtitle: An Heroick Poem
works.author: Sir William Davenant
works.blurb: Davenant’s unfinished heroic poem in decasyllabic quatrains — three books and twenty cantos of love, war and statecraft among the Lombards.

works.title: The Greater Testament
works.subtitle: Le Testament, translated by John Payne
works.author: François Villon
works.blurb: Begun about 1461, after Villon's release from prison at Meung, this long mock will mingles confession, satire and lament, and holds the ballads on which his fame mostly rests, among them the Ballad of Old-Time Ladies.

works.title: The Green Helmet
works.subtitle: An Heroic Farce
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: Cuchulain returns from Scotland to find Laegaire and Conall refusing to honour his claim as the champion, while a Red Man from the sea comes to collect an old debt: a beheading game agreed a year before. In rhymed fourteeners, Yeats turns the Irish tale of Bricriu's Feast into a comic-heroic farce, ending in a gesture of reckless generosity.

works.title: Greenfield Hill
works.subtitle: A Poem, in Seven Parts
works.author: Timothy Dwight
works.blurb: Dwight's seven-part descriptive and patriotic poem on the Connecticut village where he was minister, from its rural prospect and the burning of Fairfield to a vision of America's future.

works.blurb: The Middle High German epic of Kudrun, the Hegeling princess abducted by Hartmut and held captive for thirteen years until her kin come to win her back, in thirty-two tales of four-line stanzas, rendered into English verse by Mary Pickering Nichols.

works.title: Guidone and Lucia
works.author: Walter Savage Landor
works.blurb: A narrative poem in rhymed couplets, set among the Guelph and Ghibelline feuds of Italy, of the lovers Guidone and Lucia.

works.title: Gunlaug
works.author: Walter Savage Landor
works.blurb: A narrative poem in rhymed couplets on the Icelandic poet Gunlaug, his love for Helga, and his quarrel and duel with his friend Rafen.

works.title: Guthlac
works.subtitle: Guthlac A and Guthlac B
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The life of St. Guthlac of Crowland, a former warrior turned hermit who does battle with demons in the Lincolnshire fens (Guthlac A), and an account, closely based on Felix's Latin Life, of his final illness and death (Guthlac B).

works.title: Guthlac (Old English)
works.subtitle: Guthlac A and Guthlac B: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The Old English verse of the life of St. Guthlac of Crowland, a former warrior turned hermit who does battle with demons in the Lincolnshire fens (Guthlac A), and an account of his final illness and death (Guthlac B).

works.title: Halieutica
works.subtitle: On Fishing
works.author: Oppian
works.blurb: A didactic poem in five books on the natures, habits and capture of sea creatures, addressed to the emperors Marcus Aurelius and Commodus.

works.title: The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of Denmark
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Prince Hamlet, summoned home to Elsinore by his father's death, is told by the Ghost that Claudius, now king and married to Hamlet's mother, murdered him. Feigning madness and staging a play to catch the king's conscience, Hamlet delays his revenge while the court around him unravels: Polonius is killed, Ophelia is driven to drowning, and Laertes returns for vengeance. The final duel leaves almost the whole court dead and the throne to Fortinbras of Norway.

works.title: The Code of Hammurabi
works.subtitle: The Oldest Code of Laws in the World
works.author: Hammurabi
works.blurb: The best-known law code of ancient Mesopotamia, issued by the king of Babylon c. 1750 BC: laws on theft, land, trade, marriage, injury and the hire of labour.

works.title: Harold: A Drama
works.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
works.blurb: Tennyson's verse drama of the last Saxon king. Harold, Earl of Wessex, is shipwrecked on the Norman coast and forced to swear an oath to Duke William, a vow that haunts him when the dying Edward the Confessor names him heir. Crowned king, he defeats his brother Tostig and the Norwegians at Stamford Bridge, then marches south to meet the Normans at Hastings, where he falls and Edith finds his body on the field of the dead.

works.title: Harold the Dauntless
works.subtitle: A Poem in Six Cantos
works.author: Sir Walter Scott
works.blurb: A verse romance of the Danish settlement of Northumbria: the fierce heathen Harold, son of Count Witikind, is drawn through blood, magic and a warning from the grave toward repentance and the love of the Danish maid Eivir.

works.title: The Lay of Havelok the Dane
works.subtitle: Middle English verse romance, ed. W. W. Skeat (EETS, 1868)
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: An English verse romance of about 3,000 lines in which Havelok, the dispossessed son of a Danish king, is raised by a fisherman, marries the English princess Goldeborw, and wins back both kingdoms.

works.title: Heaven and Earth
works.subtitle: A Mystery
works.author: George Gordon, Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's biblical drama on the eve of the Flood, begun at Ravenna in October 1821 and first published in The Liberal in 1823. Anah and Aholibamah, descendants of Cain, are loved by the angels Samiasa and Azaziel, while the patriarch Noah's son Japhet loves Anah. As the waters rise, the angels carry the two women away and Japhet is left on a rock as the Ark floats towards him. Only the first part of the work was written.

works.title: Hecuba
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: After the fall of Troy, the captive queen Hecuba loses her daughter Polyxena to sacrifice at the tomb of Akhilleus, then finds the body of her youngest son Polydorus, murdered for his gold by the Thracian king who was sheltering him. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy of grief turned to vengeance in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Helen of Troy
works.author: Andrew Lang
works.blurb: Lang's retelling of the story of Helen in six books of rhyme royal, from the coming of Paris to Sparta to the sack of Troy and the return of Helen to Menelaus, with Helen conceived as the unwilling victim of the gods.

sections.title: Book I: The Coming of Paris
Book II: The Spell of Aphrodite
Book III: The Flight of Helen
Book IV: The Death of Corythus
Book VI: The Sack of Troy. The Return of Helen

works.title: Helen
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Euripides follows the Recantation of Stesichorus: the Helen who went to Troy was only a phantom of cloud, while the true Helen waited in Egypt, chaste, at the tomb of King Proteus. When shipwrecked Menelaus arrives, husband and wife must trick the king who wishes to marry her. Arthur Way renders this romantic tragedy in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: The Ethiopics; or, Adventures of Theagenes and Chariclea
works.subtitle: Smith translation, 1855
works.author: Heliodorus of Emesa
works.blurb: The Greek romance of the lovers Theagenes and Chariclea, parted by pirates, priests and kings from Delphi to Egypt and Ethiopia: the best-known ancient novel, in Rowland Smith's English prose of 1855.

works.title: Hellas
works.subtitle: A Lyrical Drama
works.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
works.blurb: Shelley's lyrical drama of the Greek War of Independence, set in the Sultan's Constantinople, closing with the chorus 'The world's great age begins anew'.

works.title: The Henriade
works.subtitle: An epic poem in ten cantos
works.author: Voltaire
works.translator: trans. Tobias Smollett, Thomas Francklin and others (1762)
works.blurb: Voltaire's epic of Henri IV and the French Wars of Religion, from the St Bartholomew massacre to the siege and surrender of Paris.

works.title: The First Part of King Henry the Fourth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: The Percy family, who helped Henry IV to the throne, rise against him, led by the fiery Hotspur. Meanwhile the king's son, Prince Hal, wastes his days in Eastcheap taverns with the fat knight Sir John Falstaff and his thieving companions. Hal at last turns to honour, takes up arms for his father, and kills Hotspur at the battle of Shrewsbury.

works.title: The Second Part of King Henry the Fourth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: The Archbishop of York and his allies rise in a second rebellion, and Prince John of Lancaster crushes it at Gaultree Forest by a false promise of peace and a prompt arrest. Falstaff, sent recruiting into Gloucestershire, trades old memories with Justice Shallow and takes bribes from the men he chooses to spare. Meanwhile the dying king, troubled by a crown that has cost him sleep, makes his peace with Prince Hal, who on his accession rejects Falstaff in the street.

works.title: Henry the Leper (Der Arme Heinrich)
works.subtitle: A Swabian Miracle-Rhyme
works.author: Hartmann von Aue
works.blurb: Hartmann's tale of a nobleman struck with leprosy and the peasant girl who offers her life for his cure, in Rossetti's rhymed paraphrase.

works.title: The Life of King Henry the Fifth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Henry V presses his claim to the throne of France, exposes the traitors Cambridge, Scroop and Grey at Southampton, takes Harfleur, and wins against heavy odds at Agincourt, with the Chorus asking the audience to supply what the stage cannot show. The war ends in the comic, halting wooing of Katherine of France.

works.title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: The play opens at the funeral of Henry V, as the English hold France only by the valour of Talbot, whom Joan la Pucelle and the French confront at Orleans and beyond. In the Temple Garden the red and white roses are plucked, and the quarrel of York and Lancaster begins. Suffolk, meanwhile, woos Margaret of Anjou on the young king's behalf, with designs of his own.

works.title: The Second Part of King Henry the Sixth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Henry VI's marriage to Margaret of Anjou opens a reign of faction: the Duchess of Gloucester's sorcery brings down the good Duke Humphrey, murdered at the instigation of Suffolk, who is himself killed at sea by pirates. Jack Cade's rabble rising sweeps London in prose and carnage, while Richard of York throws off his pretence and openly claims the crown, winning the first battle of St Albans and opening the Wars of the Roses.

works.title: The Third Part of King Henry the Sixth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Henry VI, weak and pious, disinherits his own son in favour of the Duke of York, setting the Wars of the Roses ablaze: York is taunted and slain at Wakefield, the king watches the carnage from a molehill at Towton, and Warwick the Kingmaker changes sides when Edward IV marries for love. Edward's victory at Tewkesbury closes the play, with Gloucester, the future Richard III, murdering the captive Henry in the Tower.

works.title: King Henry the Eighth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Henry VIII's court sees the proud Duke of Buckingham brought down by Cardinal Wolsey's schemes, until Wolsey's own power turns to ruin when the king's eye falls on Anne Bullen. Queen Katherine defends her marriage at the Blackfriars trial and dies with dignity at Kimbolton. The play ends with the king's marriage to Anne and Cranmer's prophecy of greatness at the christening of the infant Elizabeth.

works.title: Hercules Furens
works.subtitle: Mad Hercules
works.author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
works.blurb: Juno, furious that Hercules has returned alive from the underworld, sends a madness upon him. While the tyrant Lycus presses Hercules’ wife Megara and old Amphitryon at the altar, the hero comes home, kills the usurper, and is then driven by Juno to slaughter his own wife and children, taking them for the family of his enemy Eurystheus. He wakes in his right mind to see what he has done, and only the entreaties of his friend Theseus keep him from suicide.

works.title: Hermann and Dorothea
works.subtitle: Hermann und Dorothea
works.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
works.blurb: A domestic epic in nine cantos of unrhymed hexameters: a German innkeeper's son falls in love with a refugee girl from the Rhine, against the backdrop of the French Revolution.

sections.title: V. Polyhymnia: The Citizen of the World

works.title: Hero and Leander
works.subtitle: Sestiads III–VI (Chapman's continuation of Marlowe)
works.author: George Chapman
works.blurb: Chapman's continuation of Marlowe's unfinished erotic epyllion, carrying the story of Hero and Leander from the lovers' first night to Leander's drowning in the Hellespont.

works.title: The Histories
works.subtitle: The History of Herodotus, in nine books, called by the names of the Muses
works.author: Herodotus
works.blurb: Herodotus's account of the rise of the Persian Empire and the Greek wars against it, in G. C. Macaulay's English prose of 1890.

works.title: The Catalogues of Women and Other Fragments
works.subtitle: Fragments of the Hesiodic poems, in prose translation
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: The surviving fragments of the poems ancient readers ascribed to Hesiod beyond the Theogony and Works and Days: the genealogical Catalogue of Women, the Great Eoiae, the Melampodia, the Aegimius and shorter pieces, mostly preserved as quotations by later writers.

sections.title: The Catalogues of Women and Eoiae

works.title: The Hind and the Panther
works.subtitle: A Poem, in Three Parts
works.author: John Dryden
works.blurb: A long allegorical fable in which the milk-white Hind (the Catholic Church) and the Panther (the Church of England) debate faith and politics after James II’s accession.

works.title: Hippolytus
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Aphrodite, scorned by the chaste huntsman Hippolytus, makes his stepmother Phaedra fall helplessly in love with him, and the secret destroys them both, in Arthur Way's rhymed English verse version of Euripides' tragedy.

works.title: Antoninus Caracalla
works.subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Aelius Spartianus
works.author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
works.blurb: The Life of the emperor Caracalla (AD 211-217), who murdered his brother Geta and ruled alone, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Spartianus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

works.title: Antoninus Diadumenianus
works.subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Aelius Lampridius
works.author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
works.blurb: The Life of Diadumenianus, the young son of Macrinus, made his father's colleague and put to death with him in AD 218, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Lampridius, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

works.title: Antoninus Elagabalus
works.subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Aelius Lampridius
works.author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
works.blurb: The Life of the emperor Elagabalus (AD 218-222), the young priest of the Syrian sun-god, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Lampridius, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

works.title: Antoninus Geta
works.subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Aelius Spartianus
works.author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
works.blurb: The short Life of Geta, Caracalla's younger brother and co-heir, murdered soon after their father's death, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Spartianus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

works.title: The Three Gordians
works.subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Julius Capitolinus
works.author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
works.blurb: The Lives of the three Gordians, the elder and younger Gordian proclaimed in Africa in AD 238 and the boy emperor Gordian III (reigned 238-244), in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

works.title: Opellius Macrinus
works.subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Julius Capitolinus
works.author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
works.blurb: The Life of Opellius Macrinus, the praetorian prefect who succeeded the murdered Caracalla and reigned briefly (AD 217-218), in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

works.title: The Two Maximini
works.subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Julius Capitolinus
works.author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
works.blurb: The Life of the soldier-emperor Maximinus and of his son and colleague Maximinus the Younger (AD 235-238), in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

works.title: Maximus and Balbinus
works.subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Julius Capitolinus
works.author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
works.blurb: The Life of Maximus (Pupienus) and Balbinus, the two senators raised to the purple in AD 238 against Maximinus, in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

works.title: Severus Alexander
works.subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Aelius Lampridius
works.author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
works.blurb: The Life of the emperor Severus Alexander (AD 222-235), the longest in this volume and the most openly admiring, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Lampridius, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

works.title: H.M.S. Pinafore
works.subtitle: Or, The Lass That Loved a Sailor
works.author: W. S. Gilbert
works.blurb: Aboard H.M.S. Pinafore off Portsmouth, Captain Corcoran's daughter Josephine loves the humble sailor Ralph Rakestraw, while the Captain wants her to marry Sir Joseph Porter, First Lord of the Admiralty, who rose from office boy to rule the Queen's Navee. The lovers plan to elope, the villainous Dick Deadeye betrays them, and Little Buttercup's confession of a baby-swap long ago puts every rank in its right place.

works.title: The Homeric Hymns
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Thirty-three anonymous hymns of invocation to the Greek gods, transmitted alongside Homer’s epics since antiquity and traditionally (though almost certainly wrongly) attributed to him.

Hymn XV — To Heracles The Lion-Hearted
Hymn XXIII — To The Son Of Cronos, Most High
Hymn XXV — To The Muses And Apollo
Hymn XXX — To Earth The Mother Of All

works.title: The Homeric Hymns
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: George Chapman’s verse versions of the Homeric Hymns, the anonymous invocations to the Greek gods that antiquity ascribed to Homer, published around 1624 as the companion to his Iliad and Odyssey.

sections.title: Hymn XIV — To The Mother Of The Gods
Hymn XV — To Heracles The Lion-Hearted
Hymn XXIII — To The Son Of Cronos, Most High
Hymn XXV — To The Muses And Apollo
Hymn XXX — To Earth The Mother Of All
A Hymn to Men of Hospitality

works.title: The Homeric Hymns
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Andrew Lang’s prose version of the thirty-three Homeric Hymns, the anonymous invocations to the Greek gods that antiquity ascribed to Homer. Lang numbers them in his own order, so his Hymn IV is the long Hymn to Demeter. Square brackets in the text are Lang’s own, marking passages of doubtful authenticity; his essays, notes and illustrations are omitted.

sections.title: XIII. To the Mother of the Gods
XXIV. To the Muses and Apollo
XXIX. To Earth, the Mother of All

works.title: The Hop-Garden
works.subtitle: A Georgic in Two Books
works.author: Christopher Smart
works.blurb: Smart's georgic in blank verse on the cultivation of hops in his native Kent, in the manner of Virgil and in the Miltonic style, first printed in his Poems on Several Occasions.

works.title: The House of Fame
works.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
works.blurb: A dream vision in three books in which the narrator is carried by a golden eagle to the palace of Fame, where rumour, reputation and the whims of the goddess decide which names endure.

works.title: Hudibras
works.subtitle: In Three Parts, Written in the Time of the Late Wars
works.author: Samuel Butler
works.blurb: Samuel Butler's mock-heroic satire on the Puritans and the Civil War, in which the knight Sir Hudibras and his squire Ralpho ride out to reform the world and are beaten, jailed and humbled in galloping octosyllabic couplets.

sections.title: An Heroical Epistle of Hudibras to Sidrophel
An Heroical Epistle of Hudibras to His Lady
The Lady's Answer to the Knight

works.title: The Tale of Alleyne
works.subtitle: from Moral Tales in Verse, vol. I (London, 1797)
works.author: Thomas Hull
works.blurb: A verse tale in two parts from Hull’s Moral Tales, preceded by a separate verse introduction.

works.title: The Tale of Cadwal
works.subtitle: from Moral Tales in Verse, vol. II (London, 1797)
works.author: Thomas Hull
works.blurb: A verse tale in two parts from Hull’s Moral Tales, preceded by a separate verse introduction.

works.title: The Tale of Edward and Orra
works.subtitle: from Moral Tales in Verse, vol. II (London, 1797)
works.author: Thomas Hull
works.blurb: A verse tale in four parts; the author’s note says its events occurred in a private London family about the middle of the eighteenth century.

works.title: The Tale of Foscue
works.subtitle: from Moral Tales in Verse, vol. I (London, 1797)
works.author: Thomas Hull
works.type: Narrative poem, in the manner of the old English ballad
works.blurb: A tale in two parts, written in imitation of the old English ballad; the source note says its hero, a Farmer-General, belongs to the years around 1761.

works.title: Richard Plantagenet
works.subtitle: A Legendary Tale, Now First Published
works.author: Thomas Hull
works.blurb: A legendary tale in two parts: the bricklayer Richard Plantagenet tells, in his old age, the story of his birth to the knight who has given him his land at Eastwell (London, 1774).

works.title: The Humours of the Court
works.subtitle: A Comedy in Three Acts
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's comedy in three acts, first published about 1893. The action fills three days at Belflor, the residence of the Countess Diana, where the Duke of Milan appears as Ricardo and her secretary Frederick, the major-domo Sir Gregory and his daughter Laura figure in the courtly intrigues.

works.title: Hymns to the Night
works.subtitle: Hymnen an die Nacht, translated from the German
works.author: Novalis (Friedrich von Hardenberg)
works.blurb: Six meditations on night, sleep and death, written after the death of the poet's betrothed, in George MacDonald's English.

works.title: Idylls of the King
works.subtitle: In Twelve Books
works.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
works.blurb: Tennyson's cycle of twelve idylls retelling the rise and fall of King Arthur's court, from The Coming of Arthur to The Passing of Arthur, framed by a dedication to Prince Albert and an epilogue to Queen Victoria.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Theodore Alois Buckley’s literal prose translation of Homer’s Iliad, keeping close to the Greek and marking its own additions in square brackets.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Samuel Butler’s brisk, plain-spoken prose translation of Homer’s epic of the wrath of Akhilleus and the last year of the siege of Troy.

works.title: The Iliad
works.subtitle: The Iliads of Homer, translated by George Chapman
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: George Chapman’s Iliad, the first complete English translation of the poem from the Greek, whose rolling fourteeners Keats praised in his sonnet “On First Looking into Chapman’s Homer.”

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.translator: trans. William Cowper (1791; Southey’s edition, New York 1860)
works.blurb: William Cowper’s blank-verse translation of the Iliad, first published in 1791, here in the 1860 New York edition of Robert Southey’s text.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: The Earl of Derby, three times Prime Minister, rendered Homer’s epic of the wrath of Akhilleus into stately Victorian blank verse.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Thomas Hobbes's rhymed-quatrain translation of the Iliad, first published in 1676 when the philosopher of the Leviathan was in his late eighties, here in the 1676 London edition of William Crook.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.translator: trans. Andrew Lang, Walter Leaf and Ernest Myers (1911)
works.blurb: The prose translation of the Iliad by Walter Leaf, Andrew Lang and Ernest Myers, in a deliberately archaic, Authorised-Version-flavoured English, here in the 1911 revised edition.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: A. T. Murray’s literal prose translation of the wrath of Akhilleus and the last year of the siege of Troy, from the Loeb Classical Library of 1924.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Alexander Pope’s celebrated heroic-couplet translation of the Iliad, one of the great achievements of Augustan English verse.

works.title: The Iliad (Way)
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Arthur S. Way’s rhymed verse translation of the Iliad, in long swinging anapaestic lines, published in two volumes in 1886 and 1888.

works.title: In a Balcony
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A short drama in one scene. Norbert, a young statesman, has won the Queen's favour and asks Constance, her cousin and companion, to let him claim her hand as his reward. Constance advises a cautious approach; the Queen, hearing him speak, mistakes whom he loves, and the evening ends in discovery.

works.title: Indian Idylls
works.subtitle: from the Sanskrit of the Mahabharata
works.author: Vyasa
works.blurb: Eight episodes from the Mahabharata in Sir Edwin Arnold's English verse, from the love of Savitri and the tale of Nala and Damayanti to the last journey of the Pandavas and Yudhisthira's entry into heaven.

works.title: The Inferno (Carlyle)
works.subtitle: Prose translation by John Aitken Carlyle, revised by H. Oelsner (Temple Classics)
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.translator: trans. John Aitken Carlyle (1849), revised by H. Oelsner (Temple Classics, 1900)
works.blurb: Dante's journey through Hell in John Aitken Carlyle's plain, literal prose, revised for the Temple Classics by Hermann Oelsner, whose added words are kept in square brackets.

works.title: The Inferno (Sibbald)
works.subtitle: Translated by James Romanes Sibbald
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Dante's journey through Hell, in James Romanes Sibbald's Victorian terza rima, the form and rhyme of the original kept.

works.title: The Inferno (Wright)
works.subtitle: Translated by Ichabod Charles Wright
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Dante's journey through Hell in Ichabod Charles Wright's rhymed tercets, the three-line stanza of the original kept.

works.title: Ion
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: At Delphi, a temple servant named Ion, once a foundling left in the sanctuary of Apollo, meets the childless Athenian queen Kreusa and her husband Xuthus. A muddled oracle, a failed poisoning and an ark of hidden tokens bring mother and son to recognise one another. Arthur Way renders Euripides' play in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Iphigeneia at Aulis
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: At Aulis the Greek fleet lies windbound, and the seer Kalchas declares that the goddess Artemis will release the winds only if Agamemnon sacrifices his daughter. Lured to the camp with the promise of a marriage to Akhilleus, Iphigeneia must choose between her mother's grief and her own willing death. Arthur Way renders Euripides' last tragedy in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Iphigeneia in Taurica
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Snatched from the altar at Aulis by Artemis, Iphigeneia serves as priestess in the savage land of the Taurians, where every Greek who lands is sacrificed to the goddess. When two strangers are seized on the shore, she finds that one of them is her brother Orestes, and together they plot an escape with the goddess's image. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy of recognition in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Iphigenia in Tauris
works.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
works.blurb: Goethe's verse drama in five acts. Iphigenia, saved from sacrifice at Aulis and made priestess of Diana among the Taurians, longs for Greece. When her brother Orestes, pursued by the Furies, arrives with his friend Pylades as captives destined for the altar, she must choose between truth and escape, and between loyalty to the king who sheltered her and the call of her family.

works.title: Discourses, Volume I
works.subtitle: To Demonicus, To Nicocles, Nicocles or the Cyprians, Panegyricus, To Philip, Archidamus
works.author: Isocrates
works.blurb: Six of the discourses of the Athenian orator Isocrates, from the first volume of Norlin's Loeb edition: three on kingship and conduct, the Panegyricus, and the appeals to Philip and Archidamus.

works.title: Discourses, Volume II
works.subtitle: On the Peace, Areopagiticus, Against the Sophists, Antidosis, Panathenaicus
works.author: Isocrates
works.blurb: Five of the discourses of the Athenian orator Isocrates, from the second volume of Norlin's Loeb edition: the appeals On the Peace and the Areopagiticus, the prospectus Against the Sophists, the Antidosis (his defence of his life's work as a teacher), and the Panathenaicus.

works.title: Italy
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Samuel Rogers
works.blurb: Samuel Rogers's travel poem in blank verse, published in two parts in 1822 and 1828, in which a pilgrim from the north passes through the Alps, Lombardy, Venice, Florence, Rome and Naples, telling the local legends as he goes.

works.title: Jenny
works.author: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
works.blurb: A dramatic monologue spoken at dawn by a young man over the sleeping prostitute whose head rests on his knee.

works.title: Jerusalem
works.subtitle: The Emanation of the Giant Albion
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Blake's longest prophetic poem, in four chapters, in which the sleeping giant Albion is called back to Jerusalem, his lost Emanation, and to the forgiveness of sins.

works.title: Jerusalem Delivered
works.subtitle: Gerusalemme Liberata
works.author: Torquato Tasso
works.blurb: Tasso's epic of the First Crusade and the siege of Jerusalem under Godfrey of Bouillon, in twenty books of ottava rima, in Edward Fairfax's English version.

works.title: Jerusalem Delivered
works.subtitle: Translated into English Spenserian Verse by J. H. Wiffen
works.author: Torquato Tasso
works.blurb: Tasso's epic of the First Crusade and the siege of Jerusalem under Godfrey of Bouillon, in twenty books, in J. H. Wiffen's English version in nine-line Spenserian stanzas (1824–25).

works.title: The Jew of Malta
works.author: Christopher Marlowe
works.blurb: Barabas, the richest Jew of Malta, is stripped of his wealth by Governor Ferneze to pay the tribute owed the Turks, and sets out on a course of revenge that costs him his daughter Abigail, a convent of nuns, two friars and his own accomplices. Prefaced by Machiavel in person, Marlowe's savage comedy of greed, religion and policy ends with Barabas boiled in the very cauldron he prepared for the Turkish prince.

sections.title: Prologue to the Stage, at the Cock-pit
Epilogue to the Stage, at the Cock-pit

works.title: Joan of Arc, an Epic Poem
works.subtitle: In Ten Books (first edition, 1796)
works.author: Robert Southey
works.blurb: Southey's youthful republican epic in ten books of blank verse, written in 1793 and published in 1796: Joan of Arc heals the wounded Dunois, wins over Charles VII and the besieged city of Orleans, and in visions of Heaven and Hell sees the crimes of kings and the hope of a freer world.

works.title: The Book of Job
works.subtitle: Authorized Version of the book of Job.
works.author: The Bible (Authorized King James Version)
works.blurb: A long poetic dialogue between Job and his friends, set within a prose frame.

works.title: Job the White
works.subtitle: Fo'c's'le Yarns, Third Series: 2
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: A sequel to The Manx Witch, in dialect verse, which Brown published in The New Review in December 1895.

works.title: Clifton
works.subtitle: a Poem, in Two Cantos
works.author: Henry Jones
works.blurb: Henry Jones's topographical poem on Clifton and the Hotwells near Bristol, praising its spa, its houses and its company in heroic couplets.

works.title: The Isle of Wight
works.subtitle: a Poem, in Three Cantos
works.author: Henry Jones
works.blurb: Henry Jones's topographical poem in three cantos on the Isle of Wight, its scenery and towns, written in heroic couplets.

works.title: Against Apion
works.subtitle: Josephus's defence of the antiquity of the Jewish people against Apion and other Greek detractors, in two books
works.author: Flavius Josephus
works.blurb: Josephus's reply to the slanders of Apion, Manetho, Apollonius Molon and others, setting out the antiquity of the Jews and the excellence of their law, in William Whiston's English of 1737.

works.title: The Antiquities of the Jews
works.subtitle: The Jewish Antiquities, in twenty books, from the Creation to the twelfth year of Nero
works.author: Flavius Josephus
works.blurb: Josephus's history of the Jewish people from the Creation to the eve of the revolt against Rome, in twenty books, in William Whiston's English of 1737.

works.title: The Wars of the Jews; or, The History of the Destruction of Jerusalem
works.subtitle: The Jewish War, in seven books, from the capture of Jerusalem by Antiochus Epiphanes to the fall of Masada
works.author: Flavius Josephus
works.blurb: Josephus's eyewitness account of the Jewish revolt against Rome (AD 66–73), from the siege of Jotapata to the burning of the Temple and the end at Masada, in William Whiston's English of 1737.

works.title: The Life of Flavius Josephus
works.subtitle: Josephus's autobiography, written about AD 100 as an appendix to the Antiquities
works.author: Flavius Josephus
works.blurb: Josephus's account of his priestly descent, his schooling among the Pharisees, Sadducees and Essenes, his command in Galilee during the revolt against Rome, and his later life, in William Whiston's English of 1737.

works.title: Judas Maccabaeus
works.subtitle: A Play in Five Acts
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A verse play on the Jewish revolt against the Syrian king Antiochus Epiphanes. Antiochus, with the renegade High-Priest Jason, tries to force Greek gods on Jerusalem; a mother and her seven sons endure martyrdom; Judas Maccabaeus rallies the Jews, defeats the general Nicanor and retakes the Temple; and the play closes with the death of Antiochus.

works.title: Judith
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.translator: trans. Cosette Faust Newton & Stith Thompson (1918)
works.blurb: A retelling, in the Nowell Codex alongside Beowulf, of the apocryphal Book of Judith: the widow Judith beheads the drunken Assyrian general Holofernes and delivers her people, recast in the heroic idiom of Old English verse.

works.title: Judith (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: A retelling, in the Nowell Codex alongside Beowulf, of the apocryphal Book of Judith, in the original Old English: the widow Judith beheads the drunken Assyrian general Holofernes and delivers her people, recast in the heroic idiom of Old English verse.

works.title: Juliana
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: One of Cynewulf's four signed poems: the passion of the virgin martyr Juliana of Nicomedia, who resists both an unwanted marriage to a pagan prefect and torture by a demon sent to break her faith.

works.title: Juliana (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: The Old English verse of one of Cynewulf's four signed poems: the passion of the virgin martyr Juliana of Nicomedia, who resists both an unwanted marriage to a pagan prefect and torture by a demon sent to break her faith.

works.title: The Civil War
works.subtitle: Commentaries on the civil war between Caesar and Pompey, 49–48 BC, in three books (De Bello Civili)
works.author: Julius Caesar
works.translator: trans. W. A. McDevitte and W. S. Bohn (1869)
works.blurb: Caesar's own account of the outbreak of the war with Pompey and the Senate: the crossing of the Rubicon, the Italian and Spanish campaigns, the siege of Massilia, and the struggle in Illyricum, Africa, Epirus and Thessaly down to the eve of the Alexandrian war.

works.title: The Gallic War
works.subtitle: Commentaries on the war in Gaul, 58–52 BC, in eight books (De Bello Gallico)
works.author: Julius Caesar
works.translator: trans. W. A. McDevitte and W. S. Bohn (1869)
works.blurb: Caesar's own account of his campaigns against the Gauls, Germans and Britons, from the Helvetian migration to the siege of Alesia and the final pacification of Gaul, with Hirtius's continuation.

works.title: The Tragedy of Julius Caesar
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Rome's leaders fear that Julius Caesar, fresh from his triumph over Pompey's sons, will make himself king. Cassius draws the honourable Brutus into a conspiracy, and the conspirators stab Caesar in the Capitol on the Ides of March. Brutus justifies the killing to the crowd, but Mark Antony's funeral speech turns the people against the assassins and they are driven from the city. Brutus and Cassius quarrel, then are overwhelmed by Antony and Octavius at Philippi, where both die by their own hands.

works.title: The Kalevala
works.subtitle: The Epic Poem of Finland
works.author: Elias Lönnrot
works.blurb: Fifty runes of Finnish folk song gathered into one epic: the birth of the sage Wainamoinen, the rivalry of Finns and the people of Pohjola for the Sampo, the doomed Kullervo, and the hero's departure as a new age arrives.

works.title: The Kasîdah of Hâjî Abdû El-Yezdî
works.author: Sir Richard Francis Burton
works.blurb: A philosophical quatrain-sequence in which a desert traveller, Haji Abdu, reflects on faith, fate and the vanity of creeds. Burton's own composition, offered as a rendering from the Persian.

works.title: Keep Your Own Secret
works.author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
works.blurb: At the court of Parma the Prince, his secretary Don Cesar and the courtier Don Felix each hide a love from the rest, and every secret confided to the wrong ear tangles the plot further. The comedy ends with Nisida's hand placed in Felix's and a moral against trusting even a friend with a secret.

works.title: King Arthur
works.subtitle: Books I to XII
works.author: Edward Bulwer Lytton
works.blurb: Bulwer Lytton’s twelve-book romantic epic in Spenserian stanzas, following Arthur and the wizard Merlin through the three labours of Fable-land.

works.title: King Horn
works.subtitle: Middle English text of Cambridge University Library MS Gg.4.27.2, ed. J. R. Lumby (1866), re-ed. G. H. McKnight (1901)
works.author: Anonymous
works.blurb: The earliest surviving English verse romance: the exiled prince Horn, cast adrift as a boy after Saracens kill his father, wins the love of Rymenhild, proves himself in Ireland, and returns to reclaim his kingdom.

works.title: The Life and Death of King John
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: King John holds the English crown against the claim of his nephew Arthur, whom France backs, and the play follows the quarrel through the siege of Angiers, the bargained marriage of Louis and Blanche, and the grief of Arthur's mother Constance. Philip Faulconbridge, the Bastard, acknowledged as Richard Lionheart's son, becomes the play's sardonic commentator on politics and 'commodity'. Arthur dies leaping from the castle walls, the barons turn against John, and the king is poisoned at Swinstead Abbey, leaving England to young Henry.

works.title: The Tragedy of King Lear
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: King Lear, old and weary of rule, divides his kingdom among his daughters according to their professions of love, banishing the plain-spoken Cordelia and Kent. Goneril and Regan soon strip him of his retinue and turn him out into the storm, where he goes mad upon the heath beside his Fool and the disguised Edgar. Meanwhile Gloucester, deceived by his bastard son Edmund, is blinded for helping the king. Cordelia returns with a French army, but Lear and she are defeated, and the play ends in the deaths of Cordelia, Lear and almost all the rest.

works.title: King Victor and King Charles: A Tragedy
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A historical tragedy of the House of Savoy. In 1730 the aged Victor Amadeus, first King of Sardinia, abdicates in favour of his timid son Charles; within a year he regrets it and tries to take the crown back, and the second half of the play follows the son's struggle to keep his throne against his father and the minister D'Ormea.
