works.title: Patience
works.author: Gawain Poet
works.blurb: A retelling of the Book of Jonah in about 530 alliterative lines, preceded by a prologue on the Beatitudes of poverty and patience. The reluctant prophet flees by sea, is swallowed by the whale and is finally rebuked for his anger at God's mercy.

works.title: Description of Greece, vol. 1 (Books I-VI)
works.subtitle: Attica, Corinth, Laconia, Messenia and Elis
works.author: Pausanias
works.blurb: The first half of the traveller Pausanias's Greek guidebook: Attica, Corinth, Laconia, Messenia and Elis, with their temples, statues, legends and battles, in A. R. Shilleto's English of 1886.

works.title: Description of Greece, vol. 2 (Books VII-X)
works.subtitle: Achaia, Arcadia, Boeotia and Phocis
works.author: Pausanias
works.blurb: The second half of the traveller Pausanias's Greek guidebook: Achaia, Arcadia, Boeotia and Phocis, with their temples, statues, legends and battles, in A. R. Shilleto's English of 1886.

works.title: Pearl
works.author: Gawain Poet
works.blurb: A grieving father falls asleep on the grave of his infant daughter and dreams her transfigured into a maiden of Heaven, radiant among the elect — an elegy of loss answered by consolation, in interlocking rhymed stanzas.

works.title: Pearl (Middle English text)
works.subtitle: The Pearl
works.author: Gawain Poet
works.blurb: The original Middle English text of the dream-vision elegy, in 101 twelve-line stanzas of interlocking rhyme and alliteration. A bereaved father falls asleep by the grave of his lost pearl and sees her, transfigured, across a stream in the heavenly city.

works.title: Peer Gynt
works.subtitle: A Dramatic Poem
works.author: Henrik Ibsen
works.blurb: Peer Gynt, a boastful young peasant, steals a bride, flees into the mountains and the hall of the Troll King, and goes out into the world: a rich trader in Morocco, a prophet among the Bedouin, an emperor in a Cairo madhouse. Returning old and empty-handed, he meets the Button-Moulder, who has come to melt him down, and the faithful Solveig, who has waited.

works.title: The Psalms of David (Psalms 44–150)
works.subtitle: Metrical paraphrase from the Sidney Psalter, in the 1823 printed text
works.author: Mary Sidney Herbert, Countess of Pembroke
works.blurb: The Countess of Pembroke's verse paraphrase of Psalms 44–150, each psalm in a different stanza form, completing the psalter begun by her brother Sir Philip Sidney.

works.title: Pericles, Prince of Tyre
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: To make a wife of the incestuous Antiochus's daughter, Prince Pericles of Tyre must solve a deadly riddle, and having solved it he flees, beginning years of shipwreck and exile narrated by the ghostly poet Gower. He wins Thaisa at Pentapolis, loses her at sea in childbirth, and leaves their daughter Marina at Tarsus, where jealous Dionyza plots her murder and pirates carry her to a brothel in Mytilene. After a long grief he is reunited with Marina and, guided by Diana, with Thaisa at Ephesus.

works.title: The Persians
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: At the Persian court of Susa, the elders and the queen mother Atossa wait anxiously for news of Xerxes and his vast army, gone to conquer Greece. A messenger arrives with the tale of Salamis and the ruin of the fleet, and the ghost of Darius is raised from the tomb to name the king's pride as the cause. Xerxes returns in rags to a chorus of lament.

works.title: Peru
works.subtitle: A Poem in Six Cantos
works.author: Helen Maria Williams
works.blurb: A poem in six cantos on the Spanish conquest of Peru, the fall of the Inca Ataliba and the sufferings of his queen Alzira, ending in an appeal against cruelty and the lust for gold.

works.title: The Satyricon
works.subtitle: Satyricon, or the Satyrical Adventures of Encolpius
works.author: Petronius
works.blurb: The surviving episodes of Petronius's comic novel of Nero's Italy, in which Encolpius and his companions drift from lodging-house to the banquet of the freedman Trimalchio, in Michael Heseltine's English prose of 1913.

works.title: Phaedra
works.author: Jean Racine
works.blurb: At Troezen, Phaedra, wife of the absent Theseus, wastes away with a guilty passion for her stepson Hippolytus. Word comes that Theseus is dead, and she confesses her love; then he returns alive. Her nurse Oenone accuses Hippolytus of the very crime Phaedra herself desired, and Theseus calls down Neptune's curse on his son, who is killed by a sea monster. Phaedra takes poison and admits her guilt before she dies.

works.title: Phaedra
works.subtitle: or Hippolytus
works.author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
works.blurb: Phaedra, wife of the absent Theseus, is consumed by a guilty passion for her stepson Hippolytus, an austere young huntsman who scorns love. Her nurse carries her secret to him and he recoils in horror. When Theseus unexpectedly returns, Phaedra accuses Hippolytus of attacking her. Theseus calls down a curse on his son, and a monster from the sea destroys him. Phaedra confesses the truth and kills herself.

works.title: The Phenomena and Diosemeia
works.author: Aratus of Soli
works.blurb: A heroic-couplet version of Aratus’s star-poem and its weather signs by John Lamb, Dean of Bristol, published in 1848.

works.title: Phaenomena
works.author: Aratus
works.blurb: Aratus’s hexameter account of the constellations, the celestial circles, the risings of the zodiac and the weather signs, a poem of the stars that was widely read and translated in antiquity.

sections.title: A. Constellations north of the ecliptic (Lines 19–318)
B. Constellations south of the ecliptic (Lines 319–453)
D. Circles of the celestial sphere (Lines 462–558)

works.title: Pharonnida
works.subtitle: A Heroick Poem
works.author: William Chamberlayne
works.blurb: A heroic romance in rhymed couplets, in five books of five cantos each, of love and adventure among Christians and Turks; text from the 1659 edition (EEBO-TCP), in original spelling.

works.title: Pharsalia
works.subtitle: De Bello Civili (The Civil War)
works.author: Lucan
works.blurb: Lucan’s unfinished epic of the Roman civil war between Julius Caesar and Pompey, notable for banishing the gods from its narrative entirely.

works.title: The Civil War (Pharsalia)
works.subtitle: Books I-X, Loeb translation by J. D. Duff
works.author: Lucan
works.blurb: J. D. Duff's plain prose translation of Lucan's unfinished epic of the Roman civil war between Caesar and Pompey, ten books ending where Lucan's text breaks off.

works.title: Pharsalia
works.subtitle: Lucan's Pharsalia, containing the civil wars between Caesar and Pompey
works.author: Lucan
works.blurb: Sir Arthur Gorges's 1614 rhymed translation of Lucan's epic of the Roman civil war, in octosyllabic couplets, with a verse argument before each book.

works.title: Pharsalia (May)
works.subtitle: Lucans Pharsalia: or The Civill Warres of Rome, betweene Pompey the Great, and Iulius Caesar
works.author: Lucan
works.blurb: Thomas May's rhymed heroic-couplet translation of Lucan's epic of the Roman civil war, the first complete English version in pentameter couplets, with May's own verse argument before each book.

works.title: Pharsalia (Rowe)
works.subtitle: Lucan's Pharsalia, translated into English verse by Nicholas Rowe
works.author: Lucan
works.blurb: Nicholas Rowe's version of Lucan's epic of the Roman civil war between Caesar and Pompey, in heroic couplets, published after the translator's death in 1718.

works.title: Philoctetes
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Odysseus brings the young Neoptolemus to Lemnos to trick the exiled Philoctetes out of the bow of Heracles, without which Troy cannot fall. Neoptolemus, moved by pity and shame, gives the bow back, and only the appearance of the deified Heracles persuades the wounded archer to sail for Troy and healing.

works.title: Philoctetes
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Left on desolate Lemnos for ten years with a festering wound, the archer Philoctetes is the only man who can bend the bow of Heracles, and Troy cannot fall without it. Odysseus sends young Neoptolemus to win the weapon by deceit, but the boy finds he cannot betray a suffering man, and only the voice of the deified Heracles can resolve the clash of honour and necessity.

works.title: The Phoenician Maidens
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Thebes is besieged by Polyneikes and his Argive host, and the house of Oedipus stands on the edge of its last catastrophe: Jocasta, Kreon, the blind seer Teiresias and a chorus of Phoenician maidens watch as the brothers move toward single combat. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy in rhymed English verse.

works.title: The Phoenix
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.translator: trans. Cosette Faust Newton & Stith Thompson (1918)
works.blurb: A richly decorative description of the mythical phoenix and its cyclical death and rebirth in a paradisal eastern land, allegorized in the poem's second half as a figure of Christian resurrection.

works.title: The Phoenix (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The Old English verse of a richly decorative description of the mythical phoenix and its cyclical death and rebirth in a paradisal eastern land, allegorized in the poem's second half as a figure of Christian resurrection.

works.title: The Piccolomini
works.author: Friedrich Schiller
works.blurb: At Pilsen, in the Thirty Years' War, the imperial generals gather round their commander Wallenstein while a plot against him is already being laid by Octavio Piccolomini, whose son Max loves Wallenstein's daughter Thekla. Octavio holds a secret commission to take the generalship, and father and son are drawn toward a collision of loyalties.

works.title: Piers Plowman
works.subtitle: The Vision of Piers Ploughman
works.author: William Langland
works.blurb: Falling asleep on the Malvern Hills, the dreamer Will sees a field full of folk and sets out through a sequence of visions to find Do-well, Do-bet, and Do-best — a vast alliterative satire of church, court, and commons.

works.title: The Pilgrims of the Sun
works.author: James Hogg
works.blurb: A visionary poem in four books, in Spenserian stanzas, in which a Scottish girl, Mary Lee, is borne in spirit through the planets and the sun, with a dedication to Lord Byron.

works.title: Pippa Passes
works.subtitle: A Drama
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: Browning's drama of New Year's Day at Asolo follows Pippa, a silk-mill girl on her one holiday, whose songs, passing unheard by, break in on four scenes of love, guilt, plot and temptation and change the lives of those who hear them.

works.title: The Pirates of Penzance
works.subtitle: Or, The Slave of Duty
works.author: W. S. Gilbert
works.blurb: Frederic, bound apprentice to a band of tender-hearted pirates by his nurse's mistake, is freed on his twenty-first birthday and falls in love with Mabel, daughter of Major-General Stanley. But he was born on 29 February, so his indentures have barely a quarter of their term run, and his duty to the pirates and to the law pull him apart until a call to yield in Queen Victoria's name resolves the matter.

works.title: Apology
works.subtitle: The defence of Socrates before the Athenian jury
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: Socrates' speech to the Athenian jury at his trial for impiety and corrupting the young, followed by his words after the verdict and the sentence of death. Plato's account of the philosopher's defence of the examined life.

works.title: Crito
works.subtitle: Socrates in prison refuses to escape
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: In the prison at dawn, Crito urges the condemned Socrates to escape. Socrates replies by questioning him on justice and, speaking for the Laws of Athens, explains why he must stay and accept his sentence.

works.title: Euthyphro
works.subtitle: Socrates and Euthyphro on the nature of piety
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: On the porch of the King Archon, Socrates meets Euthyphro, who is about to prosecute his own father for murder, and asks him what piety really is. Each definition falls apart under questioning, and the dialogue ends without an answer.

works.title: Gorgias
works.subtitle: Socrates on rhetoric, justice and the good life
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: Socrates questions the rhetoricians Gorgias and Polus, and then the ambitious Callicles, on whether the orator's power is a true art or mere flattery, and whether it is better to do wrong or to suffer it. Ends with the myth of the judgment of the dead.

works.title: Laws
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: Plato's last and longest dialogue: an Athenian Stranger, a Cretan and a Spartan walk from Knossos to the cave of Zeus, talking the whole way, and draw up the laws of a new colony, from education, marriage and drinking parties to crime, religion and the Nocturnal Council that is to guard the state.

works.title: Meno
works.subtitle: The dialogue on whether virtue can be taught
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: Meno asks whether virtue can be taught; Socrates answers with a geometry lesson for a slave boy, the theory of recollection, and a search for what virtue is.

works.title: Parmenides
works.subtitle: The dialogue on the One and the Forms
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: Cephalus recounts how the young Socrates met the aged Parmenides and Zeno, and how Parmenides tested the theory of Forms and then led the young Aristoteles through the long exercise on the One.

works.title: Phaedo
works.subtitle: The dialogue on the immortality of the soul and the death of Socrates
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: On his last day in prison Socrates talks with his friends about death, the soul and its survival, and then drinks the hemlock.

works.title: Phaedrus
works.subtitle: The dialogue on love, rhetoric and the soul
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: Socrates and Phaedrus talk beneath a plane-tree by the Ilissus: three speeches on love lead to the myth of the soul's winged chariot, and then to the nature of true rhetoric and the worth of writing.

works.title: Protagoras
works.subtitle: The dialogue on whether virtue can be taught
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: Socrates meets the great sophist Protagoras at the house of Callias and asks whether virtue is one thing or many, and whether it can be taught.

works.title: The Republic
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: Socrates and his companions in the Piraeus ask what justice is, and build in speech an ideal city and a just soul, ending with the myth of Er.

works.title: Sophist
works.subtitle: The dialogue on being and not-being
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: Theodorus brings a stranger from Elea to Socrates, and with Theaetetus he hunts the sophist through a series of divisions, which forces a reckoning with the riddle of what is not.

works.title: Statesman
works.subtitle: The dialogue on the art of ruling, also called Politicus
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: The Eleatic Stranger, with the young Socrates, seeks the definition of the statesman by division, tells the myth of the reversed cosmos, and likens the king's art to weaving.

works.title: Symposium
works.subtitle: The banquet at Agathon's house and the speeches in praise of Love
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: At a supper in the house of the tragic poet Agathon, the guests, Socrates among them, each deliver a speech in praise of Love; the drunken Alcibiades breaks in at the end.

works.title: Theaetetus
works.subtitle: The dialogue on the nature of knowledge
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: Socrates, the midwife of ideas, questions the young Theaetetus on what knowledge is: perception, true opinion, or true opinion with an account.

works.title: Timaeus
works.subtitle: The dialogue on the making of the world, the soul and the human body
works.author: Plato
works.blurb: Timaeus tells how a good Creator shaped the ordered world, its soul and its living creatures, after Critias recalls the story of Atlantis.

works.title: Amphitryon
works.subtitle: Jupiter in Disguise
works.author: Plautus
works.blurb: Jupiter takes the shape of the Theban general Amphitryon, and Mercury that of his slave Sosia, so that the god may spend the night with Alcmena while her husband is at the wars; when the true master and servant come home, nobody in the house can tell who is who, until Jupiter shows himself and Alcmena has borne twins, Hercules and Iphiclus.

works.title: Aulularia; or, The Concealed Treasure
works.subtitle: The Pot of Gold
works.author: Plautus
works.blurb: A comedy of Euclio, a miser who has found a pot of gold hidden by his grandfather and cannot rest for fear of thieves, while a rich neighbour asks for his daughter's hand, a slave steals the pot, and the girl's secret comes out. The ending is lost. Molière drew on it for L'Avare.

works.title: Bacchides; or, The Twin-Sisters
works.author: Plautus
works.blurb: Mnesilochus asks his friend Pistoclerus to find his lost mistress Bacchis, and Pistoclerus is drawn into the house of her twin sister, also called Bacchis; the quick-witted slave Chrysalus then tricks old Nicobulus out of his gold, not once but twice, to rescue the young men from a swaggering captain. When the fathers finally see through the scheme and come to demand their sons, the two courtesans coax them in as well.

works.title: Captivi
works.subtitle: The Captives
works.author: Plautus
works.blurb: A comedy of two captives who swap names and clothes, so that a slave may send his master home, while the old man who owns them does not know that the slave is his own lost son.

works.title: Casina
works.subtitle: The Stratagem Defeated
works.author: Plautus
works.blurb: Two slaves, Olympio the bailiff and Chalinus the armour-bearer, are set to win the foundling girl Casina as a bride, each at the secret bidding of a rival in love: old Stalino wants her for himself, and his son for himself. His wife Cleostrata takes her son's side, the matter is settled by drawing lots, and when Stalino's man wins she and her friend Myrrhina dress up Chalinus as the veiled bride, so that the old lecher and the bailiff go off to the bridal chamber with a bearded, hard-fisted wife; the play ends in a thrashing, a pardon, and the discovery that Casina is a freeborn Athenian.

works.title: Menaechmi
works.subtitle: The Twin Brothers
works.author: Plautus
works.blurb: A comedy of mistaken identity: one twin, carried off as a child to Epidamnus, is mistaken for the other, who has come in search of him, so that a courtesan, a parasite, a wife and a father-in-law all take the stranger for the man they know. It was the source of Shakespeare's Comedy of Errors.

sections.title: Act V, Scene I (second Act V heading)
Act V, Scene II (second Act V heading)

works.title: Miles Gloriosus
works.subtitle: The Braggart Captain
works.author: Plautus
works.blurb: A comedy of Ephesus in which a vainglorious soldier who has carried off an Athenian girl is outwitted by his own slave: a hole in the party wall, a twin sister who does not exist, a pretended wife next door, and a beating for the braggart in the end.

works.title: Mostellaria
works.subtitle: The Haunted House
works.author: Plautus
works.blurb: While old Theuropides is abroad, his son Philolaches squanders the estate on revels and on buying a music-girl her freedom; when the father returns unexpectedly, the quick-witted slave Tranio saves the day by claiming that the house is haunted and has been shut up, then ensnares the old man in one lie after another until the truth comes out and the young men are forgiven.

works.title: Pseudolus
works.subtitle: The Cheat
works.author: Plautus
works.blurb: A comedy of intrigue: the slave Pseudolus promises his young master Calidorus that he will win back the girl Phoenicium, whom the pimp Ballio has sold to a soldier, and he does it by tricking pimp, soldier's messenger and his own master alike. Cicero records that Plautus himself counted it among his best plays.

works.title: Rudens
works.subtitle: The Rope
works.author: Plautus
works.blurb: A comedy of shipwreck and recognition: a storm raised by the star Arcturus wrecks a procurer's ship off the coast near Cyrene and casts two girls ashore at the temple of Venus, where a fisherman hauls up in his net a wallet whose trinkets reveal that one of them is the lost daughter of the old exile who lives next door.

works.title: Trinummus
works.subtitle: The Three Pieces of Money
works.author: Plautus
works.blurb: A comedy of money and friendship, adapted from Philemon's The Treasure. While the merchant Charmides is abroad, his spendthrift son Lesbonicus sells the family house, and Charmides' friend Callicles buys it, in secret, to protect the treasure buried beneath it. To give the daughter a dowry without shaming her brother, a hired sharper is sent with a pretended letter and 'three pieces of money'; but Charmides returns just in time to meet him. The play opens with Luxury leading her daughter Poverty to the young man's door.

works.title: The Pleasures of Memory
works.subtitle: In Two Parts
works.author: Samuel Rogers
works.blurb: Samuel Rogers's best-known poem, in heroic couplets, on the association of ideas and the consolations of memory, from a revisited village to the afterlife.

works.title: Letters
works.subtitle: Selected letters, with the correspondence with the Emperor Trajan
works.author: Pliny the Younger
works.translator: trans. William Melmoth (1746), revised by F. C. T. Bosanquet (1878)
works.blurb: Pliny's polished letters to friends and statesmen, among them the eruption of Vesuvius and his ghost stories, followed by his official correspondence with the Emperor Trajan, including the exchange on the Christians of Bithynia.

sections.title: Book X: Correspondence with the Emperor Trajan

works.title: Parallel Lives, Part I
works.subtitle: Theseus to Marcus Cato, with their Comparisons
works.author: Plutarch
works.translator: trans. John Dryden and others, revised by Arthur Hugh Clough (1859)
works.blurb: Plutarch sets the lives of Greek and Roman statesmen and soldiers side by side, reading character through deeds, sayings and small incidents, and closes most pairs with a comparison of the two men. This first part opens with the founders and lawgivers, Theseus and Romulus, Lycurgus and Numa, Solon and Poplicola, then follows the great captains and politicians of Athens and Rome, among them Themistocles, Pericles, Alcibiades, Coriolanus, Aemilius Paulus and Cato the Censor.

sections.title: Comparison of Timoleon with Aemilius Paulus
Comparison of Aristides with Marcus Cato

works.title: Parallel Lives, Part II
works.subtitle: Philopoemen to Pompey and Agesilaus, with their Comparisons
works.author: Plutarch
works.translator: trans. John Dryden and others, revised by Arthur Hugh Clough (1859)
works.blurb: The second part of the Lives pairs Greek and Roman soldiers and statesmen of the Hellenistic and late Republican ages: Philopoemen and Flamininus, the liberators and last defenders of Greece; Pyrrhus and Marius; Lysander and Sylla; Cimon and Lucullus; Nicias and Crassus, two fortunes ruined abroad; Sertorius and Eumenes, exiles who led foreign armies; and Agesilaus and Pompey. As before, Plutarch reads character through deeds and sayings, and closes most pairs with a comparison.

works.title: Parallel Lives, Part III
works.subtitle: Alexander to Cicero, with their Comparisons
works.author: Plutarch
works.translator: trans. John Dryden and others, revised by Arthur Hugh Clough (1859)
works.blurb: Here Plutarch pairs the conquerors and the statesmen who failed to save their republics: Alexander with Caesar, the honest Phocion with Cato the Younger, the reforming kings of Sparta, Agis and Cleomenes, with the tribunes Tiberius and Caius Gracchus, and finally the orator Demosthenes with Cicero. Anecdote, omen and last words are his preferred evidence of character.

sections.title: Comparison of Tiberius and Caius Gracchus with Agis and Cleomenes

works.title: Parallel Lives, Part IV
works.subtitle: Demetrius to Otho, with their Comparisons
works.author: Plutarch
works.translator: trans. John Dryden and others, revised by Arthur Hugh Clough (1859)
works.blurb: The last part of the Lives pairs Demetrius the Besieger with Mark Antony, Dion of Syracuse with Marcus Brutus, and closes with the single Lives of Aratus of Sicyon, the Persian king Artaxerxes, and the short-lived emperors Galba and Otho. Plutarch reads ambition, luxury and loyalty through the fates of men who rose by arms and fell to their own excess or to conspiracy, from the Hellenistic kings to the civil wars of Rome and the year of the four emperors.

works.title: The Poetic Edda
works.subtitle: Lays of the Gods and Lays of the Heroes, translated from the Icelandic with the stanza numbering of the standard editions
works.author: Anonymous (Old Norse)
works.blurb: The great Old Norse collection of mythological and heroic lays preserved in the Codex Regius, in Bellows's 1923 verse translation, with the Eddas' own prose links kept in place.

works.title: The Elder Edda
works.subtitle: The Poetic Edda of Sæmund
works.author: Anonymous (Old Norse)
works.blurb: The Old Norse mythological and heroic lays of the Codex Regius in Benjamin Thorpe's 1866 prose translation, with the manuscripts' own prose links kept in place.

sections.title: Fragments of the Lay of Sigurd and Brynhild

works.title: The Poet's Pilgrimage to Waterloo
works.subtitle: Proem and two parts (1816)
works.author: Robert Southey
works.blurb: Southey's account in six-line stanzas of his journey in 1815 through Flanders and Brussels to the field of Waterloo, followed by a dream-vision on the Mountain of the Muse in which he is shown the hopes of mankind after the victory.

Part I, Canto IV: The Scene of War

Part II, Canto II: The Evil Prophet
Part II, Canto III: The Sacred Mountain
Part II, Canto IV: The Hopes of Man

works.title: Politian: Scenes from an Unpublished Drama
works.author: Edgar Allan Poe
works.blurb: Poe's only drama, left unfinished, survives in five blank-verse scenes set in Rome. Politian, Earl of Leicester, loves Lalage, a ward whose betrothal to the Count Castiglione stands in the way; haunted by melancholy and fatal premonition, he is drawn toward a challenge that the scenes break off before resolving.

works.title: Poltava
works.subtitle: A poem in three cantos
works.author: Alexander Pushkin
works.blurb: Pushkin's narrative poem of Mazeppa, Kotzubei and his daughter Marie, set against the Ukrainian hetman's betrayal of Peter the Great and the battle of Poltava (1709), in Charles Edward Turner's 1899 English version.

works.title: Poly-Olbion
works.subtitle: A Chorographicall Description of Great Britain, in thirty Songs
works.author: Michael Drayton
works.blurb: Drayton's topographical poem in alexandrines on the rivers, hills, forests and history of England and Wales, in thirty Songs (Songs 1-18 printed 1612, Songs 19-30 in 1622), each opening with its verse Argument; Selden's prose Illustrations are omitted.

works.title: The Histories, Books I–IX
works.author: Polybius
works.blurb: Polybius's account of how Rome came to rule the Mediterranean world in barely fifty-three years, from the First Punic War to the fall of Carthage, with his famous analysis of the Roman constitution in Book VI.

works.title: The Histories, Books X–XL and fragments
works.author: Polybius
works.blurb: The surviving later books of Polybius's history of Rome's rise, from the recovery of Tarentum and Scipio in Spain through Cannae's aftermath, Zama, the wars with Philip, Antiochus and Perseus, to the destruction of Carthage and Corinth in 146 BC, with his reflections on historical method and his own conclusion.

works.title: Polyeucte
works.author: Pierre Corneille
works.blurb: Polyeucte, an Armenian nobleman newly converted to Christianity, is married to Pauline, who once loved the Roman knight Severus and obeyed her father in marrying another. When Severus returns in favour with the Emperor, Polyeucte's zeal leads him to smash the pagan idols and refuse to recant, even at the pleading of his wife and father-in-law. His martyrdom in turn converts Pauline and, finally, her father Felix. Corneille's tragedy of 1643 is written in rhymed couplets.

sections.title: Act IV: Polyeucte, Cleon, Three Other Guards

works.title: Garrick's Looking-Glass; or, the Art of Rising on the Stage
works.subtitle: A Poem in Three Cantos
works.author: Samuel Jackson Pratt
works.blurb: A satirical poem in three cantos on the theatrical world of David Garrick, published in 1776 (TCP K040357).

works.title: Humanity, or the Rights of Nature
works.subtitle: A Poem in Two Books
works.author: Samuel Jackson Pratt
works.blurb: Pratt’s verse attack on the slave trade and on cruelty to the weak, in heroic couplets, published in 1788 (TCP K038048).

works.title: Sympathy; or, a Sketch of the Social Passion
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Samuel Jackson Pratt
works.blurb: A two-book poem in praise of fellow-feeling as the bond of society, published in 1781 (TCP K094645).

works.title: Prince Arthur
works.subtitle: An Heroick Poem in Ten Books
works.author: Sir Richard Blackmore
works.blurb: Blackmore's first epic, in ten books of rhymed couplets, follows the British prince Arthur against the Saxons, with Lucifer and the powers of Hell working to thwart him.

works.title: Prince Hohenstiel-Schwangau, Saviour of Society
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A dramatic monologue in blank verse in which a disgraced ruler, a thinly veiled Napoleon III, defends his career to a woman in London.

works.title: The Prince's Quest
works.author: William Watson
works.blurb: A romance in ten parts of a prince who sets out in search of the meaning of life and love, written in rhymed couplets.

works.title: Prometheus Bound
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: For giving fire to mortals against the will of Zeus, the Titan Prometheus is nailed to a crag in the Scythian wastes by Strength and Force, while a reluctant Hephaestus does the work. Visited by the sea-nymphs, by Oceanus and by the wandering, cow-horned Io, he foretells the fall of Zeus, until Hermes comes to demand the secret and the rocks collapse upon him.

works.title: Prometheus Unbound
works.subtitle: A Lyrical Drama in Four Acts
works.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
works.blurb: Shelley's lyrical drama in four acts, in which the Titan chained to the Caucasus is freed when Jupiter is overthrown and love takes the place of tyranny.

works.title: Psalm of the West
works.author: Sidney Lanier
works.blurb: Lanier's long poem on the making of America, running from Columbus's night voyage and the Norse landing in Vinland through the Mayflower and Lexington.

works.title: Psyche
works.subtitle: or, The Legend of Love
works.author: Mary Tighe
works.blurb: Mary Tighe's retelling of the myth of Cupid and Psyche, from Apuleius, in six cantos of Spenserian stanzas.

sections.title: Dedicatory Sonnet, Addressed to My Mother

works.title: Punica
works.subtitle: The Second Punick War between Hannibal and the Romanes
works.author: Silius Italicus
works.blurb: Silius Italicus's Latin epic of the war between Rome and Hannibal, the longest surviving Latin epic, in seventeen books of heroic couplets by Thomas Ross.

works.title: The Purgatorio (Okey)
works.subtitle: Prose translation by Thomas Okey (Temple Classics)
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Dante's climb of the mountain of Purgatory in Thomas Okey's plain, literal prose for the Temple Classics, printed in 1901 as the facing English of the Italian text.

works.title: The Purple Island
works.subtitle: or, The Isle of Man
works.author: Phineas Fletcher
works.blurb: The body of man allegorised as an island, its anatomy described in Spenserian-derived stanzas, and the war of the virtues and vices for it in the last cantos.

works.title: Queen Hynde
works.author: James Hogg
works.blurb: Hogg's long romance in six parts, in tetrameter couplets, of a legendary Queen of Scotland in the age of St Columba, and the Norse suitors who beset her.

works.title: Queen Mary: A Drama
works.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
works.blurb: Tennyson's historical drama of the reign of Mary Tudor, from her triumphant entry into London and the Wyatt rebellion to her marriage to Philip of Spain, the burning of Cranmer, the loss of Calais and her death, with the throne passing to Elizabeth.

works.title: The Queen's Wake
works.subtitle: A Legendary Poem
works.author: James Hogg
works.blurb: Hogg's legendary poem of a minstrel contest at Holyrood, where the bards of Scotland sing before Mary, Queen of Scots, in the first weeks after her return from France. Twelve of the seventeen songs are given, among them Kilmeny and The Witch of Fife, together with the framing narrative divided into the Introduction, the three Nights, and the interludes between the songs.

sections.title: Interlude before The Witch of Fife
Interlude after The Witch of Fife
Interlude before The Fate of Macgregor

works.title: The Quest of the Sangraal
works.author: Robert Stephen Hawker
works.blurb: Hawker's blank-verse narrative of King Arthur's knights setting out from Tintagel on the quest for the Holy Grail (the Sangraal), with Merlin's prophecy and the lots cast for the four quarters of the world.

works.title: The Institutio Oratoria
works.subtitle: The Education of an Orator
works.author: Quintilian
works.blurb: Quintilian's twelve-book education of the orator, from the first lessons of childhood to the ideal orator's character and style, with a celebrated survey of Greek and Roman authors.

works.title: The Raghuvamsa (The Story of Raghu's Line)
works.subtitle: Raghuvamsa
works.author: Kalidasa
works.blurb: Kalidasa's epic of the solar dynasty of Raghu, from King Dilipa's vow at the hermitage of Vasishtha through Rama's life and banishment of Sita to the decline of the line under the last king, Agnivarna.

works.title: Ralph Roister Doister
works.author: Nicholas Udall
works.blurb: The vain braggart Ralph Roister Doister, egged on by the parasite Matthew Merygreeke, sets out to win the rich widow Christian Custance, who is already promised to the merchant Gawyn Goodlucke. His love letter is read aloud with the punctuation turned so that it insults her, his mock funeral and his gifts come to nothing, and in the end Custance and her maids beat off his assault on her house. Often called the first English comedy, the play follows Plautus and Terence but is set among English townsfolk, with songs and a closing prayer for the Queen.

works.title: The Ramayana
works.subtitle: The Epic of Rama, Prince of India, Condensed into English Verse
works.author: Valmiki
works.blurb: Romesh Chunder Dutt's condensed English rendering of the Sanskrit epic of Rama, in twelve books of rhymed couplets, from the bridal of Sita to the sacrifice of the horse and the recognition of Lava and Kusa. Published by J. M. Dent and Co., London, 1899.

works.title: The Rape of Helen
works.subtitle: Prose translation by A. W. Mair
works.author: Colluthus
works.blurb: A short epic retelling the judgement of Paris and the abduction of Helen from Sparta.

works.title: The Rape of Proserpine (Digges)
works.author: Claudian
works.blurb: The first English verse translation of Claudian's unfinished epic of Pluto's abduction of Proserpine, by Leonard Digges, the editor of Shakespeare's Poems (1640).

works.title: The Rape of the Bucket
works.subtitle: La Secchia Rapita, an heroi-comical poem in twelve cantos
works.author: Alessandro Tassoni
works.blurb: Tassoni's mock-heroic epic of the war between Modena and Bologna over a stolen wooden bucket, the first of its kind in Italian, in James Atkinson's English ottava rima.

works.title: The Rape of the Lock
works.subtitle: An Heroi-Comical Poem, in Five Cantos
works.author: Alexander Pope
works.blurb: A mock-epic on a society scandal — a lock of hair snipped in jest — blown up with the full machinery of Homeric epic, sylphs and all.

works.title: Red Cotton Night-Cap Country; or, Turf and Towers
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A narrative in four parts, in blank verse, of a rich young Parisian's religious mania and fatal leap, based on a recent Normandy law case.

works.title: The Regement of Princes
works.subtitle: De Regimine Principum
works.author: Thomas Hoccleve
works.blurb: Sleepless at Chester's Inn, the clerk Hoccleve meets an old beggar who talks him into writing a book of counsel for Prince Henry: a verse mirror for princes on justice, mercy, patience, prudence, largesse and peace, in rhyme royal.

works.title: Remorse
works.subtitle: A Tragedy in Five Acts
works.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
works.blurb: Coleridge's tragedy was first played at Drury Lane Theatre on 23 January 1813 and ran for twenty nights. Don Alvar, thought dead, returns in disguise to Granada, where his younger brother Ordonio, who had arranged his murder, is courting Alvar's betrothed Teresa. Alvar's attempt to rouse his brother's conscience, played out amid the persecution of the Moors, ends in violence and reckoning. It is a reworking of Coleridge's earlier play Osorio.

works.title: The Return of the Druses: A Tragedy
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A tragedy set on an islet of the Sporades in the fifteenth century. The Druses, exiles from Lebanon living under the Knights of Rhodes, believe their long-awaited prophet Hakeem is about to return and lead them home. Djabal, the man they hail as his incarnation, knows himself an impostor, and the play follows his unmasking amid a Venetian fleet, a Latin knight, and the woman who loves him.

works.title: The Return of Ulysses
works.subtitle: A Drama in Five Acts in a mixed manner
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's drama in five acts on the homecoming of Odysseus, first published in 1890. Athena brings Ulysses to Ithaca, where, in disguise, he meets Eumaeus and Telemachus and at last confronts the wooers of Penelope in his own hall; a chorus of the wooers sings between the speeches.

works.title: Rhesus
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: On the night after Hector's victory, the Trojan sentinels rouse their chief, a spy is sent into the Greek camp, and the Thracian king Rhesus arrives with his famous snow-white horses, only to be murdered in his sleep by Odysseus and Diomedes. Arthur Way renders the play, whose authorship has long been disputed, in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: The Tragedy of King Richard the Second
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Richard II banishes Bolingbroke and Mowbray, seizes the estate of the dying John of Gaunt, and sails for Ireland, only to find on his return that the exiled Bolingbroke has come home with an army. Deposed in Westminster Hall and imprisoned, Richard loses his crown to the man who becomes Henry IV. He is murdered at Pomfret Castle by Sir Pierce of Exton, and Henry is left to mourn the deed he wished for.

works.title: The Tragedy of King Richard the Third
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Richard, Duke of Gloucester, plots his way to the crown through the deaths of his brother Clarence, the wooing of Lady Anne, the murder of the princes in the Tower and the use and discarding of Buckingham. On the eve of Bosworth the ghosts of his victims curse him in his sleep and bless his rival, and Richmond's victory begins the Tudor line as Henry VII.

works.title: Roderick, the Last of the Goths
works.subtitle: A Tragic Poem
works.author: Robert Southey
works.blurb: A blank-verse epic in twenty-five sections on the last Visigothic king of Spain, who after his defeat by the Moors lives on as a penitent and fights again beside Pelayo.

sections.title: IV. The Monastery of St. Felix
XXI. The Fountain in the Forest

works.title: Rokeby
works.subtitle: A Poem in Six Cantos
works.author: Sir Walter Scott
works.blurb: A verse romance of the English Civil War, set around Barnard Castle and the River Greta just after Marston Moor, whose outlaw songs — 'Brignall Banks' and 'Allen-a-Dale' among them — became favourites.

works.title: The Romaunt of the Rose
works.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
works.type: Allegorical dream vision (translation from Guillaume de Lorris and Jean de Meun)
works.blurb: A dreamer enters the walled Garden of Love and sets his heart on a rosebud, helped and hindered by allegorical figures such as Fair Welcome, Danger and Reason, in the English version of the great French allegory.

works.title: The Tragedy of Romeo and Juliet
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: In Verona, the children of two feuding houses, Romeo Montague and Juliet Capulet, fall in love at a masked ball and marry in secret with the help of Friar Lawrence. When Tybalt kills Mercutio and Romeo kills Tybalt, Romeo is banished, and Juliet, pressed to marry Paris, takes a sleeping potion that makes her seem dead. The message to Romeo goes astray, and both lovers die in the tomb, ending their parents' quarrel too late.

works.title: Rose Mary
works.author: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
works.blurb: A ballad in three parts of the magic Beryl-stone, of the maiden Rose Mary who must read it, and of the spirits that dwell in it, with a Beryl-song between the parts.

works.title: The Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam
works.subtitle: Fifth Edition
works.author: Edward FitzGerald
works.translator: trans. Edward FitzGerald (1889), from Omar Khayyam
works.blurb: FitzGerald's free English version of the quatrains attributed to Omar Khayyam, the fifth edition of 1889.

works.title: The Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam
works.subtitle: First Edition
works.author: Edward FitzGerald
works.translator: trans. Edward FitzGerald (1859), from Omar Khayyam
works.blurb: FitzGerald's free English version of the quatrains attributed to Omar Khayyam, the first edition of 1859.

works.title: Rubáiyát of Doc Sifers
works.author: James Whitcomb Riley
works.blurb: A Hoosier country doctor, Doc Sifers, is sketched in numbered quatrain-stanzas in Indiana dialect, from his rounds on horseback and his fire-fighting to his plain-spoken kindness.

works.title: Salaman and Absal
works.subtitle: An Allegory
works.author: Jami
works.blurb: Jami's allegory of a king of Greece whose son Salaman, nursed and then seduced by the beautiful Absal, flees with her, is saved from a funeral pyre, and is finally freed from earthly love by the heavenly Venus, with the closing section explaining the story as the soul's journey.

works.title: The Conspiracy of Catiline
works.subtitle: De Coniuratione Catilinae, on the plot of 63 BC
works.author: Sallust
works.blurb: Sallust’s account of the conspiracy of Lucius Sergius Catiline, a ruined patrician who plotted to seize Rome in 63 BC, and of its exposure by the consul Cicero, with the speeches of Caesar and Cato on the fate of the conspirators and Catiline’s death in battle.

works.title: The Jugurthine War
works.subtitle: Bellum Iugurthinum, 112–105 BC
works.author: Sallust
works.blurb: Sallust’s history of the war Rome fought against Jugurtha, the Numidian prince who murdered his rivals, bribed Roman commanders and senators, and was finally betrayed by his father-in-law Bocchus, with the rise of Marius and Sulla, and Sallust’s reflections on the corruption of the Roman nobility.

works.title: Samson Agonistes
works.subtitle: A Dramatic Poem
works.author: John Milton
works.blurb: A tragedy on the Greek model — the blinded, captive Samson among the Philistines, moving toward his final act.

works.title: Sardanapalus
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: George Gordon, Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's tragedy in five acts, first published in 1821, on the last king of Assyria. Sardanapalus, a pleasure-loving monarch who prefers peace and his Ionian slave Myrrha to war and empire, is roused too late when the Mede Arbaces and the priest Beleses rebel; after fighting bravely he builds a funeral pyre in his palace and dies upon it with Myrrha.

works.title: Ane Pleasant Satyre of the Thrie Estaitis
works.subtitle: In Commendatioun of Vertew and Vituperatioun of Vyce
works.author: Sir David Lyndsay
works.blurb: A long Scots morality play in rhyme, first staged in 1552, in which the young King Humanitas, led astray by Wantonnes and Sensualitie, is brought to reform by Divyne Correctioun and Dame Veritie, while Johne the Common-weill and the poor man Pauper accuse the clergy, lords and merchants of the Thrie Estaitis.

works.title: The School of the Heart
works.author: Henry Alford
works.blurb: A long blank-verse poem in six lessons: a young man's meditation on love, nature, the Church and death, which the author later called a collection of detached passages of youthful feeling.

works.title: The Second Shepherds' Play
works.subtitle: Wakefield (Towneley) Cycle
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: Three Yorkshire shepherds, grumbling on a cold moor, are joined by the sheep-stealer Mak, who steals a lamb and hides it in a cradle at home, passing it off as his newborn son. When the shepherds find it, they toss Mak in a blanket; then an angel sings of Christ's birth, and they go to adore the true child in Bethlehem. The play is famous for its comic parody of the Nativity.

works.title: Apocolocyntosis
works.subtitle: The Pumpkinification of Claudius
works.author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
works.blurb: Seneca’s mock-deification of the dead emperor Claudius, a satire in prose and verse. Claudius labours to breathe his last, arrives at the gates of heaven stammering and lame, is argued over by the gods, and is at last condemned and sent below, to rattle dice for ever in a box with no bottom.

works.subtitle: Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium
works.author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
works.blurb: Letters 93 to 124 of the series Seneca wrote in his last years to his friend Lucilius: on the quality rather than the length of life, precepts and doctrines, grief for the dead, the soul’s immortality, the corporeality of virtue, the style that mirrors character, and the nature of the good.

works.title: The Seven Against Thebes
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: Oedipus's sons Eteocles and Polynices, doomed by their father's curse, face each other across the walls of Thebes. As a scout reports the seven champions of the Argive host, one to each gate, Eteocles assigns a defender to six of them, and then, learning that his own brother stands at the seventh, resolves to meet him in person. The brothers kill each other, and the play closes on the dirge for them and the defiance of Antigone.

works.title: The Shadowy Waters
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: Forgael, a sea-king, sails the waste seas in search of the immortal love promised him by the birds of the otherworld, while his crew grow mutinous. They capture a ship and its royal passenger, Dectora, whom Forgael enchants with the music of his harp, so that she is drawn to follow him beyond the world. In the end she cuts the rope that binds them to the world, and the two drift together into the shadowy waters. Yeats prefaces the play with a verse dedication to Lady Gregory, written among the seven woods of Coole.

works.title: The Shahnama of Firdausi
works.subtitle: Done into English by Arthur George Warner and Edmond Warner
works.author: Firdausi
works.translator: trans. Arthur George Warner and Edmond Warner (1905–1925)
works.blurb: The Warners' complete blank-verse English translation of Firdausi's Persian national epic; all nine volumes, from the creation of kingship under Gaiumart to the war with Mazandaran, Suhrab, Siyawush and the coming of Kai Khusrau, then Kai Khusrau's long wars with Turan (Piran, Kamus, the Khan of Chin, Bizhan and Manizha, the Twelve Rukhs, the fall of Afrasiyab) and the reign of Luhrasp, then the reign of Gushtasp (the coming of Zarduhsht, the wars with Arjasp, Asfandiyar's Seven Stages, the fight of Rustam and Asfandiyar, the death of Rustam), Bahman, Humai and Darab, and the last two reigns of the Kaianian line, Dara and Sikandar, the legend of Alexander; then the Sasanian dynasty, from the Ashkanians and the rise of Ardshir Papakan through the reigns of his successors, Bahram Gur's hunts and adventures, Nushirwan's justice with the tales of Buzurjmihr and Mahbud and the invention of chess, and Hurmuzd, to the long reign of Khusrau Parwiz (the revolt of Bahram Chubina, Khusrau's flight to Rum, Shirin, and his fall), then the brief reigns of his successors (the lament of Barbad, the death of Shirin, the women Shahs Purandukht and Azarmdukht), and last the reign of Yazdagird: the Arab conquest, the death of Rustam at Kadisiya, the flight to Khurasan and the murder of Yazdagird by the miller, ending with Firdausi's own closing words.

works.author: Firdausi
works.blurb: James Atkinson's abridged English version of Firdausi's Persian national epic, alternating verse with prose summary, from Kaiumers to Firdausi's satire on Mahmud.

works.title: Shakuntala
works.subtitle: Shakuntala and the Ring of Recognition
works.author: Kalidasa
works.blurb: King Dushyanta, hunting in the forest, comes to the hermitage of the sage Kanva and falls in love with his foster-daughter Shakuntala; they marry by mutual consent, and he leaves her a signet ring. Cursed by the irascible Durvasas, the king forgets her, and rejects her when she comes to court, until a fisherman finds the lost ring and his memory returns. Years later, in the heavenly hermitage of Kashyapa, he is reunited with Shakuntala and their son Bharata.

works.title: The Shepheard’s Calender
works.subtitle: Twelve Æglogues Proportionable to the Twelve Monethes
works.author: Edmund Spenser
works.blurb: Spenser’s first major work: twelve eclogues, one for each month, mixing pastoral love-complaint, satire of the clergy, and elegy in a deliberately archaic English.

works.title: The Shepherd of Hermas
works.subtitle: Visions, Mandates and Parables (Similitudes)
works.author: Hermas
works.blurb: An early Christian book of five visions, twelve mandates and ten parables, written at Rome in the second century and widely read in the early Church.

works.title: The Shepherd's Week
works.subtitle: In Six Pastorals
works.author: John Gay
works.blurb: Gay's six burlesque pastorals, one for each day of the week, in which English rustics quarrel, court, mourn and get drunk in mock-Spenserian dialect, a parody of Ambrose Philips's pastoral manner

works.title: The Shield of Hercules
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: Elton’s blank-verse version of the poem traditionally, though doubtfully, attributed to Hesiod, on Heracles’ duel with Cycnus and the description of his shield.

works.title: The Shield of Heracles
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: An epic fragment on Heracles’ duel with the brigand Cycnus, built around a long description of the hero’s richly decorated shield and traditionally, though doubtfully, attributed to Hesiod.

works.title: The Shield of Heracles
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: A prose version of the poem on Herakles’ combat with Kyknos, son of Ares, built around a long description of the hero’s decorated shield; ancient tradition ascribed it to Hesiod, though its authorship is doubtful.

works.title: The Shipwreck
works.subtitle: In Three Cantos
works.author: William Falconer
works.blurb: A narrative poem in heroic couplets of a merchant ship's voyage from Alexandria and its loss on the coast of Greece, drawn from the author's own experience at sea.

works.title: The Sibylline Oracles
works.subtitle: Translated from the Greek into English blank verse
works.author: The Sibylline Oracles
works.blurb: Twelve books of Greek hexameter prophecy put into the mouth of the pagan Sibyl by Jewish and Christian writers between the second century BC and the fifth century AD, from the creation and the flood to the fall of Rome and the last judgment.

works.title: The Psalms of David (Psalms 1–43)
works.subtitle: Metrical paraphrase from the Sidney Psalter, in the 1823 printed text
works.author: Sir Philip Sidney
works.blurb: Sir Philip Sidney's verse paraphrase of the first forty-three Psalms, each in a different metre and stanza form, begun in the early 1580s and completed by his sister Mary, Countess of Pembroke.

works.title: The Siege of Thebes
works.author: John Lydgate
works.blurb: Lydgate, as a Benedictine pilgrim newly arrived at Canterbury, is told by the Host to tell a tale on the road home, and he gives the story of Thebes: Oedipus, the Sphinx, the doomed rivalry of Eteocles and Polynices, and the Argive siege that ends in the brothers' death. A continuation of the Canterbury Tales in Chaucer's spirit, ending with a plea for peace.

works.title: The Siege of Valencia
works.subtitle: A Dramatic Poem
works.author: Felicia Hemans
works.blurb: Valencia, held by the Christian governor Alvar Gonzalez, a descendant of the Cid, lies under siege by the Moors. Abdullah, the Moorish chief, has taken two of Gonzalez’s sons prisoner and offers their lives in exchange for the city. Gonzalez refuses, and the play follows his wife Elmina, his daughter Ximena and the priest Hernandez through the city’s last days, to the deaths of the sons and of Gonzalez himself, as Castilian help arrives.

works.title: The Story of Sigurd the Volsung and the Fall of the Niblungs
works.subtitle: In four books: Sigmund, Regin, Brynhild, Gudrun
works.author: William Morris
works.blurb: Morris's epic retelling of the Volsunga Saga in long anapaestic lines: the Volsung kings, Sigurd's slaying of Fafnir, his waking of Brynhild, the Niblungs' treachery, and the vengeance of Gudrun, in four books.

works.title: Sir Amadace
works.subtitle: A verse rendering
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: Sir Amadace, ruined by his own open-handedness, sets out with what money is left and finds a dead man refused burial because of his debts. He spends everything to lay the corpse in the ground, and the favour is repaid when a mysterious White Knight helps him win a princess and a kingdom, on one terrible condition.

works.title: Sir Eglamour of Artois
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A tail-rhyme romance of Sir Eglamour, who wins the love of Christabel, daughter of the Earl of Artois, by slaying a giant and a monstrous boar, and by killing a dragon at Rome. After long separation, their child, carried off by a griffin, grows up to be a knight and, unknowing, is wed to his own mother, until a token reveals the truth and the family is reunited.

works.title: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
works.subtitle: A Middle-English Arthurian Romance
works.author: Gawain Poet
works.blurb: A green-skinned knight rides into Arthur's Christmas feast with an impossible challenge; Sir Gawain's answer sends him on a year-long quest that tests his courage, his courtesy, and his honesty alike.

works.title: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
works.subtitle: A verse rendering
works.author: Gawain Poet
works.blurb: A green-skinned knight rides into Arthur's Christmas feast with an impossible challenge; Sir Gawain's answer sends him on a year-long quest that tests his courage, his courtesy, and his honesty alike. Here the poem is rendered in rhymed, bobbed-and-wheeled stanzas.

works.title: Sir Gawayne and the Grene Knyȝt (Middle English text)
works.subtitle: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
works.author: Gawain Poet
works.blurb: The original alliterative Middle English of the great Arthurian romance: a green-skinned knight rides into Camelot at Christmas, and Gawain's answer to his beheading game leads him through a year of trial to the castle of Bertilak, the temptations of the lady, and the green girdle.

works.title: Sir Isumbras
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A tail-rhyme romance of a proud and prosperous knight who is warned by a bird to choose penance in this life. He loses wealth, wife and three sons, serves as a smith and a palmer, and at last regains all by God's mercy and wins a Christian kingdom from the Saracens.

works.title: Launfal
works.subtitle: Sir Launfal
works.author: Thomas Chestre
works.blurb: A tail-rhyme Breton lay of about 1,040 lines, adapted from Marie de France's Lanval and the anonymous Graelent: a knight of Arthur's court, impoverished and slighted by Guinevere, is loved by the fairy Tryamour.

works.title: Sir Orpheo
works.subtitle: Sir Orfeo
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A Middle English Breton lay of about 510 lines, the Orpheus story moved into fairyland: King Orpheo's queen Heurodis is carried off by the king of Faerie, and Orpheo gives up his crown to live as a harper in the wilderness, follows the fairy riders into their country, and wins her back with his playing.

works.title: Sir Perceval of Galles
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A tail-rhyme romance of the boy Perceval, reared in the wilds by his widowed mother, who rides to Arthur's court, avenges his father's death on the Red Knight and wins a lady's release from a Saracen sultan.

works.title: Sir Tristrem
works.subtitle: A verse rendering
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: Tristrem, son of Roland Riis and of Blancheflower, King Mark's sister, is brought up by the loyal Rohant and educated in the courtly arts before he comes to his uncle Mark in Cornwall. He kills the Irish champion Moraunt, is healed by Ysonde, wins her as Mark's bride, and shares with her a love that survives suspicion, banishment and exile.

works.title: Sister Songs
works.subtitle: An Offering to Two Sisters
works.author: Francis Thompson
works.blurb: Published in 1895, Sister Songs is Thompson’s offering to Monica and Madeline (Sylvia) Meynell, daughters of his patrons Wilfrid and Alice Meynell. It moves from a Proem addressed to Spring through two long parts to a closing Inscription.

works.title: Solomon and Saturn
works.subtitle: The poetic dialogues
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.translator: trans. J. M. Kemble, The Dialogue of Salomon and Saturnus (Ælfric Society, 1848)
works.blurb: Old English verse dialogues in which the wise King Solomon answers the riddling questions of the Chaldean prince Saturn.

works.title: Solomon and Saturn (Old English)
works.subtitle: The poetic dialogues: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: Old English verse dialogues in which the wise King Solomon answers the riddling questions of the Chaldean prince Saturn.

works.title: Solomon on the Vanity of the World
works.subtitle: A Poem in Three Books
works.author: Matthew Prior
works.blurb: Prior's longest poem: Solomon looks for happiness in knowledge, pleasure and power, and finds that all is vanity. Each book opens with the poet's prose argument.

works.title: The Song of Hiawatha
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A trochaic epic drawing on Ojibwe legend, following the life of the hero Hiawatha — his childhood, wooing, feats, and eventual departure — in a rhythm modeled on the Finnish Kalevala.

sections.title: The Son of the Evening Star

works.title: The Song of the Merchant Kalashnikov
works.subtitle: A Song of the Tzar Ivan Vasilyevich, of the Young Oprichnik and of the Bold Merchant Kalashnikov
works.author: Mikhail Lermontov
works.blurb: In the Moscow of Ivan the Terrible, the merchant Kalashnikov fights and kills the Tsar's favourite oprichnik to avenge the insult to his wife, and pays for it on the block.

works.title: The Song of Los
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Los sings the long history of the laws and religions that bound Africa and Asia, until Orc's fires break out in Europe and America.

works.title: The Song of Roland
works.subtitle: La Chanson de Roland
works.author: Anonymous (Old French)
works.blurb: Betrayed by his stepfather Ganelon, Charlemagne's nephew Roland holds the pass at Roncevaux against the Saracens, refuses to sound his horn until too late, and dies a martyr; the Emperor then avenges him.

works.title: The Song of Roland
works.subtitle: La Chanson de Roland
works.author: Anonymous (Old French)
works.blurb: John O'Hagan's version renders the epic of Roland's last stand at Roncevaux in rhymed octosyllabic couplets, divided into three Parts and numbered laisses, with scene headings of his own.

sections.title: Part I: The Treason of Ganelon
Part II: The Prelude of the Great Battle (Laisses LXXXIII–CXLVII)
Part II: The Great Battle Continued (Laisses CXLVIII–CXCVII)

works.title: The Song of Songs
works.subtitle: Authorized Version of the Song of Solomon.
works.author: The Bible (Authorized King James Version)
works.blurb: An anthology of Hebrew love lyrics, traditionally ascribed to Solomon.

works.title: Sordello
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: Browning's long narrative poem in six books follows the thirteenth-century Mantuan troubadour Sordello through the Guelf and Ghibelline wars of northern Italy, and is chiefly a study of the growth and failure of a poet's soul.

works.title: A Soul's Tragedy
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A two-part drama set in the Italian town of Faenza. In the verse first act, "the poetry of Chiappino's life", the blustering republican Chiappino quarrels with his friend Luitolfo and strikes down the tyrannical Provost. In the prose second act the people make him Provost in turn, and the Pope's Legate Ogniben quietly takes his measure.

works.title: The Romaunce of the Sowdone of Babylone and of Ferumbras His Sone Who Conquerede Rome
works.subtitle: The Sowdone of Babylone
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A Middle English romance in rhymed quatrains. The Saracen Soudan Laban of Babylon sacks Rome; his son Ferumbras is defeated and converted, and his daughter Floripas helps the imprisoned peers of Charlemagne win their freedom before Charles himself defeats Laban in Spain. Preserved in a single manuscript.

works.title: The Spanish Gypsy
works.author: George Eliot
works.blurb: A dramatic poem of fifteenth-century Spain, in five books. Fedalma, a Gypsy foundling brought up in the household of the Duke Silva, is about to marry him when her father Zarca, chief of the Zincali, claims her for the cause of his people. She renounces her love, and after her father's death sails with the exiled Gypsies for Africa. It mixes narrative blank verse, dramatic dialogue with named speakers, and songs.

works.title: The Spanish Student
works.subtitle: A Play in Three Acts
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A verse play set in Spain. The student Victorian loves Preciosa, a gypsy dancer of Madrid, whom the profligate Count of Lara also pursues. Her gypsy guardian, jealousies and a slandering plot divide the lovers, and the story passes from Madrid to the Guadarrama mountains, with serenades and gypsy songs set within the dialogue, before her true parentage is revealed.

works.title: The Spanish Tragedy
works.subtitle: Containing the lamentable end of Don Horatio and Bel-imperia, with the pitiful death of old Hieronimo
works.author: Thomas Kyd
works.blurb: The ghost of the Spanish courtier Don Andrea, slain in battle, is led back from the underworld by Revenge to watch his killer Balthazar punished. Instead he sees Andrea's friend Horatio murdered in his father's arbour and Hieronimo, the Knight-Marshall of Spain, driven half mad by grief as he seeks justice from a corrupt court. Hieronimo at last stages a play before the court in which the real deaths are carried out.

works.title: The Spirit of Discovery by Sea
works.subtitle: A Descriptive and Historical Poem
works.author: William Lisle Bowles
works.blurb: A blank-verse poem in five books on the history of maritime discovery, from the Ark to the voyages of the eighteenth century.

works.title: The Historie of Squyer Meldrum
works.author: Sir David Lyndsay
works.blurb: Lyndsay's verse romance of William Meldrum of Cleish and Binns, a Fife laird: a gallant, fighting, loving squire who defends a lady from robbers, wins a tournament in Ireland and a wife at home, and dies in his bed, leaving a Testament that is part mock-heroic, part valediction.

sections.title: The Historie of Squyer William Meldrum, of Cleische and Bynnis
The Testament of the Nobill and Vailyeand Squyer William Meldrum of the Bynnis

works.title: The Squyr of Lowe Degre
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A romance of about 1,130 lines in rhymed couplets: a squire of low degree loves the king of Hungary's daughter. She bids him win fame in arms abroad, the king's steward betrays him, and after seven years of mourning over a body she wrongly takes to be his, the princess finds him alive and they are married.

works.title: Le Morte Arthur
works.subtitle: The stanzaic Morte Arthur
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: An English verse romance of about 1400 in eight-line stanzas, telling the last days of King Arthur: the love of Lancelot and Guinevere, the Maid of Ascolot, the war between Arthur and Lancelot, Mordred's treason, the passing of Arthur and the deaths of Lancelot and Guinevere. It was a main source of Malory's last books.

works.title: The Story of Rimini
works.author: Leigh Hunt
works.blurb: Hunt's retelling of the story of Paolo and Francesca, from Dante's Inferno, in four cantos of heroic couplets: the bride fetched to Rimini, her journey, the fatal passion and its end.

works.title: Strafford: A Tragedy
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: Browning's first play, written for the actor Macready. Thomas Wentworth, Earl of Strafford, King Charles I's chief minister, returns from Ireland to face the Parliamentary party led by his old friend John Pym. Betrayed by the weak King he serves, Strafford is impeached and condemned, and the play ends with their last meeting before his execution.

works.title: Such Stuff as Dreams Are Made Of
works.subtitle: A drama taken from Calderón's La Vida es Sueño
works.author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
works.blurb: Basilio, King of Poland, confines his son Segismund from birth because of a prophecy, then drugs him and lets him wake in the palace for a day to test it. FitzGerald's free version of La vida es sueño, whose title he turns into a joke on the stolen phrase.

works.title: The Lives of the Twelve Caesars
works.subtitle: With the Lives of the Grammarians, Rhetoricians and Poets
works.author: Suetonius
works.translator: trans. Alexander Thomson, revised by T. Forester (1855)
works.blurb: Suetonius's lives of the Caesars from Julius to Domitian, with his surviving short Lives of grammarians, rhetoricians and poets, in Alexander Thomson's translation (1796) as revised by T. Forester for Bohn's Classical Library (1855). Thomson's own essays on the history and literature of each period are omitted.

works.title: The Suppliant Maidens
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: The fifty daughters of Danaus flee Egypt to escape forced marriage to their cousins, the sons of Aegyptus, and beg sanctuary at Argos. King Pelasgus must choose between sheltering them and war; the Argive assembly votes to protect them, and the Egyptian herald's threats are turned back as the maidens give thanks.

works.title: The Suppliants
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: After the failed assault of the Seven against Thebes, the mothers of the fallen Argive chiefs come to Eleusis and beg Theseus to win back the unburied bodies of their sons. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Sylvia; or, The May Queen
works.subtitle: A Lyrical Drama
works.author: George Darley
works.blurb: A lyrical drama set in the Apennines. The traveller Romanzo falls in love with Sylvia, May Queen of a glen shared between the fairy queen Morgana and Ararach, king of the fiends. The fiends plot to seize Sylvia and to torment Romanzo with a phantom show, while the comic servant Andrea, transformed by the fiends, blunders between the two parties, until the fairy host drives off the fiends and the lovers are reunited. Blank verse, songs and comic prose.

works.title: Syphilis
works.subtitle: A Poetical History of the French Disease
works.author: Girolamo Fracastoro
works.blurb: Fracastoro's Latin didactic poem on the origin, nature and cure of the new disease that gave syphilis its name, in Nahum Tate's English couplets.

works.title: The Life and Death of Julius Agricola
works.subtitle: Church and Brodribb translation, 1876
works.author: Tacitus
works.translator: trans. Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb (1876)
works.blurb: Tacitus's memoir of his father-in-law Gnaeus Julius Agricola, governor of Britain, from his boyhood in Gaul through the campaigns against the Caledonians to his death under Domitian, in Church and Brodribb's English prose of 1876.

sections.title: The Life and Death of Julius Agricola

works.title: The Annals
works.subtitle: Church and Brodribb translation, 1876
works.author: Tacitus
works.translator: trans. Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb (1876)
works.blurb: Tacitus's annals of the Roman Empire from the death of Augustus through the reigns of Tiberius, Claudius and Nero, in the surviving books (I–VI and XI–XVI), in Church and Brodribb's English prose of 1876.

works.title: Germania
works.subtitle: The Origin and Situation of the Germans
works.author: Tacitus
works.translator: trans. Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb (1876)
works.blurb: Tacitus's short ethnography of the Germanic peoples beyond the Rhine and Danube, their land, customs, government, war and religion, and the tribe-by-tribe survey that follows, in Church and Brodribb's English prose of 1876.

works.title: The Histories
works.subtitle: Fyfe translation, 1912
works.author: Tacitus
works.blurb: Tacitus's account of the civil wars of AD 69 and the Flavian accession: Galba, Otho and Vitellius, the rise of Vespasian, the revolt of Civilis on the Rhine and the siege of Jerusalem, in W. Hamilton Fyfe's English prose of 1912. The surviving books end mid-narrative.

works.title: The Táin
works.subtitle: Táin Bó Cúailnge, the Cattle-Raid of Cooley, in English verse
works.author: Anonymous (Old Irish)
works.blurb: The central epic of the Ulster cycle in Mary Hutton's English blank verse: Queen Maev of Connaught and King Ailill gather the Four Fifths of Ireland to seize the Brown Bull of Cooley, and the boy-hero Cúchulainn (her Cucullin) holds the Ulster border alone until Ulster rises. It opens with the tale of how the poets recovered the lost Táin from the ghost of Fergus.

works.title: The Taking of Ilios
works.subtitle: Prose translation by A. W. Mair
works.author: Tryphiodorus
works.blurb: A short late-antique epic on the last night of the Trojan War, from the building of the wooden horse to the sacrifice of Polyxena.

works.title: A Tale of Eternity
works.subtitle: The Haunted Hurst
works.author: Gerald Massey
works.blurb: Gerald Massey's long narrative poem of haunting and the afterlife, in seven parts, first published in 1870.

works.title: The Tale of Gamelyn
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A younger son, Gamelyn, is cheated of his inheritance and kept in servitude by his elder brother. He wrestles his way to fame, escapes his bonds, and becomes king of the outlaws in the greenwood. When his brother has him arraigned, Gamelyn returns, takes the judge's seat and hangs the corrupt justice, the sheriff and the jury. The story is the source of Shakespeare's As You Like It.

works.title: A Tale of Paraguay
works.subtitle: Dedication, Proem and four cantos (1825)
works.author: Robert Southey
works.blurb: Southey's Spenserian tale of the Guarani Indian pair Quiara and Monnema, left alone by a plague of smallpox, and of their son Yeruti and daughter Mooma, whom the Jesuit missionary Dobrizhoffer receives into the mission of St Joachin; written in 1824-25 and dedicated to his daughter Edith May.

works.title: Tamburlaine the Great: Part 1
works.author: Christopher Marlowe
works.blurb: Marlowe's first great play, in blank verse, follows the Scythian shepherd Tamburlaine from his seizure of the Persian crown to his triumph over Bajazeth, the Soldan of Egypt and the city of Damascus.

works.title: Tamburlaine the Great: Part 2
works.author: Christopher Marlowe
works.blurb: The sequel in blank verse follows Tamburlaine through the death of Zenocrate, the killing of his faint-hearted son Calyphas and the burning of Babylon, to his own death.

works.title: The Taming of the Shrew
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: A tinker, Christopher Sly, is tricked by a Lord into believing he is a nobleman, and a company of players performs the play-within-a-play for him. In Padua, Baptista will not let his gentle younger daughter Bianca marry until his sharp-tongued elder daughter Katherina has a husband, so the fortune-hunting Petruchio woos Katherina and sets about taming her by contradiction and deprivation. While Bianca's suitors scheme and exchange disguises, Petruchio wins a wager at the final feast when Katherina alone obeys her husband's summons.

works.title: Tartuffe; or, The Hypocrite
works.author: Molière
works.blurb: Orgon, a prosperous Parisian householder, has taken the pious Tartuffe into his home and fallen wholly under his spell, promising him his daughter's hand and his fortune. Orgon's family, led by the sharp-tongued maid Dorine and his wife Elmire, try to open his eyes to the impostor, who is in fact scheming to seize the house and seduce Elmire. Molière's comedy of religious hypocrisy was banned for five years after its first performance in 1664.

works.title: Temora: An Ancient Epic Poem
works.subtitle: In Eight Books
works.author: James Macpherson
works.blurb: Ossian's epic of Cairbar's murder of King Cormac and Fingal's expedition to Ireland to restore the throne, ending in the battle with Cathmor, in measured prose.

works.title: The Tempest
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Prospero, the usurped Duke of Milan, has lived twelve years on an enchanted island with his daughter Miranda, served by the spirit Ariel and the savage Caliban. When his enemies sail past, he raises a storm and wrecks their ship, and through illusion, music and a courtship between Miranda and Ferdinand he brings them to repentance. In the end he forgives his brother, frees Ariel, and abjures his magic.

works.title: The Temple of Nature
works.subtitle: or, The Origin of Society
works.author: Erasmus Darwin
works.blurb: Darwin's last poem, published after his death, traces in four cantos the progress of life from its first stirrings in the ocean to the rise of mind, society and morality. Written in heroic couplets, it versifies his evolutionary speculations in the mysteries of an ancient temple.

sections.title: Canto III. Progress of the Mind
Canto IV. Of Good and Evil

works.title: Adelphi
works.subtitle: The Brothers
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's last comedy: two brothers, one strict and one indulgent, raise two sons between them, and a scandal, a stolen music-girl and a clever slave test both methods of upbringing, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: Andria
works.subtitle: The Fair Andrian
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's first comedy: a young Athenian's secret love for a girl from Andros, a father's pretended wedding plans, and a clever slave, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: Eunuchus
works.subtitle: The Eunuch
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's most popular comedy: a courtesan, a boastful captain, a disguised young man and a parasite, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: Heautontimorumenos
works.subtitle: The Self-Tormentor
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's play of two fathers and their sons: a harsh old man punishes himself with farm labour for driving his son abroad, while his neighbour's son and a scheming slave run up a courtesan's bills, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: Hecyra
works.subtitle: The Mother-in-Law
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's most reversed play, twice driven from the stage: a young husband's secret guilt, a wife in hiding and a wrongly blamed mother-in-law, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: Phormio
works.subtitle: The Scheming Parasite
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's most celebrated comedy of intrigue: a parasite weds a penniless girl to a young Athenian by a trick at law, and two old brothers are caught out by a secret that Phormio holds, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: The Testament of Beauty
works.subtitle: A Poem in Four Books
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Published on Bridges's eighty-fifth birthday, in his last year as Poet Laureate, this long meditative poem in loose Alexandrines sets out his philosophy of beauty as the meeting-point of instinct and spirit in the mind of man. It is in four books: Introduction, Selfhood, Breed and Ethick.

works.title: Thalaba the Destroyer
works.author: Robert Southey
works.blurb: An Arabian romance in twelve books, in irregular unrhymed verse: the orphan Thalaba is chosen to destroy the sorcerers of the Domdaniel caverns that murdered his family.

works.title: The Apostle
works.subtitle: Az apostol
works.author: Sándor Petőfi
works.blurb: Petőfi's long poem of democratic faith: the foundling Szilveszter, raised in cruelty, grows up to become a wandering preacher of liberty and brotherhood, here in twenty parts in English verse by William N. Loew.

works.title: The Bride's Prelude
works.author: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
works.blurb: An unfinished narrative poem begun in 1848: on the morning of Aloyse's wedding she tells her sister Amelotte the story of her lost love.

works.title: The Bridge
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Hart Crane
works.blurb: Hart Crane’s long poem of America, taking the Brooklyn Bridge as its emblem: from Columbus’s landfall in Ave Maria through the Pocahontas section, Cutty Sark, the Whitmanic Cape Hatteras, the Three Songs, Quaker Hill and The Tunnel, to the closing hymn of Atlantis.

sections.title: II. Powhatan’s Daughter: 1. The Harbor Dawn
V. Three Songs: 2. National Winter Garden

works.title: The Cenci
works.subtitle: A Tragedy in Five Acts
works.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
works.blurb: Shelley's blank-verse tragedy of the Roman nobleman Francesco Cenci, whose cruelty to his family drives his daughter Beatrice to plot his murder; she is tried and executed for the deed. Based on a sixteenth-century Roman crime, it was written in 1819.

works.title: The Doctor
works.subtitle: Fo'c's'le Yarns, Second Series: 1
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: The longest of the Fo'c's'le Yarns: a seaman's tale in rhymed Manx dialect of the Doctor and the people around him, told to a forecastle audience that suspects him of spinning stories.

works.title: The Excursion
works.author: William Wordsworth
works.blurb: Wordsworth's nine-book blank-verse poem follows the poet, the Wanderer, the Solitary and the Pastor through a Lake District excursion in which grief and despondency are met with reflections on nature, faith, human suffering and the moral life.

sections.title: Book Sixth: The Church-yard among the Mountains
Book Seventh: The Church-yard among the Mountains (continued)
Book Ninth: Discourse of the Wanderer, and an Evening Visit to the Lake

works.title: The Golden Violet
works.author: Letitia Elizabeth Landon (L.E.L.)
works.blurb: A frame poem of a two-day minstrel contest in Provence for the prize of the Golden Violet, in which each minstrel sings his or her own tale.

sections.title: The Broken Spell: The First Provençal Minstrel's Lay
The Falcon: The Lay of the Norman Knight
The Dream: The Lay of the Scottish Minstrel
